docs.title: INDEX — docs/ (Layer 2: documentation index)
docs.text:
Source of truth for the framework. Each line below is the canonical doc for its topic — read it instead of re-deriving from source. Folder map: CONTEXT.md (sibling) · repo entry: ../AGENTS.md.

The tree is organised by reader: guide/ (app developers), reference/ (lookup), concepts/ (explanation), decisions/ (binding ADRs), contributing/ (framework contributors), project/ (maintainers: plan, state, records).

docs.title: guide/ — building an app with Capsule
docs.text:

  • guide/quickstart.md — first app in minutes.
  • guide/hello-world.md — the annotated hello-world.

docs.title: decisions/ — binding (never decided twice)
docs.text:
• decisions/index.md — the ADR list with status; 000N = the adr-00N cited across the docs.
  • decisions/0001-embedded-runtime.md — embedded HTTP server + QuickJS on-device runtime (accepted; server library now CivetWeb per 0004).
  • decisions/0002-capsule-ui.md — native-look component layer, Tailwind + iOS/Material preset (proposed).
  • decisions/0003-ai-and-agents.md — on-device AI + agent tools, OTA-updatable agent logic (proposed; Tier-1 spike built).
  • decisions/0004-web-serving-transport.md — loopback HTTP server on both platforms (rejects WKURLSchemeHandler/https); tiered HTTP fidelity, WS/SSE deferred-by-design; 2026-10-24 amendment: CivetWeb on both platforms.
  • decisions/log.md — consolidated API/implementation decisions (SDK SLA, monolithic core).

docs.title: CONTEXT — Capsule Framework (Layer 1: the map)
docs.text:
Canonical, version-controlled copy — lives in this repo (capsule/ is the public monorepo and owns the documentation). Paths below are relative to docs/; ../ = repo root.

Capsule is an open-core mobile framework: ship any web bundle inside a generated native shell, with an on-device runtime (CivetWeb + QuickJS) and OTA code push (CodeSync).

Layer model (ICM). Read top-down, stop when you have enough: Layer 0 ../AGENTS.md (entry + rules) → Layer 1 this file (folder+package map) → Layer 2 index.md (every doc) → Layer 3 individual docs → Layer 4 source (../packages/*/). References only ever point down.

docs.title: CONVENTIONS — ICM no-drift rules
docs.text: How the AI-navigability layer is kept correct over time. These are the Interpreted Context Methodology (ICM) principles adapted to this repo. When the layers and the code disagree, the code wins — fix the layer.

docs.title: Principles
docs.text:
1. One stage, one job. Each CONTEXT.md / workflow folder covers a single concern. Don't grow a god-doc.
  2. Plain text as interface. Markdown only. No tooling required to read a layer.
  3. Layered context, read top-down. ../../AGENTS.md + the folder's own AGENTS.md (L0) → ../CONTEXT.md (L1) → ../index.md + per-area CONTEXT.md (L2) → individual doc (L3) → source (L4). An agent stops reading as soon as it has enough. AGENTS.md is the only agent entry point. Tool-specific files (CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, .github/copilot-instructions.md) are one- or two-line pointers to it with no content of their own, so there is nothing to drift. Every package (packages/*), examples/ and scripts/ has a nested AGENTS.md — what it is, entry files, the exact test command, local rules, which docs describe it — and points to its README.md for the file map instead of repeating it.
  4. Configure the factory, not the product. Workflows describe how to do a recurring task; they don't hold the task's one-off output.
  5. Automate the repetitive. Any command run repeatedly — especially multi-step or multi-directory (e.g. "for every example…") — becomes a Node script in the repo's scripts/ exposed as a root pnpm script (pnpm dev:*, pnpm update:*), never a manual loop pasted into prose. Docs point to the script; the script is the single source of the shortcut. Scripts are OS-agnostic (Node built-ins only, scripts/lib/env.mjs for per-OS executables) and read machine paths from the git-ignored .env.local — never hard-coded.

docs.title: Reference rules
docs.text:
• One canonical source per fact. Each topic is owned by exactly one doc (see ../index.md). Everywhere else points to it — never restates it.
  • References point downward only. L0→L1→L2→L3→L4. The single allowed upward pointer is a child CONTEXT.md naming its parent map. No cycles.
  • No duplication. If you're tempted to copy a paragraph, link instead. A fact in two places will drift; a link can't.
  • Specs are contracts. Spec docs (ADRs, core-api.md, lockfile.md) define constraints, not implementation. Implementation lives in source.

docs.title: Layer budgets (soft targets)
docs.text: Layer File Target 0 ../../AGENTS.md ≤ ~1,500 tokens — map, read order, definition of done, hard rules 0 nested AGENTS.md 20–60 lines — local rules + test command; file maps stay in the README 1 ../CONTEXT.md ~300 tokens — the map, nothing more 2 ../index.md, per-area CONTEXT.md, ../contributing/workflows/*/CONTEXT.md one-liners + contract

docs.title: Workflow stage contracts
docs.text:
Each contributing/workflows/<name>/CONTEXT.md is a contract with three sections:

  • Inputs — table of which files/layers to load (point to exact docs).
  • Process — ordered steps; mark human checkpoints and quality audits.
  • Outputs — what is produced and where (usually edits to source + docs, not a new artifact folder — this is a product repo, not a content pipeline).

output/ folders, when a workflow needs one, carry a .gitkeep and are git-ignored — structure is versioned, generated artifacts are not.

docs.title: Doc metadata
docs.text:
Docs and code point at each other, and pnpm docs:check keeps both directions true. The map of every page and the folders it covers is generated: docs-map (pnpm gen).

Front matter. Every page under docs/ except reference/generated/ starts with:

---
title: "Database (SQLite)"      # quoted; used for the browser tab and search
audience: app-developer         # app-developer | contributor | maintainer | everyone
status: current                 # current | planned | draft | record
code:                           # optional: repo-relative globs of the source this page documents
  - packages/core/src/db.ts
  - packages/capsule-android/capsule/src/main/kotlin/dev/capsule/db/**
tests:                          # optional: the tests that pin that behaviour
  - packages/core/src/__tests__/db.test.ts
---
  • status: current describes what is built; planned is a design not built yet; draft is unsettled or exploratory; record is history kept as written (ADRs, the decision log, history, research, incidents). The site marks planned, draft and record pages in the navigation.
  • Globs are repo-relative with forward slashes and start with a path segment. ** matches any number of folders, * stays within one, ? is one character. List the files a reader would open, not the whole package. Keep the page's # heading; title doesn't replace it.

Code header. A source file names the doc that explains it in a comment within its first 15 lines, in its language's comment style:

// Docs: docs/guide/database.md

The value is one or more comma-separated repo-relative doc paths, each optionally with an #anchor. Headers are read in packages/, scripts/ and examples/*/src/, never in the vendored sources under packages/native/civetweb and packages/native/quickjs.

Checks (scripts/docs-check.mjs; the parser and glob matcher are in scripts/docs-lint/lib/meta.mjs):

Rule Checks Level R1 every page has front matter with a valid title, audience and status, and no unknown keys error R2 every code: / tests: glob matches at least one file, so a page can't keep pointing at deleted code error R3 every code header points at an existing doc, and at an existing heading when it has an #anchor error R4 a file matched by a page's code: globs that has a header which doesn't list that page warning

When you move or delete code, update the globs that pointed at it (R2 tells you which). When a file gets a header, list every page whose code: covers it (R4).

docs.title: When you change the code
docs.text:
• New doc → put it in the folder for its reader (guide/ app developers · reference/ lookup · concepts/ explanation · decisions/ ADRs · contributing/ framework contributors · project/ maintainers), name it in descriptive kebab-case (numbers only for ADRs and dated records), give it front matter, add its one-line entry to ../index.md and its mkdocs.yml nav line.
  • New top-level area or hard rule → update ../CONTEXT.md / ../../AGENTS.md (its repo map too).
  • Changed a package's commands, entry files or local rules → update that package's AGENTS.md in the same change. A new package gets its own AGENTS.md and a row in the root repo map.
  • New recurring multi-step procedure → add ../contributing/workflows/<name>/CONTEXT.md.
  • New reusable script/tool → drop it in ../../scripts/ (Node, header comment with usage), add a root pnpm script, and list it in contributing/commands.md; any new machine path goes in .env.example.
  • Phase or next-action changed → update ../project/state.md (the pointer only; status detail stays in project/roadmap.md).
  • End of a work session → append an entry to ../project/history.md; never rewrite past entries.
  • Moved/renamed/deleted a doc → fix every pointer to it (grep the slug first).

docs.title: Phase 1 — Foundation ✅ Done
docs.text:
Goal: A working capsule dev + capsule build android + hot reload loop. Status: ✅ Complete — all Phase 1 deliverables done, 36 TS tests + 24 Kotlin tests passing, app installed on real Samsung device.

By the end of Phase 1, a developer can scaffold a React/Vue/Svelte/Vanilla app, run it on an Android emulator with <50ms hot reload, and build a signed APK.

docs.title: Phase 1 Deliverables
docs.text:
1. Monorepo scaffold — pnpm workspace + Turbo pipeline
  2. @capsule/cli — init, add android, sync, dev, build android, run android
  3. @capsule/core — JS bridge runtime + geolocation API (proof of concept)
  4. capsule-android — Kotlin AAR (Activity + WebView + JS bridge)
  5. Project templates — react-ts, vue-ts, svelte-ts, vanilla-ts

Docker images + GitHub CI/CD are deferred to Phase 8 — Ecosystem. Phase 1 is fully local: real device (Samsung M62) + emulator.

docs.title: 1.5 Changesets (version management)
docs.text:
Capsule is a multi-package monorepo publishing to npm. Changesets coordinates version bumps across packages — when @capsule/core releases a new version, @capsule/cli (which depends on it) gets bumped correctly.

pnpm add -D -w @changesets/cli
pnpm changeset init

This creates .changeset/config.json. Commit the .changeset/ directory. Usage:

# When you make a change that should ship:
pnpm changeset          # prompts: which packages? what bump? write a summary
# Commit the generated .changeset/*.md file with your code change

# To release:
pnpm changeset version  # bumps package.json versions + updates CHANGELOG.md
pnpm changeset publish  # publishes all bumped packages to npm

Phase 1: Run pnpm changeset init during monorepo setup. No need to publish to npm yet — Phase 2 handles the first release. But record changes with pnpm changeset from day one so the CHANGELOG is accurate at first publish.

docs.title: 2.2 Bridge protocol (src/bridge.ts)
docs.text:
Implements the JSON-RPC 2.0 bridge from ../project/known-issues.md Issue 2.

// packages/core/src/bridge.ts

type JsonRpcRequest = {
  jsonrpc: '2.0'
  id: string
  method: string
  params?: unknown
}

type JsonRpcSuccess = {
  jsonrpc: '2.0'
  id: string
  result: unknown
}

type JsonRpcError = {
  jsonrpc: '2.0'
  id: string
  error: { code: number; message: string; data?: unknown }
}

type JsonRpcNotification = {
  jsonrpc: '2.0'
  method: string
  params?: unknown
  // no id field — distinguishes notifications from responses
}

declare const __capsule_host: {
  postMessage: (json: string) => void
}

type ResponseHandler = (response: JsonRpcSuccess | JsonRpcError) => void
type NotificationHandler = (params: unknown) => void

class CapsuleBridge {
  private pendingRequests = new Map<string, ResponseHandler>()
  private notificationHandlers = new Map<string, Set<NotificationHandler>>()
  private requestCounter = 0
  private isNative = typeof __capsule_host !== 'undefined'

  constructor() {
    // Native layer calls this for all inbound messages (responses + notifications)
    ;(window as any).__capsuleReceive = (json: string) => {
      this.handleMessage(json)
    }
  }

  call<T = unknown>(method: string, params?: unknown): Promise<T> {
    if (!this.isNative) {
      return Promise.reject(new CapsuleError(1001, 'BRIDGE_UNAVAILABLE',
        'Not running in a Capsule native shell'))
    }

    return new Promise<T>((resolve, reject) => {
      const id = `capsule-${++this.requestCounter}-${Date.now()}`
      const request: JsonRpcRequest = { jsonrpc: '2.0', id, method, params }

      this.pendingRequests.set(id, (response) => {
        if ('error' in response) {
          reject(new CapsuleError(response.error.code, response.error.message, response.error.data))
        } else {
          resolve(response.result as T)
        }
      })

      __capsule_host.postMessage(JSON.stringify(request))
    })
  }

  on(method: string, handler: NotificationHandler): () => void {
    if (!this.notificationHandlers.has(method)) {
      this.notificationHandlers.set(method, new Set())
    }
    this.notificationHandlers.get(method)!.add(handler)

    // Return unsubscribe function
    return () => {
      this.notificationHandlers.get(method)?.delete(handler)
    }
  }

  private handleMessage(json: string) {
    let msg: JsonRpcSuccess | JsonRpcError | JsonRpcNotification

    try {
      msg = JSON.parse(json)
    } catch {
      console.error('[Capsule] Failed to parse bridge message:', json)
      return
    }

    if (!('id' in msg)) {
      // Notification — no id field
      const notification = msg as JsonRpcNotification
      this.notificationHandlers.get(notification.method)?.forEach(h => h(notification.params))
      return
    }

    const handler = this.pendingRequests.get(msg.id)
    if (handler) {
      this.pendingRequests.delete(msg.id)
      handler(msg as JsonRpcSuccess | JsonRpcError)
    }
  }
}

export class CapsuleError extends Error {
  constructor(
    public readonly code: number,
    message: string,
    public readonly data?: unknown
  ) {
    super(message)
    this.name = 'CapsuleError'
  }
}

// Singleton bridge — instantiated once per page
export const bridge = new CapsuleBridge()

docs.text:
First real capability — proves the bridge works end-to-end.

// packages/core/src/geolocation.ts
import { bridge } from './bridge.js'

export interface GeolocationPosition {
  coords: {
    latitude: number
    longitude: number
    accuracy: number
    altitude: number | null
    altitudeAccuracy: number | null
    heading: number | null
    speed: number | null
  }
  timestamp: number
}

export interface GeolocationOptions {
  enableHighAccuracy?: boolean
  timeout?: number
  maximumAge?: number
}

export const geolocation = {
  async getCurrentPosition(options?: GeolocationOptions): Promise<GeolocationPosition> {
    return bridge.call<GeolocationPosition>('geolocation.getCurrentPosition', options ?? {})
  },

  watchPosition(
    callback: (position: GeolocationPosition) => void,
    options?: GeolocationOptions
  ): () => void {
    // Returns unsubscribe function
    const unsub = bridge.on('geolocation.positionUpdate', (params) => {
      callback(params as GeolocationPosition)
    })

    bridge.call('geolocation.watchPosition', options ?? {}).catch(() => unsub())

    return () => {
      unsub()
      bridge.call('geolocation.clearWatch', {}).catch(() => {})
    }
  }
}

// packages/cli/src/config.ts
import { createJiti } from 'jiti'
import { join } from 'node:path'
import { existsSync } from 'node:fs'

export interface CapsuleConfig {
  appId:   string
  appName: string
  version: {
    name:        string
    buildNumber: number
  }
  android?: {
    minSdk:     number
    targetSdk:  number
    compileSdk: number
    permissions?: string[]
    signing?: {
      storeFile?:     string
      storePassword?: string
      keyAlias?:      string
      keyPassword?:   string
    }
    gradleOverrides?: Record<string, unknown>
  }
  ios?: {
    deployment?: string
    bundleId?:   string
  }
  plugins?: Array<string | { path: string; trust?: string; overrides?: string }>
  codeSync?: {
    enabled:          boolean
    url?:             string
    apiKey?:          string
    channel?:         string
    strategy?:        'background' | 'immediate' | 'on-next-launch'
    checkOnForeground?: boolean
    mandatory?:       boolean
  }
  web?: {
    mobileReset?: boolean
  }
}

export function defineConfig(config: CapsuleConfig): CapsuleConfig {
  return config
}

export async function loadConfig(projectRoot: string): Promise<CapsuleConfig> {
  const configPath = join(projectRoot, 'capsule.config.ts')

  if (!existsSync(configPath)) {
    throw new Error(`capsule.config.ts not found in ${projectRoot}`)
  }

  const jiti = createJiti(projectRoot, { interopDefault: true })
  const mod = await jiti.import(configPath) as { default: CapsuleConfig }

  return mod.default
}

docs.title: 3.4 capsule init command
docs.text:
// packages/cli/src/commands/init.ts
import { Command } from 'commander'
import prompts from 'prompts'
import chalk from 'chalk'
import ora from 'ora'
import { copySync, writeFileSync, ensureDirSync } from 'fs-extra'
import { join } from 'node:path'
import { execaSync } from 'execa'

const command = new Command('init')
  .argument('[name]', 'project directory name')
  .option('--template <template>', 'react-ts | vue-ts | svelte-ts | vanilla-ts', 'react-ts')
  .option('--app-id <appId>', 'reverse-domain app ID (e.g. com.yourcompany.app)')
  .description('Scaffold a new Capsule project')
  .action(async (name: string | undefined, opts) => {
    // Interactive prompts if args not provided
    const answers = await prompts([
      {
        type: name ? null : 'text',
        name: 'name',
        message: 'Project name',
        initial: 'my-app'
      },
      {
        type: opts.appId ? null : 'text',
        name: 'appId',
        message: 'App ID (reverse-domain)',
        initial: 'com.example.myapp'
      },
      {
        type: opts.template ? null : 'select',
        name: 'template',
        message: 'Template',
        choices: [
          { title: 'React + TypeScript', value: 'react-ts' },
          { title: 'Vue + TypeScript',   value: 'vue-ts' },
          { title: 'Svelte + TypeScript', value: 'svelte-ts' },
          { title: 'Vanilla TypeScript', value: 'vanilla-ts' },
        ]
      }
    ])

    const projectName = name ?? answers.name
    const appId = opts.appId ?? answers.appId
    const template = opts.template ?? answers.template

    const spinner = ora(`Creating ${projectName}...`).start()

    // Copy template files
    const templateDir = join(__dirname, '../../templates', template)
    const projectDir = join(process.cwd(), projectName)

    ensureDirSync(projectDir)
    copySync(templateDir, projectDir)

    // Write capsule.config.ts
    writeFileSync(join(projectDir, 'capsule.config.ts'), generateConfig(appId, projectName))

    // Write capsule.lock (empty — will be populated by capsule sync)
    writeFileSync(join(projectDir, 'capsule.lock'), generateInitialLock())

    // Write .gitignore
    writeFileSync(join(projectDir, '.gitignore'), GITIGNORE)

    spinner.text = 'Installing dependencies...'
    execaSync('pnpm', ['install'], { cwd: projectDir })

    spinner.succeed(chalk.green(`Created ${projectName}`))

    console.log(`
  ${chalk.bold('Next steps:')}
    ${chalk.cyan(`cd ${projectName}`)}
    ${chalk.cyan('capsule add android')}
    ${chalk.cyan('capsule dev')}
`)
  })

function generateConfig(appId: string, appName: string): string {
  return `import { defineConfig } from '@capsule/cli'

export default defineConfig({
  appId:   '${appId}',
  appName: '${appName}',

  version: {
    name:        '1.0.0',
    buildNumber: 1
  },

  android: {
    minSdk:     26,
    targetSdk:  35,
    compileSdk: 35,
  }
})
`
}

function generateInitialLock(): string {
  return `# capsule.lock
# Generated by @capsule/cli. Do not edit manually.
# Regenerate with: capsule sync
lockfileVersion: 1
# Run 'capsule add android' then 'capsule sync' to populate this file.
`
}

const GITIGNORE = `# Dependencies
node_modules/

# Generated by capsule — do not commit
.capsule/

# Build output
dist/

# Environment variables
.env
.env.local
*.env

# Logs
*.log
`

export default command

docs.title: 3.5 capsule sync — the core generator
docs.text:
This command reads capsule.config.ts + capsule.lock and generates .capsule/android/ (a thin Gradle project wrapper).

Key files generated inside .capsule/android/: - settings.gradle.kts — includes the AAR dependency - build.gradle.kts — app module config derived from capsule.config.ts - AndroidManifest.xml — generated from appId + permissions - app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml — appName

This is the core of Capsule's promise — developers never edit these files.

See cli.md § capsule sync for what capsule sync generates; the generator itself is packages/cli/src/sync/sync.ts.

docs.title: 3.6 capsule dev — dev server
docs.text:
1. Load capsule.config.ts
2. Detect connected devices/emulators (adb devices)
3. Spawn Vite dev server (port 5173 by default)
4. Run: adb reverse tcp:5173 tcp:5173
5. Print: "Ready — app loading on emulator"
6. Watch for Ctrl+C → cleanup

If --tunnel: use cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:5173 and print the HTTPS URL + QR code.

docs.title: 3.7 capsule build android
docs.text:
1. Load capsule.config.ts + capsule.lock
2. Run capsule sync (ensure .capsule/ is up to date)
3. Run: vite build → dist/
4. Copy dist/ → .capsule/android/app/src/main/assets/www/
5. Run: ./gradlew assembleDebug   (or bundleRelease / assembleRelease with --release)
6. Output: .capsule/android/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk

docs.title: 4.3 CapsuleActivity.kt — single entry point
docs.text:
// packages/capsule-android/capsule/src/main/kotlin/dev/capsule/CapsuleActivity.kt
package dev.capsule

import android.annotation.SuppressLint
import android.os.Bundle
import android.view.View
import android.webkit.*
import androidx.appcompat.app.AppCompatActivity
import kotlinx.coroutines.CoroutineScope
import kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers
import kotlinx.coroutines.SupervisorJob

open class CapsuleActivity : AppCompatActivity() {

    protected lateinit var webView: WebView
    private val scope = CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main + SupervisorJob())

    // Override in generated .capsule/android/ wrapper to configure the shell
    open val capsuleConfig: CapsuleShellConfig
        get() = CapsuleShellConfig()

    @SuppressLint("SetJavaScriptEnabled")
    override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
        super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)

        webView = WebView(this).also { wv ->
            wv.settings.apply {
                javaScriptEnabled        = true
                domStorageEnabled        = true
                allowFileAccess          = true
                allowContentAccess       = true
                mediaPlaybackRequiresUserGesture = false
                mixedContentMode         = WebSettings.MIXED_CONTENT_ALWAYS_ALLOW
            }

            // Register the JS bridge
            wv.addJavascriptInterface(
                CapsuleBridge(this, scope, capsuleConfig),
                "__capsule_host"
            )

            wv.webViewClient = CapsuleWebViewClient()
            wv.webChromeClient = CapsuleWebChromeClient()

            setContentView(wv)
        }

        loadApp()

        // OnBackPressedDispatcher — replaces deprecated onBackPressed() (API 33+)
        onBackPressedDispatcher.addCallback(this) {
            if (webView.canGoBack()) webView.goBack()
            else isEnabled = false  // let system handle (closes activity)
        }
    }

    private fun loadApp() {
        val url = if (BuildConfig.DEBUG && capsuleConfig.devServerUrl != null) {
            capsuleConfig.devServerUrl!!    // e.g. http://10.0.2.2:5173
        } else {
            // Phase 2: CapsuleRuntime delegates here after the embedded server is bound:
            // "http://127.0.0.1:${capsuleConfig.port}/"
            // Phase 1 fallback: serve from bundled assets (file:// semantics; adequate for Phase 1)
            "file:///android_asset/www/index.html"
        }
        webView.loadUrl(url)
    }

    // Phase 2: CapsuleActivity becomes a thin shell that delegates to CapsuleRuntime:
    //
    //   override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
    //       super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)
    //       runtime = CapsuleRuntime(bridge, server, jsRuntime, splash, codeSync)
    //       runtime.start(webView)
    //   }
    //
    // CapsuleRuntime owns the startup sequence: splash → embedded-server bind → QuickJS evaluate
    // → WebView navigate to http://127.0.0.1:{port}/. See 0001-embedded-runtime.md.

}

docs.title: 4.4 CapsuleBridge.kt — JSON-RPC 2.0 dispatcher
docs.text:
// packages/capsule-android/capsule/src/main/kotlin/dev/capsule/CapsuleBridge.kt
package dev.capsule

import android.content.Context
import android.webkit.JavascriptInterface
import android.webkit.WebView
import kotlinx.coroutines.CoroutineScope
import kotlinx.coroutines.launch
import kotlinx.serialization.json.*

class CapsuleBridge(
    private val context: Context,
    private val scope: CoroutineScope,
    private val config: CapsuleShellConfig
) {
    // Registry-based dispatch — enables capsule override command
    // Built-in handlers are registered first; overrides register on top
    internal val handlers = mutableMapOf<String, BridgeHandler>()
    private lateinit var webView: WebView

    init {
        registerBuiltIns()
    }

    fun attachWebView(wv: WebView) { webView = wv }

    @JavascriptInterface
    fun postMessage(json: String) {
        scope.launch {
            try {
                val request = Json.parseToJsonElement(json).jsonObject

                val id     = request["id"]?.jsonPrimitive?.content
                val method = request["method"]?.jsonPrimitive?.content
                    ?: return@launch sendError(null, 1001, "METHOD_MISSING")
                val params = request["params"] ?: JsonObject(emptyMap())

                val handler = handlers[method]
                    ?: return@launch sendError(id, 1002, "METHOD_NOT_FOUND",
                        "Unknown method: $method")

                try {
                    val result = handler.handle(params)
                    if (id != null) sendResult(id, result)
                } catch (e: CapsuleException) {
                    sendError(id, e.code, e.bridgeMessage, e.data)
                } catch (e: Exception) {
                    sendError(id, 1000, "INTERNAL_ERROR", e.message)
                }

            } catch (e: Exception) {
                sendError(null, 1000, "PARSE_ERROR", "Failed to parse message")
            }
        }
    }

    private fun registerBuiltIns() {
        // Phase 1: 6 built-in handlers (geolocation, camera, haptics, push, biometrics, alerts)
        GeolocationHandler(context).register(handlers)
        // Phase 4: NFC, Bluetooth, filesystem, SQLite db, background jobs
        // Phase 2: QuickJSBridge — server-side @capsule/core calls inside QuickJS
    }

    private fun sendResult(id: String, result: JsonElement) {
        val response = buildJsonObject {
            put("jsonrpc", "2.0")
            put("id", id)
            put("result", result)
        }.toString()
        dispatchToWebView(response)
    }

    private fun sendError(id: String?, code: Int, message: String, data: Any? = null) {
        val response = buildJsonObject {
            put("jsonrpc", "2.0")
            if (id != null) put("id", id) else put("id", JsonNull)
            putJsonObject("error") {
                put("code", code)
                put("message", message)
                if (data != null) put("data", data.toString())
            }
        }.toString()
        dispatchToWebView(response)
    }

    // Send a notification (event) to the web layer — no id field
    fun sendNotification(method: String, params: JsonElement) {
        val notification = buildJsonObject {
            put("jsonrpc", "2.0")
            put("method", method)
            put("params", params)
        }.toString()
        dispatchToWebView(notification)
    }

    private fun dispatchToWebView(json: String) {
        webView.post {
            // Use JSON.parse to avoid string injection — pass as a data URI argument
            webView.evaluateJavascript(
                "window.__capsuleReceive(${Json.encodeToString(json)})",
                null
            )
        }
    }
}

interface BridgeHandler {
    val method: String
    suspend fun handle(params: JsonElement): JsonElement
    fun register(registry: MutableMap<String, BridgeHandler>) {
        registry[method] = this
    }
}

class CapsuleException(
    val code: Int,
    val bridgeMessage: String,
    val data: Any? = null
) : Exception(bridgeMessage)

docs.title: 4.5 GeolocationHandler.kt
docs.text:
Requires com.google.android.gms:play-services-location in the shell's libs.versions.toml. Add implementation(libs.play.services.location) to build.gradle.kts — already included in Step 4.2 above.

// packages/capsule-android/capsule/src/main/kotlin/dev/capsule/handlers/GeolocationHandler.kt
package dev.capsule.handlers

import android.Manifest
import android.content.Context
import android.content.pm.PackageManager
import android.location.Location
import androidx.core.content.ContextCompat
import com.google.android.gms.location.LocationServices
import dev.capsule.BridgeHandler
import dev.capsule.CapsuleException
import kotlinx.coroutines.suspendCancellableCoroutine
import kotlinx.serialization.json.*
import kotlin.coroutines.resume
import kotlin.coroutines.resumeWithException

class GeolocationHandler(private val context: Context) : BridgeHandler {
    override val method = "geolocation.getCurrentPosition"

    override suspend fun handle(params: JsonElement): JsonElement {
        if (ContextCompat.checkSelfPermission(context, Manifest.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION)
            != PackageManager.PERMISSION_GRANTED) {
            throw CapsuleException(2001, "PERMISSION_DENIED",
                mapOf("permission" to "ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION"))
        }

        val location = getLastLocation()
            ?: throw CapsuleException(3001, "LOCATION_UNAVAILABLE")

        return buildJsonObject {
            putJsonObject("coords") {
                put("latitude",         location.latitude)
                put("longitude",        location.longitude)
                put("accuracy",         location.accuracy.toDouble())
                put("altitude",         if (location.hasAltitude()) location.altitude else JsonNull)
                put("altitudeAccuracy", JsonNull)
                put("heading",          if (location.hasBearing()) location.bearing.toDouble() else JsonNull)
                put("speed",            if (location.hasSpeed()) location.speed.toDouble() else JsonNull)
            }
            put("timestamp", location.time)
        }
    }

    private suspend fun getLastLocation(): Location? = suspendCancellableCoroutine { cont ->
        LocationServices.getFusedLocationProviderClient(context)
            .lastLocation
            .addOnSuccessListener { location -> cont.resume(location) }
            .addOnFailureListener { e -> cont.resumeWithException(e) }
    }
}

import { useState, useEffect } from 'react'
import { geolocation } from '@capsule/core'

export default function App() {
  const [position, setPosition] = useState<{ lat: number; lng: number } | null>(null)

  useEffect(() => {
    geolocation.getCurrentPosition()
      .then(p => setPosition({ lat: p.coords.latitude, lng: p.coords.longitude }))
      .catch(console.error)
  }, [])

  return (
    <div style={{ padding: 24 }}>
      <h1>Capsule App</h1>
      {position
        ? <p>📍 {position.lat.toFixed(4)}, {position.lng.toFixed(4)}</p>
        : <p>Getting location...</p>
      }
    </div>
  )
}

docs.title: Step 8 — Local Development Shell Override
docs.text:
Before publishing a real release, you need to test the Kotlin AAR you're building locally. Add this to the CLI:

// packages/cli/src/sync/resolve-shell.ts

// If CAPSULE_SHELL_OVERRIDE_PATH is set, use that AAR directly
// instead of resolving from GitHub Releases.
// For use during Capsule framework development only.
const override = process.env.CAPSULE_SHELL_OVERRIDE_PATH
if (override) {
  console.warn('[capsule] Using local shell override:', override)
  return { aarPath: override, version: 'local', sha256: 'override' }
}

// Normal path: resolve from GitHub Releases

Usage during development:

# Build the AAR locally
cd packages/capsule-android
./gradlew assembleDebug

# Point the CLI at it
export CAPSULE_SHELL_OVERRIDE_PATH=/path/to/capsule-android/capsule/build/outputs/aar/capsule-debug.aar

# Test
cd examples/react-ts
capsule sync && capsule dev

docs.title: MurmurHash3 cross-platform note (record here for Phase 4)

Before Phase 4, create a reference test vector file (test/hash-vectors.json) with ≥20 {deviceId, seed, expected} tuples and run it against both implementations in CI. Pin exact library versions. Mismatches silently bucket users into the wrong cohort.

docs.title: Next Phase
docs.text:
Phase 1 is complete. Next up:

→ See roadmap.md for Phase 2 (Embedded Runtime — embedded HTTP server + QuickJS + CapsuleRuntime).

Phase 2 entry point: CapsuleRuntime coordinator + interfaces + fakes (Step 1 in the roadmap). See 0001-embedded-runtime.md for full Phase 2 architecture and the 7-step implementation plan.

docs.title: Capsule vs Ionic/Capacitor — Architectural Comparison
docs.text: Capacitor (Ionic's native runtime) is the right benchmark — it's the architectural equivalent of Capsule.

docs.title: 1. Generated native project — no committed android/ or ios/
docs.text:
Capacitor requires you to commit the full android/ and ios/ directories (thousands of files). Capsule generates .capsule/android/ from capsule.config.ts via capsule sync. You .gitignore it entirely.

This is the same philosophy as Nuxt's .nuxt/ — your project repo is clean. No Android Studio merge conflicts. No accidental Gradle version drift.

docs.title: 2. capsule.lock — native dependency versioning
docs.text:
Capacitor has no lock file concept for the native shell. You don't know which version of the native runtime your project was built against unless you check Gradle files manually.

Capsule tracks aarHash (content hash of the native shell) and configHash in capsule.lock. You commit this file. --frozen-lockfile fails fast in CI if someone changed the config without syncing.

docs.title: 3. Bundler-agnostic by design
docs.text:
Capacitor is heavily Vite-oriented. Their official docs and tooling assume Vite.

Capsule has web.buildCommand / web.devCommand as first-class config. Angular with ng build, Rspack, Rollup, Webpack — they all just work by setting two strings. The examples directory proves this: rollup-solid, rspack-lit, webpack-preact all coexist.

docs.title: 4. OTA updates and background jobs designed in from day 1
docs.text:
Capacitor's OTA update story is Appflow — a paid external service. It's not in the framework.

Capsule has codeSync and jobs[] as first-class schema fields (Phase 2, but the architecture is designed for them). Background jobs with constraints (network: 'unmetered', battery: 'charging'), sync strategies (merge vs replace), scheduled notifications — all part of the config schema. No third-party service required.

docs.title: 5. No Ionic vs. Capacitor split
docs.text:
Ionic is a UI component library. Capacitor is the native runtime. They're separate products that happen to be made by the same company. You can use Capacitor without Ionic, but the docs and mental model constantly blur the line.

Capsule is one thing: a framework. One CLI, one core package, one config file.

docs.title: 6. Testable native layer by design
docs.text: Capacitor plugins are notoriously hard to unit test — they depend on Android/iOS context. Capsule's provider pattern (AlertsProvider, StorageProvider, etc.) decouples the API definition from the Android implementation. Every handler has a fake provider, every handler has isolated unit tests in pure Kotlin/JUnit. No emulator needed for the tests.

docs.title: 7. Template system with real framework support
docs.text:
Capacitor's ionic start heavily pushes Ionic UI components. For vanilla React, Vue, Svelte, or Angular without Ionic components, you're essentially on your own.

Capsule has 7 framework-native templates (vanilla-js, vanilla-ts, react-ts, vue-ts, svelte-ts, angular-ts, jquery-bootstrap) via giget — designed to become separate repos, independently maintained, zero lock-in to Capsule's UI opinions.

docs.title: Where Capsule is not yet superior (honest)
docs.text:
Area Capacitor Capsule iOS Mature Not implemented (Phase 4) Plugin ecosystem 200+ plugins (camera, biometrics, push, etc.) 6 built-in APIs Production-tested Thousands of apps 0 production apps Community Large None yet

(The old "web serving scheme" weakness is closed: Capsule replaced file:///android_asset/www/ with an embedded loopback HTTP server in Phase 2 — see below.)

docs.title: Web serving architecture decision
docs.text:
Decided — embedded loopback HTTP server on both platforms. See adr-004 for the full rationale, and ../contributing/platform-parity.md for the parity map. WKURLSchemeHandler and https://localhost were considered and rejected (no WebSocket support / cross-platform asymmetry / cert-trust burden respectively).

Mode Android iOS Dev Vite dev server at http://192.168.x.x:PORT via adb reverse Same Production CivetWeb → http://127.0.0.1:{port}/ CivetWeb (the same C server) → http://127.0.0.1:{port}/

This gives both platforms full http:// semantics: localStorage, IndexedDB, service workers, and CORS all behave correctly — and keeps /api route behaviour identical across platforms. Unlike Capacitor (custom capacitor:// scheme on iOS), Capsule runs a real server on both sides, so on-device /api routes get full HTTP fidelity (streaming now; WebSockets/SSE on the roadmap).

docs.title: Extensibility & Positioning — Exploration (pre-ADR)
docs.text:
Status: exploring · decision pending. Captures the "batteries-included vs thin-core" positioning debate and the plugin-architecture thinking from the 2026-06-24 brainstorm, plus the supporting competitive research, so we can resume without re-deriving it. Do not build a plugin/extension system off this yet — it's premature until there's real long-tail/ecosystem demand. When we commit, this graduates to adr-004-extensibility-model.md.

Related: 0003-ai-and-agents.md (agent tools = native bridge surface), 2026-06-24-planning-brainstorm.md (sequencing), the capability seam in protocol/CapabilityRegistry, and the upkeep lockstep discipline (upkeep.md).

docs.title: The question
docs.text:
Two identities for a cross-platform mobile framework:

  • Batteries-included & opinionated (Expo managed-workflow style): ship one complete, tested native shell; the developer writes JS. "It just works." Caps the niche long tail.
  • Thin core & open ecosystem (Capacitor style): tiny core, everything else is third-party native plugins. Max flexibility — and max "plugin hell."

Owner's current lean (2026-06-24): "I tend to be in both… I don't know," while agreeing that Capsule's OTA + capability architecture makes the opinionated path genuinely better, not just safer.

docs.title: The synthesis that resolves "both"
docs.text:
It's not an either/or once you pick the right axis. The dividing line isn't open vs closed — it's native vs JS:

  • Be opinionated where mistakes are expensive and un-hot-fixable → native. Native code can't be OTA'd (store policy + security), breaks builds, and carries the version-matrix risk. So keep native curated, tested, and shipped as one coherent shell. This is the Expo-like "it just works."
  • Be thin-core/open where it's cheap and safe → JS / OTA. Anything implementable in JS (higher-level APIs, agent tools, business logic, even some "native-sounding" features — see classification below) ships as a normal npm package or an OTA bundle. No native build, no autolink, no version hell.

So Capsule is both, by layer: opinionated batteries-included shell + open thin-core JS/OTA surface. The owner's instinct is correct and reconcilable — the question was just mis-framed as one axis.

docs.title: Why Capacitor became "plugin hell" (root causes)
docs.text:
1. Native code distributed as third-party npm packages → version drift ("plugin v5 needs Capacitor v6"), opaque native build breakage, dependence on abandoned packages.
  2. Autolinking magic that fails cryptically.
  3. No runtime capability negotiation → a JS update can call a plugin API the installed binary lacks → crash.

docs.title: Capsule's architectural antidotes (already present)
docs.text:
• (3) → solved by CapabilityRegistry + OTA gating. The shell advertises {capability: version}; a JS bundle declares what it needs; OTA refuses an update the installed shell can't satisfy. Capacitor has no equivalent. (Built into every Phase-3 API as the CAPABILITY/CAPABILITY_VERSION constants.)
  • (1) → solved by CLI-enforced lockstep. Versions are reconciled by tooling, not the user (the library-catalog ↔ sync.ts linked-pair discipline from the upkeep doc, generalized).
  • The structural move: the unit of native extension is the shell, not the plugin. Capsule already treats the shell as a first-class swappable artifact (CAPSULE_SHELL_OVERRIDE_PATH; the planned "shell registry"). There is always one coherent, tested native binary per app — assembled/selected with the capabilities it needs, version-pinned — instead of a pile of independently-versioned native packages autolinked together. No version matrix = no hell.
  • The bias: push everything that can be JS into the OTA layer, keep the native primitive set small and general. Fewer native surfaces = less to break. (Also makes the agent-tool surface in adr-003 clean.)

docs.title: Proposed tiered model (the likely ADR shape)
docs.text:
1. First-party curated shell — the table-stakes APIs ship in the tested shell. "Batteries-included" is a feature vs Capacitor's assembly-required hell.
  2. JS / OTA capabilities (the big one) — anything not needing platform code ships as npm or OTA bundles. Frictionless; where most "plugins" should live; where Capsule has far more room than Capacitor because of QuickJS + OTA.
  3. Governed native extension (later, long tail) — not free npm-native plugins, but a vetted registry of shell modules, each pinned to the shell version it's built against, assembled into a custom shell by the CLI with lockstep enforced and capability-gated.
  4. Build-your-own-shell — power-user escape hatch for anything off-registry.

Rule: most extension is JS/OTA (frictionless); native extension is whole-shell-level and CLI-governed (no version matrix); free-for-all npm-native is never allowed.

docs.title: Does every native-sounding API actually need native code?
docs.text:
No — useful when deciding "core vs JS/OTA" for each future capability:

Capability Truly needs native? Note Camera, NFC, Bluetooth, Biometrics, Push, Secure Storage, Local Notifications, Status bar, Background jobs, App Badge, App Launcher, Browser (Custom Tabs), Share, Splash, Screen Orientation, Telecom/SMS Yes Platform APIs / hardware — must be in the shell. SQLite No wa-sqlite/sql.js (WASM) runs in the WebView with OPFS persistence — pure JS, OTA-updatable. Toast / Action Sheet Optional Can be web UI in the WebView; native is polish, not necessity. Higher-level APIs, agent tools, orchestration No JS composing native primitives → OTA layer.

docs.title: Positioning / marketing angle
docs.text: "Opinionated, batteries-included, no plugin hell, JS/OTA for the long tail" is a differentiator, not just a safety choice — and a concrete contrast to Capacitor's assemble-and-pray native-plugin model. The OTA + capability architecture is what makes the opinionated path better, not merely safer.

docs.title: Open questions to resolve before this becomes adr-004
docs.text:
• Where exactly is the first-party shell line? (Which capabilities are "always in the shell" vs "registry shell-module" vs "JS-only"?)
  • What governs the vetted registry (review bar, who can publish, signing)?
  • Does the shell-module mechanism assemble at sync/build time, or are there prebuilt shell variants in the registry? (Build-time assembly vs binary selection.)
  • How does capability gating interact with registry modules at OTA time (advertise per-module versions)?
  • Pro-tier hook: private shell registry as a monetization surface (ties to biz model).

docs.title: When to revisit
docs.text: Not now. Keep shipping first-party into the curated shell and writing JS for everything else. Revisit when (a) real long-tail/niche native demand appears, (b) third parties want to contribute capabilities, or (c) the Pro-tier private-shell-registry becomes a monetization priority (Phase 6+). The CapabilityRegistry is the seam a future system gates on, and "shell, not plugin" is the principle to hold until then.

docs.title: Appendix — competitive research (2026-06-24 scan, condensed)
docs.text:
• Capacitor 7 GA (2025-01-20), Capacitor 8 (2025-12-08): SPM default on iOS, Android edge-to-edge / SystemBars, ~6-month release cadence tracking annual OS releases.
  • Official plugin set expanding: Capacitor absorbed Barcode Scanner and added Privacy Screen, Http, Cookies, File Transfer/Viewer, Background Runner, and split Browser → @capacitor/browser + @capacitor/inappbrowser. (Signal: even Capacitor is curating more into "official.")
  • Appflow winding down (sales stopped 2025-02-11, EOL 2027-12-31; Live Updates → paid OutSystems cloud). Independent OTA (Capawesome Cloud, Capgo) is filling the vacuum — validates Capsule's OTA bet.
  • On-device LLM is now first-party: Ionic shipped capacitor-local-llm v1.0.0 (2026-05-11) — unified TS API over Apple Foundation Models + Gemini Nano (text + image gen + sessions). Plus Capacitor Skills (2026-06-03) = reusable AI-agent primitives — the same thesis as adr-003. So Tier-1 ai is now parity; the moat is OTA-updatable agents.
  • Framework7 v9 (2025-11, latest v9.0.5 2026-05-27): iOS-26 visual redesign, React 19 / Svelte 5 adapters. Pure UI/router layer — defers all native to Capacitor/Cordova; no native or AI moves. (Relevant only to Phase-6 migration UX, not native-capability competition.)
  • Community native-plugin concentration (the "hell" surface): clusters around @capacitor-community, Capawesome (Robin Genz), Capgo (Martin Donadieu), Aparajita. High-value categories Capacitor users reach for: secure storage, ML-Kit barcode, file picker, app badge, social/OAuth login, in-app review/update, background geolocation, TTS/STT.

docs.title: Migrating Ionic & Framework7 Apps into Capsule
docs.text: Companion to chatgpt-plugin-compatibility.md. That doc covers the plugin importer (Capacitor/Cordova native → Capsule ABI). This doc answers the higher-level question: can an existing Ionic or Framework7 app run inside Capsule, and is it worth building a migration on-ramp?

docs.title: The core reframe: UI is free, native is the work
docs.text:
Ionic and Framework7 are web UI libraries, not runtimes.

  • Ionic = web components (@ionic/react, @ionic/vue, @ionic/angular, or raw ionic-core custom elements). The native runtime underneath is Capacitor (or legacy Cordova).
  • Framework7 = a web UI + in-app router (vanilla / React / Vue). Native access is via Cordova/Capacitor plugins the app added.

Capsule's entire architecture is "serve any web bundle in a WebView." Therefore:

Layer Migration cost Why UI components / router ~Free They're web code. They render in Capsule's WebView exactly as in Capacitor's. Point web.buildCommand at the existing ionic build / framework7 build. Capsule's bundler-agnostic design (rollup-solid, rspack-lit, webpack-preact examples) already proves arbitrary bundlers work. Native plugin calls (@capacitor/camera, Preferences, Keyboard, StatusBar, App…) The real work These hit the native bridge. Handled by the plugin importer + a Capacitor-compat shim (below).

Do not try to host Capacitor's Bridge/lifecycle internals. That recreates the Capsule → Capacitor → Cordova stack the plugin-compatibility doc explicitly rejects. The goal is make migration cheap, not execution universal.

docs.title: The highest-leverage piece: @capsule/compat-capacitor
docs.text:
A JS shim package that re-implements @capacitor/core's registerPlugin() and the Level-1 plugin facades (Camera, Preferences, Device, Share, Haptics, Clipboard) as thin wrappers over Capsule's existing JSON-RPC bridge.

With it, migrating a well-behaved Ionic app is:

# 1. Alias @capacitor/* → @capsule/compat-capacitor in package.json
# 2. Point web.buildCommand at the existing build
# 3. capsule sync && capsule build android

For Level-1 plugins this is zero application-code change. That is the single best acquisition funnel: a capsule migrate ionic command that demos in ~5 minutes.

docs.title: Table-stakes native equivalents (must exist or migrated apps feel broken)
docs.text:
Ionic apps lean on a few Capacitor plugins for basic chrome/behavior. These need first-class Capsule bridge equivalents before "it just works" is true:

  • App — hardware back button + deep links (Ionic relies on this heavily on Android).
  • Keyboard — show/hide events, resize behavior.
  • StatusBar — color/style.

These are cheap to build but non-optional for a credible migration story.

docs.title: Framework7 specifics
docs.text:
F7 is generally easier than Ionic to bring over:

  • Its UI + router are pure web — no native assumptions in the router itself.
  • Its native touchpoints are whatever Cordova/Capacitor plugins the app explicitly added → same importer/shim path.
  • Watch for apps that inject cordova.js directly or call cordova.exec(...) — those route through the Cordova importer (harder; see plugin-compatibility doc §Cordova).

docs.title: Is it worth it?
docs.text:
Yes — as a go-to-market on-ramp, not a runtime compatibility layer. Rationale:

  1. Market timing. Microsoft App Center retired (March 2025) and CodePush was deprecated, orphaning many hybrid apps. Appflow is expensive and Ionic-locked. There is an actively-shopping audience.
  2. The migration command is the funnel. "Bring your existing Ionic/F7 app, get OTA + auto-rollback, no lock-in" converts directly into Server Code Push customers (see project/business/business-model.md).
  3. Cost is bounded. UI is free; the work is the importer + compat shim + ~3 table-stakes plugins — not an open-ended compatibility treadmill.

Scope guardrail: cap support at the importer + compat shim + Level-1 certified plugins. Deep-runtime plugins (those touching bridge.getWebView(), CordovaInterface, etc.) stay manual port with generated scaffolding. Never inherit another framework's runtime.

docs.title: Capsule Framework — Architecture Guidance
docs.text: Capsule — app ships inside a managed native capsule.

docs.title: Core Architectural Principles
docs.text:
The native shell is a dependency, not source code.

Developers never edit Android Gradle files or Xcode projects. The shell is versioned like any npm/maven package. SDK update = bump a version number.

Shell = native OS capabilities. Plugins = code-logic integrations.

The shell always delivers every native OS API (camera, GPS, NFC, Bluetooth, haptics, biometrics, push, calls, filesystem, DB, etc.) — unused ones are tree-shaken by R8/linker at app build time. What the shell does not include: third-party SDK wrappers, auth providers, analytics, payment SDKs, or any integration whose value is code logic rather than hardware access. Those are community plugins. This line is a hard boundary — crossing it would couple the shell to third-party release cycles and bloat every app with SDKs it doesn't use.

HTTP = data. Bridge = events. No mixing.

The embedded HTTP server (CivetWeb on both platforms — adr-004) handles request/response data flows — API calls, SSR, mutations. The Bridge (JavascriptInterface) handles push and events — native APIs, real-time updates, sensor streams. These two channels are never mixed. WebSockets/SSE in the embedded server are deferred-by-design future fidelity features (see adr-004), not part of the current minimal surface.

Invisible infrastructure.

The embedded HTTP server, QuickJS runtime, port numbers, and bundle format are implementation details. Developers write a web app. They never encounter the HTTP server, QuickJS, ports, or bundles in their capsule.config.ts, CLI output, or documentation. Crash recovery is silent. Rollback is silent. The framework's complexity is invisible.

Interfaces + fakes are mandatory.

Every new component ships with an interface and a fake implementation on the same day. No exceptions. This is not a testing preference — it is the architecture. CapsuleServer + FakeCapsuleServer, QuickJSEngine + FakeQuickJSEngine, SplashController + FakeSplashController. All CapsuleRuntime behavior is covered by pure JVM unit tests with no device needed.

docs.text:
