docs.title: All manifest fields
docs.text: Field Required Description name Yes Plugin identifier — used as the bridge prefix (barcode.scan) version Yes Semver platforms Yes ["android"], ["ios"], or ["android", "ios"] android.permissions No Android manifest permissions (no android.permission. prefix) android.minSdk No Override app minSdk for this plugin android.dependencies No Maven coordinates — CLI merges into generated build.gradle (see below) ios.infoPlist No Keys injected into Info.plist ios.capabilities No Xcode capabilities (push-notifications, nfc, etc.) ios.podDependencies No CocoaPods dependencies — [{ "name": "ZXingObjC", "version": "~> 3.6" }] sourceRepo Required for @capsule-community/* Git URL — enables capsule eject. Without this field, capsule plugin publish rejects publishing under the community scope.

docs.title: Gradle / CocoaPods Dependencies
docs.text:
Declare third-party dependencies your plugin needs. The CLI collects these at capsule sync time, resolves conflicts across all installed plugins, and injects into the generated build files — no Gradle knowledge required.

"android": {
  "dependencies": [
    "com.google.zxing:core:3.5.0",
    "androidx.camera:camera-core:1.3.0",
    "androidx.camera:camera-lifecycle:1.3.0"
  ]
}

Conflict resolution: If two plugins require the same groupId:artifactId at different versions, the CLI applies "highest compatible version wins" (mirrors Gradle default) and prints a summary at capsule sync. Hard errors only when versions are in different majors — CLI names exactly which plugins conflict. Developers can use android.gradleOverrides as a last resort.

ProGuard / R8: If your plugin uses reflection, ship a proguard.rules file at the plugin root: 

# proguard.rules
-keep class com.example.myplugin.** { *; }
The CLI merges this into the generated proguard-rules.pro. Without a proguard.rules file, the CLI adds a conservative blanket -keep for your plugin's package — safe but less optimized. R8 is enabled by default on release builds.

docs.title: Android — CapsulePlugin Base Class API
docs.text:
Every Android plugin extends CapsulePlugin:

import dev.capsule.bridge.CapsulePlugin
import dev.capsule.bridge.CapsuleBridge
import dev.capsule.bridge.BridgeCall
import dev.capsule.bridge.BridgeMethod

@CapsulePlugin(name = "barcode")
class BarcodeScanner(bridge: CapsuleBridge) : CapsulePlugin(bridge) {

    // ─── Called once when the app starts ──────────────────────────────────────
    override fun load() {
        // initialize resources, open connections
    }

    // ─── Called when app goes to background ───────────────────────────────────
    override fun pause() { /* release camera */ }

    // ─── Called when app returns to foreground ────────────────────────────────
    override fun resume() { /* reacquire */ }

    // ─── Called when app is destroyed ─────────────────────────────────────────
    override fun destroy() { /* close DB, free memory */ }

    // ─── Plugin methods — exposed to JS via @BridgeMethod ─────────────────────
    @BridgeMethod
    fun scan(call: BridgeCall) {
        val quality = call.getFloat("quality", 0.8f)
        val facing  = call.getString("facing", "back")

        onMain {
            // UI work must run on main thread
            startCameraIntent { result ->
                call.resolve(mapOf(
                    "value"  to result.rawValue,
                    "format" to result.format
                ))
            }
        }
    }

    @BridgeMethod
    fun getFlash(call: BridgeCall) {
        call.resolve(mapOf("enabled" to isFlashOn()))
    }

    @BridgeMethod
    fun setFlash(call: BridgeCall) {
        val enable = call.getBoolean("enable", false)
        setFlashEnabled(enable)
        call.resolve()           // resolve with no data
    }
}

docs.title: CapsulePlugin helpers (inherited)
docs.text:
// Thread dispatchers
onMain { /* run on UI thread */ }
onIO   { /* run on IO thread (suspend) */ }

// Access to Android context
bridge.context        // Application context
bridge.activity       // Current Activity
bridge.webView        // The WebView instance

// Emit an event to the web layer (no active JS call needed)
emit("barcode.onScanResult", mapOf("value" to "123", "format" to "QR"))

docs.title: Android — BridgeCall API
docs.text: The call object is your window into the JS request and your way to respond.

docs.title: Reading parameters
docs.text:
// Strings
call.getString("key")                  // String? — null if missing
call.getString("key", "default")       // String  — with default

// Numbers
call.getInt("key", 0)                  // Int
call.getLong("key", 0L)                // Long
call.getFloat("key", 0f)              // Float
call.getDouble("key", 0.0)            // Double

// Boolean
call.getBoolean("key", false)          // Boolean

// Nested object (as Map)
call.getObject("options")              // Map<String, Any>?

// Array
call.getArray("items")                 // List<Any>?

// Check presence
call.has("key")                        // Boolean

// Raw JSON string of all params
call.paramsJson                        // String

docs.title: Sending responses
docs.text:
// Resolve with data
call.resolve(mapOf("value" to "hello", "count" to 42))

// Resolve with no data (void method)
call.resolve()

// Reject with an error code and message
call.reject(2001, "Camera permission denied")

// Capsule standard error codes (matches known-issues.md bridge spec):
// 1xxx — framework/bridge errors (reserved for framework)
// 2xxx — permission errors
// 3xxx — hardware/resource errors (camera unavailable, not found)
// 4xxx — plugin-specific logic errors
// 5xxx — user cancellation

docs.title: iOS — CapsulePlugin Base Class API
docs.text:
import CapsuleBridge

@CapsulePlugin("barcode")
class BarcodeScanner: CapsulePlugin {

    // ─── Called once when the app starts ──────────────────────────────────────
    override func load() { }

    override func pause()   { }
    override func resume()  { }
    override func destroy() { }

    // ─── Plugin methods ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    @BridgeMethod
    func scan(_ call: BridgeCall) {
        let quality = call.getFloat("quality") ?? 0.8
        let facing  = call.getString("facing") ?? "back"

        // WKScriptMessageHandler delivers on main thread — safe to do UI work directly
        startCamera(quality: quality, facing: facing) { result in
            call.resolve([
                "value":  result.rawValue,
                "format": result.format
            ])
        }
    }

    @BridgeMethod
    func getFlash(_ call: BridgeCall) {
        call.resolve(["enabled": isFlashOn()])
    }

    @BridgeMethod
    func setFlash(_ call: BridgeCall) {
        let enable = call.getBool("enable") ?? false
        setFlashEnabled(enable)
        call.resolve()
    }
}

docs.title: TypeScript — Web Bridge (web/index.ts)
docs.text:
The web layer is what app developers import. Write it against @capsule/core.

// capsule-plugins/barcode/web/index.ts
import { bridge } from '@capsule/core'

// ─── Types ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

export interface ScanResult {
  value: string
  format: 'QR' | 'EAN13' | 'CODE128' | 'DATAMATRIX' | string
}

export interface ScanOptions {
  quality?: number          // 0.0–1.0, default 0.8
  facing?: 'front' | 'back' // default 'back'
}

// ─── Plugin API ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

export const barcode = {
  /**
   * Open the camera and scan a barcode or QR code.
   * Resolves when a code is detected or the user cancels.
   */
  scan(options?: ScanOptions): Promise<ScanResult> {
    return bridge.call('barcode.scan', options ?? {})
  },

  /**
   * Get current flash state.
   */
  getFlash(): Promise<{ enabled: boolean }> {
    return bridge.call('barcode.getFlash', {})
  },

  /**
   * Enable or disable the camera flash.
   */
  setFlash(enable: boolean): Promise<void> {
    return bridge.call('barcode.setFlash', { enable })
  },

  /**
   * Subscribe to continuous scan results.
   * Returns an unsubscribe function.
   */
  onScanResult(handler: (data: ScanResult) => void): () => void {
    return bridge.on('barcode.onScanResult', handler)
  }
}

docs.title: @capsule/core API
docs.text:
import { bridge } from '@capsule/core'

// Single call → Promise
bridge.call<T>(method: string, params: object): Promise<T>

// Subscribe to native events
bridge.on(event: string, handler: (data: unknown) => void): () => void
// Returns unsubscribe function — call it to stop listening

// Unsubscribe manually (alternative to returned function)
bridge.off(event: string, handler: Function): void

docs.title: App Developer Usage (end result)
docs.text:
After the plugin is built, the app developer uses:

// Any component — React, Vue, Svelte, or Vanilla
import { barcode } from './capsule-plugins/barcode/web'
// or, if published to npm:
import { barcode } from '@capsule/barcode'

// Single scan
const result = await barcode.scan({ facing: 'back' })
console.log(result.value, result.format)

// Event listener (for continuous mode)
const unsubscribe = barcode.onScanResult((data) => {
  console.log('Scanned:', data.value)
})

// Later: cleanup
unsubscribe()

docs.title: Auto-generating TypeScript Types
docs.text:
Instead of writing web/index.ts by hand, annotate the Kotlin class and generate:

@CapsulePlugin(name = "barcode")
class BarcodeScanner(bridge: CapsuleBridge) : CapsulePlugin(bridge) {

    @BridgeMethod
    @Returns(ScanResult::class)
    fun scan(
        @BridgeParam("quality", optional = true, default = "0.8") quality: Float,
        @BridgeParam("facing",  optional = true, default = "back") facing: String
    ): Unit

    @BridgeEvent
    @Emits(ScanResult::class)
    fun onScanResult(): Unit
}

@BridgeType
data class ScanResult(
    val value: String,
    val format: String
)

capsule generate types --plugin barcode
# writes capsule-plugins/barcode/web/index.d.ts and index.ts

docs.title: Platform-Conditional Code in the Web Bridge
docs.text:
Some plugins work on one platform only. The web layer handles this gracefully:

import { bridge, getPlatform } from '@capsule/core'

export const haptics = {
  impact(style: 'light' | 'medium' | 'heavy'): Promise<void> {
    // Web platform has no haptics — silently no-op
    if (getPlatform() === 'web') return Promise.resolve()
    return bridge.call('haptics.impact', { style })
  }
}

getPlatform() returns 'android' | 'ios' | 'web'.

docs.title: Web layer changes (TypeScript / web/index.ts)
docs.text: Vite HMR applies instantly — no rebuild needed. Changes to the TypeScript bridge are live in under 50ms.

docs.title: Native layer changes (.kt / .swift / .c)
docs.text:
Native code requires a full recompile. capsule dev watches for .kt and .swift file changes and prints a reminder:

⚠ Native source changed: capsule-plugins/barcode/android/BarcodeScanner.kt
  Hot reload does not apply to native code changes.
  Run: capsule build android  (then re-deploy to emulator)

The Vite dev server keeps running — only the native layer needs rebuilding. Typical incremental Kotlin rebuild via Gradle build cache: 5–15 seconds (not a full rebuild).

Practical workflow: 1. Edit .kt file 2. See the warning in the capsule dev terminal 3. In a second terminal: capsule build android && capsule run android 4. Continue editing web code — Vite HMR resumes immediately

docs.title: Publishing a Plugin to npm (Mode 1 Binary)
docs.text:
When your source plugin is ready to share:

# Package + publish
capsule plugin publish ./capsule-plugins/barcode

# What this does:
# 1. Runs capsule build android + ios to produce AAR and XCFramework
# 2. Packages AAR, XCFramework, and web/index.ts into an npm tarball
# 3. Publishes to npm as the configured package name
# 4. Optionally publishes AAR to GitHub Packages (Maven) and XCFramework via SPM

After publishing, other developers install it with: 

npm install @yourscope/barcode
# Then add '@yourscope/barcode' to capsule.config.ts plugins array

To let them fork the plugin source: 

// capsule-plugin.json
{
  "sourceRepo": "https://github.com/you/capsule-plugin-barcode"
}

They can then capsule eject @yourscope/barcode to get full source access.

docs.title: Complete Worked Example — @capsule/storage
docs.text: A localStorage-on-steroids plugin: web-compatible API, native backend (SQLite on device, localStorage on browser).

docs.title: capsule-plugin.json
docs.text:
{
  "name": "storage",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "platforms": ["android", "ios"],
  "android": { "permissions": [] },
  "ios": {}
}

docs.title: android/Storage.kt
docs.text:
@CapsulePlugin(name = "storage")
class Storage(bridge: CapsuleBridge) : CapsulePlugin(bridge) {

    private lateinit var db: StorageDatabase   // Room or SQLite

    override fun load() {
        db = StorageDatabase.open(bridge.context)
    }

    @BridgeMethod
    fun get(call: BridgeCall) {
        val key = call.getString("key") ?: return call.reject(4001, "key is required")
        onIO {
            val value = db.get(key)
            call.resolve(mapOf("value" to value))
        }
    }

    @BridgeMethod
    fun set(call: BridgeCall) {
        val key   = call.getString("key")   ?: return call.reject(4001, "key is required")
        val value = call.getString("value") ?: return call.reject(4001, "value is required")
        onIO {
            db.set(key, value)
            call.resolve()
        }
    }

    @BridgeMethod
    fun remove(call: BridgeCall) {
        val key = call.getString("key") ?: return call.reject(4001, "key is required")
        onIO {
            db.remove(key)
            call.resolve()
        }
    }

    @BridgeMethod
    fun clear(call: BridgeCall) {
        onIO {
            db.clear()
            call.resolve()
        }
    }

    override fun destroy() {
        db.close()
    }
}

docs.title: ios/Storage.swift
docs.text:
@CapsulePlugin("storage")
class Storage: CapsulePlugin {

    private var db: StorageDatabase!

    override func load() {
        db = StorageDatabase()
    }

    @BridgeMethod
    func get(_ call: BridgeCall) {
        guard let key = call.getString("key") else {
            return call.reject(4001, "key is required")
        }
        DispatchQueue.global(qos: .userInitiated).async {
            let value = self.db.get(key)
            call.resolve(["value": value as Any])
        }
    }

    @BridgeMethod
    func set(_ call: BridgeCall) {
        guard let key   = call.getString("key"),
              let value = call.getString("value") else {
            return call.reject(4001, "key and value are required")
        }
        DispatchQueue.global(qos: .userInitiated).async {
            self.db.set(key, value: value)
            call.resolve()
        }
    }

    @BridgeMethod
    func remove(_ call: BridgeCall) {
        guard let key = call.getString("key") else {
            return call.reject(4001, "key is required")
        }
        DispatchQueue.global(qos: .userInitiated).async {
            self.db.remove(key)
            call.resolve()
        }
    }

    @BridgeMethod
    func clear(_ call: BridgeCall) {
        DispatchQueue.global(qos: .userInitiated).async {
            self.db.clear()
            call.resolve()
        }
    }
}

docs.title: web/index.ts
docs.text:
import { bridge, getPlatform } from '@capsule/core'

export const storage = {
  async get(key: string): Promise<string | null> {
    if (getPlatform() === 'web') return localStorage.getItem(key)
    const { value } = await bridge.call<{ value: string | null }>('storage.get', { key })
    return value
  },

  async set(key: string, value: string): Promise<void> {
    if (getPlatform() === 'web') { localStorage.setItem(key, value); return }
    await bridge.call('storage.set', { key, value })
  },

  async remove(key: string): Promise<void> {
    if (getPlatform() === 'web') { localStorage.removeItem(key); return }
    await bridge.call('storage.remove', { key })
  },

  async clear(): Promise<void> {
    if (getPlatform() === 'web') { localStorage.clear(); return }
    await bridge.call('storage.clear', {})
  }
}

docs.title: Quick Reference Card
docs.text:
capsule plugin create <name>           scaffold new source plugin
capsule plugin call <name> <method>    test a method on the emulator
capsule plugin check <name>            validate TS bridge vs native annotations
capsule generate types --plugin <name> generate TS from Kotlin/Swift annotations
capsule plugin publish ./path          build + publish to npm
capsule eject @scope/plugin            fork npm plugin to local source
capsule override <capability>          patch a built-in core capability (camera, gps, push, etc.)

@CapsulePlugin(name = "foo")           mark class as a plugin
@BridgeMethod                          expose a method to JS
@BridgeParam("key")                    annotate a parameter (for type gen)
@BridgeEvent / @Emits(T::class)        mark an event emitter (for type gen)
@BridgeType                            mark a data class for TS generation

docs.title: Capsule Framework — OSS / Package Release
docs.text:
Scope: publishing the framework itself — the public GitHub repos and the distributable packages (npm + Maven AAR). This is not app-store publishing — that's publishing.md (Play/App Store via Fastlane). Two different meanings of "publish".

Status: D1–D4 decided (2026-10-24); D5 (registries) and D6 (iOS caveat) open. This doc is the pre-publish gate for the first public push and, later, the package releases.

docs.title: State (2026-10-24)
docs.text:
• Product code has no hardcoded absolute paths; gradlew is cross-platform; CI is GitHub Actions on Linux + macOS (ci.md).
  • Contributor tooling is OS-agnostic Node (scripts/*.mjs as root pnpm scripts, machine paths in a git-ignored .env.local) — the old PowerShell scripts/ repo is retired.
  • The remaining "works on my machine" friction is CAPSULE_SHELL_OVERRIDE_PATH: until the AAR is published (D5), a developer builds the AAR locally and the CLI points at it.

docs.title: D1 — Target & timing: public GitHub now ✅
docs.text:
• Public repos on GitHub (alex-vinny) now, not a private Azure DevOps phase first.
  • Why: public repos get free GitHub-hosted macOS runners, which removed the only reason for the private-Azure plan (1:1 macOS minutes while private).
  • Fresh history: each public repo starts from a single initial commit (the private history, which carried a work email and pre-cleanup docs, is archived privately). Commit author: the GitHub noreply address. After the first push, history is never rewritten.

docs.title: D2 — What is public ✅
docs.text:
• Everything public, docs included — business model, pricing, server design and infrastructure notes too (no secrets in them; the maintainer's own cluster names stay generic).
  • capsule_framework (repo; the folder is capsule/) is the monorepo: framework, docs and examples/ (folded in — demos change with the framework, so they land in the same PR and CI can run them).
  • capsule-templates stays a separate public repo: templates churn much faster, and capsule init fetches them with giget (github:alex-vinny/capsule-templates/<name>).
  • The PowerShell scripts repo is retired (see D4.1).
  • The repo reads standalone: root README.md, AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md.

docs.title: D3 — License model (open-core) ✅
docs.text:
• Framework (capsule, examples, templates): Apache-2.0 (patent grant).
  • packages/codesync-api: AGPL-3.0 — anyone can self-host the OTA server; a modified version offered as a hosted service must publish its changes. The maintainer's hosted CodeSync is the paid offer (business model).
  • Done: LICENSE, NOTICE (third-party: CivetWeb, QuickJS-ng — MIT), CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md (GitHub private vulnerability reporting), CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md (Contributor Covenant 2.1), license fields in every package.json.

docs.title: D4 — OS independence
docs.text:
1. ✅ Dev scripts ported to Node — pnpm dev:env, pnpm with-env, pnpm dev:emulator, pnpm dev:examples, pnpm update:quickjs, pnpm update:civetweb, pnpm verify (commands.md). The OTA bundle ZIP is built in-process (archiver), not with PowerShell.
  2. ⬜ Kill CAPSULE_SHELL_OVERRIDE_PATH by resolving the AAR from Maven (D5).
  3. ⬜ Pin the toolchain with mise (or asdf): node/pnpm/java in one file.
  4. ⬜ Devcontainer matching the ubuntu CI for the Android SDK/NDK. The emulator still needs KVM (Linux host), so device work stays local.
  5. Nix: not first — androidenv is fiddly; devbox is the gentler option if wanted later.

docs.title: D5 — Package registries: npm + Maven go together (open)
docs.text: They're the two halves of "install without cloning the repo": - npm → publish @capsule/cli, @capsule/core, @capsule/ui-kit to npmjs.org so capsule init / installs resolve real versions. (Check the @capsule scope is available first.) - Maven → publish the Android AAR to Maven Central (GitHub Packages as an interim) so the shell resolves as a normal Gradle dependency — the fix for D4.2. - Never commit registry tokens. A committed .npmrc holds only non-secret config; auth comes from CI secrets (NPM_TOKEN) / Maven credentials in the environment. - Version placeholder reconciled (2026-10-24): templates ask for @capsule/core ^0.1.0, the real version. capsule init still cannot resolve it until the package is on npm.

docs.title: D6 — iOS is not a blocker (open caveat)
docs.text:
• Nothing technical blocks an Android-first release: the iOS embedded server, db and ai providers are built and tested on Linux + macOS CI; the WKWebView shell is Phase 4.
  • Label early releases clearly (alpha, Android-first, iOS in bring-up).

docs.title: Pre-publish checklist (before the first public push)
docs.text:
• [x] D1 target chosen — public GitHub now, fresh single-commit repos, noreply author.
  • [x] Docs decision (D2) — everything public; examples in the monorepo; templates separate.
  • [x] Standalone README + LICENSE/NOTICE + CONTRIBUTING/SECURITY/CODE_OF_CONDUCT (D3).
  • [x] Dev scripts ported to Node (D4.1); OTA ZIP no longer needs PowerShell.
  • [x] CI on GitHub Actions (Linux + macOS, ci.md).
  • [ ] Secret scan of the tree — gitleaks detect --no-git on each repo right before its initial commit (fresh history means only the files themselves need scanning).
  • [x] Reconcile package versions (D5) — templates ask for @capsule/core ^0.1.0.
  • [x] Template source in the CLI → github:alex-vinny/capsule-templates/<name>.
  • [ ] Publish pipeline — npm + Maven AAR publish jobs (D5); until then keep the local CAPSULE_SHELL_OVERRIDE_PATH path documented.
  • [ ] Contributor onboarding extras — devcontainer / mise (D4.3–4).

docs.title: Pointers
docs.text:
• Store publishing (different topic) → publishing.md
  • Phase sequencing → roadmap.md
  • Dependency reconciliations that overlap D5 → upkeep.md
  • CI → ci.md, .github/workflows/ci.yml

docs.title: Authoring a Capsule Template
docs.text: How to create a scaffold template for capsule init. A template is a starter web app that giget copies into a new project — distinct from a plugin (a native SDK wrapper; see plugin-authoring.md). The official set lives in the templates/ repo; you can also point init at any custom source.

docs.title: What a template is
docs.text: A template's files become the user's generated project verbatim (giget copies the subdir). So a template is just a minimal, runnable Capsule app for one framework. Mirror an existing one — ../../templates/capsule-react-ts-template/ is the reference.

docs.title: Anatomy (the contract)
docs.text:
File / dir Required Notes package.json ✅ Depends on @capsule/core; framework + bundler deps; standard scripts. web entry ✅ index.html (Vite-based) or the framework's equivalent. src/ ✅ The app. Convention: Home tab + Server tab (bridge.call + GET /api/ping) so all templates demo the same surface (see examples/README.md). bundler config ✅ vite.config.ts, angular.json, etc. — non-Vite declares web.devCommand/buildCommand in capsule.config.ts. tsconfig.json for TS — .gitignore ✅ node_modules/, build output, .capsule/. README.md recommended The generated app's readme: what it is + how to dev/build/run. Portable — no machine-specific absolute paths. Don't restate framework or Capsule docs. capsule.config.ts optional capsule init/add generate it if absent; if a custom template ships its own, init won't clobber it.

No machine-specific files in a template — same rule as the examples/ folder. The README and all paths must be portable.

docs.title: Using / registering a template
docs.text:
# Official (manifest -> templates-repo subdir):
capsule init my-app --template react-ts
# Any giget source (GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket/tarball):
capsule init my-app --template gh:acme/capsule-tpl#v2
# Local path:
capsule init my-app --template ./my-local-template

Add an official template (no CLI release needed): drop the subdir into the templates/ repo and add a row to templates/manifest.json:

{ "value": "solid-ts", "title": "Solid + TypeScript", "dir": "capsule-solid-ts-template" }

Resolution (from cli.md init): dev reads local templates/manifest.json and copies the subdir; prod fetches the manifest from the templates repo and giget pulls gh:<repo>/<dir>#<branch>; the bundled list is the offline fallback.

docs.title: Pending (tracked in roadmap.md §Template extensibility)
docs.text:
• Company/internal template registry via ~/.capsulerc (adds entries to the picker).
  • Confirm the published templates-repo org/name (TEMPLATES_REPO in init.ts) at GitHub publish.

All 7 official templates now ship a portable README.md (the generated app's readme).

See also: cli.md (init implementation), examples/README.md (the shared Home/Server demo convention).

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
Capsule ships an opt-in test harness so a generated app can be tested at every layer that matters — from pure route handlers up to the real WebView on a device — without the developer wiring a toolchain by hand.

Opt in at scaffold time, exactly like Tailwind: 

capsule init my-app --template react-ts --test vitest
Omitting --test shows a prompt (None / Vitest); None is the default and ships zero test files. Mirror of --css none|tailwind.

docs.title: Framework support
docs.text:
Wired for all seven templates. The agnostic tiers (route-contract, route units, QuickJS-fidelity, integration) are identical everywhere; only the component test + vitest config are framework-specific.

Framework Component test Notes react-ts ✅ @testing-library/react vue-ts ✅ @testing-library/vue svelte-ts ✅ @testing-library/svelte Vitest projects split (see wiring notes) vanilla-ts / vanilla-js ✅ raw DOM loads index.html, imports main, clicks by id jquery-bootstrap ✅ raw DOM native .click() fires jQuery's delegated handlers angular-ts ⏳ agnostic tiers only TestBed/analog component test is a follow-up

docs.title: Why layered
docs.text:
Manual device testing (install → launch → screenshot → eyeball) is slow, token-/time-expensive, and flaky. Almost everything it checks is actually deterministic and can be asserted off-device in milliseconds. Each layer below catches a distinct failure class; only the last genuinely needs a device.

Tier File (react-ts) Runtime Catches 1 — Route contract src/test/route-contract.test.ts Vitest (node) A bridge.call('x') / fetch('/api/y') with no handler file (the 404 class) — statically, before build 1 — Route units src/test/routes.test.ts Vitest (node) Handler logic — pure functions, no bridge/server 2 — Component src/test/app.test.tsx Vitest (jsdom) UI wiring — renders <App/> against @capsule/core's FakeBridge; tab nav, async result plumbing 3 — QuickJS fidelity src/test/quickjs.test.ts Vitest (node) + quickjs-emscripten "works in dev Node sidecar, breaks in embedded QuickJS" — bundles routes like capsule build, runs dispatch/handleHttpRequest in a real QuickJS, asserts fetch is absent — Integration (HML) src/test/integration.test.ts Vitest (node) Live backend — gated on CAPSULE_API_BASE, skipped by default so CI stays hermetic 4 — On-device smoke app/src/androidTest/.../SmokeTest.kt Gradle connectedAndroidTest (Espresso-Web) Blank screen / WebView-attach / asset-load / JS crash — the one class only a real device/emulator shows

docs.title: Running
docs.text:
capsule test                 # tiers 1–3 + integration (one-shot, hermetic)
capsule test --watch         # vitest watch mode
capsule test routes          # extra args pass through to vitest (filters/flags)

CAPSULE_API_BASE=https://hml.example.com capsule test   # also runs the HML test

# Tier 4 (needs a device/emulator):
#   debug   → run `capsule dev` first (loads the dev server via adb reverse)
#   release → self-contained (embedded bundle)
cd .capsule/android && ./gradlew :app:connectedDebugAndroidTest

docs.title: How it's wired (for maintainers)
docs.text:
• Injector: packages/cli/src/testing.ts → applyTesting(projectDir, template). Copies assets/testing/_shared/ (the agnostic tiers, identical everywhere) then assets/testing/<framework>/ (vitest config + setup + component test) into the project, and patches package.json with test scripts + SHARED_DEPS + FRAMEWORK_DEPS[template]. Mirrors tailwind.ts. Called from init.ts when --test vitest (or the prompt) is chosen; falls through with a notice otherwise.
  • Component-test mock: each test does vi.mock('@capsule/core', …) returning a fresh FakeBridge as the bridge export, then reads it back via the mocked import (const fake = bridge as FakeBridge) — no __fake export hack, no hoisting trap. Vanilla/jQuery load index.html into jsdom and import main so the real handlers attach, then click by id.
  • Tier-3 detail: the QuickJS test runs in the node Vitest environment (// @vitest-environment node) — esbuild's TextEncoder instanceof Uint8Array invariant fails under jsdom. It re-creates the CLI's bundleRoutes() IIFE so it exercises the same dispatch contract Kotlin calls.
  • Svelte uses Vitest projects: svelteTesting() forces resolve.conditions: ['browser'] (so components get their client build), which would also make quickjs-emscripten load its network-fetching browser WASM. So the component test runs in a browser-conditioned jsdom project and the agnostic tiers run in a plain Node project. Other frameworks don't need this.
  • Tier-4 generator: sync.ts writes SmokeTest.kt + androidTest deps (espresso-web, ext-junit, runner) + testInstrumentationRunner on every sync. The assertion is content-agnostic (non-empty body text via a Hamcrest-1.3-safe matcher) because .capsule/android is regenerated each sync and can't be hand-tailored. Espresso pins Hamcrest 1.3 — avoid 2.x matchers (matchesPattern, blankOrNullString).

docs.title: Verification status (2026-06-12)
docs.text:
• Tiers 1–3 + integration: PASS in every wired framework, each verified by injecting into its *-from-template example and running vitest: react / vue / svelte 12 passed, vanilla-ts / vanilla-js / jquery 11 passed, angular 9 passed (agnostic tiers, no component test) — 1 skipped (integration) in each. The contract test was proven to fail with Missing JSON-RPC route file(s): hello when hello.ts is removed.
  • capsule test + the applyTesting injector: verified end-to-end (command runs the suite; injector copies _shared + framework files and merges scripts + deps).
  • Tier 4: assembleDebugAndroidTest builds green; the on-device mechanism is proven (Espresso-Web launched MainActivity and read the live DOM via getText()). A fully-green connectedAndroidTest against a feature app (react-ts-native) is intermittent due to instrumentation/emulator state (NoActivityResumedException, post-test app uninstall) on a long-running session — not a scaffold defect.

docs.title: Follow-ups
docs.text:
• Angular component test. Angular ships the agnostic tiers only. A component test needs Angular's TestBed wired into Vitest — e.g. @analogjs/vite-plugin-angular
  • a setup that calls initTestEnvironment, then @testing-library/angular's render(AppComponent). Add it under assets/testing/angular-ts/ and the deps to FRAMEWORK_DEPS['angular-ts'].
  • Tier-4 hardening for permission-requesting / slow-boot apps: a GrantPermissionRule (from config.android.permissions) and/or a launch retry to make connectedAndroidTest robust against NoActivityResumedException.
  • AI / agents testing (Phase 3 spike onward) maps onto these same tiers via a FakeAiProvider / scripted FakeLlm — the model is a provider behind the bridge, so the agent loop is deterministic given a scripted sequence of model responses. Tier 1 asserts tool-registry wiring + routing logic; Tier 2 renders against a canned ai.generate; Tier 3 runs the agent loop in real QuickJS with inference stubbed; the integration tier (gated on CAPSULE_AI_*) and Tier-4 device smoke assert structure not content against a live model (valid tool-call JSON, termination, token/latency budgets). See ../decisions/0003-ai-and-agents.md § Testing.

docs.title: Manual test plan
docs.text:
Testing matrix: browser-dev · emulator-dev · emulator-release · device-release

Legend: ✅ expected pass · ❌ expected fail (N/A for env) · 🔲 not yet tested

Automated harness (opt-in): much of this matrix is now coverable without manual device steps. capsule init --test vitest ships route-contract + unit + component + QuickJS-fidelity tests (run via capsule test) plus an on-device Espresso-Web smoke test — see the harness sections above.

docs.title: Group 0 — From-template (7 examples)
docs.text:
Validates that capsule init output works identically across all supported frameworks. All 7 have identical UI: Home tab (Say Hello alert) + Server tab (bridge.call hello + GET /api/ping).

The original "state resets" expectation was wrong and has been removed. react-from-template additionally has a Clear button to reset results manually — that button is example-only for now; propagating it to the other 6 templates is a pending TODO (see session log).

docs.text:
Cell Date Result 0.1 react-from-template · browser-dev 2026-06-11 ✅ PASS — all 8 checks (render, tab bar, React badge, Say Hello alert, hello route Hello, World! (from QuickJS), /api/ping ok, tab persistence + Clear, HMR reload) 0.1 react-from-template · emulator-dev 2026-06-11 ✅ PASS — surfaced + fixed a real gap: bridge.call('hello') returned METHOD_NOT_FOUND because the native bridge intercepted it and never reached the dev sidecar. Now returns the hello message on-device in dev. 0.1 react-from-template · emulator-release 2026-06-11 ✅ PASS — embedded runtime (QuickJS + NanoHTTPD at the time, no dev server; server since replaced by CivetWeb — re-run this row). Say Hello native alert; hello route via real QuickJS; /api/ping via NanoHTTPD→QuickJS. 0.2 vue-from-template · browser-dev 2026-06-12 ✅ PASS 0.4 angular-from-template · build 2026-06-12 🔧 Fixed build error — ng build type-checks (Vite/esbuild don't), caught res.message on unknown. Added generic: bridge.call<{ message: string }>('hello', …). 0.4 angular-from-template · browser-dev 2026-06-12 🔧 Fixed two-click bug — bridge/fetch promises resolve outside Angular's zone (__capsule.js wraps window.fetch before zone.js patches it; on-device the native __capsuleReceive callback is also out-of-zone), so the view updated only on the next click. Fixed with ChangeDetectorRef.detectChanges() after each async result in callHello/callPing. Both Angular fixes applied to the example AND the canonical capsule-angular-ts-template (the latter would otherwise break capsule init output and ship the two-click bug). The untyped bridge.call pattern is latent in the other examples but only Angular's compiler/zone surface it.

Dev-mode JSON-RPC routes on-device: as of 2026-06-11, custom src/routes/*.ts work under capsule dev android (native bridge forwards unmatched methods to the dev sidecar). Previously they only worked in browser-dev and release. Requires the dev server running + adb reverse (both set by capsule dev).

docs.title: Tailwind (optional --css tailwind) — 2026-06-12
docs.text:
Optional capsule init --css tailwind ships Tailwind v3 + a shared Capsule native preset (iOS look on the existing .btn/.card/.tab class names — no markup rewrite). Default stays --css none.

Example Build Notes react / vue / svelte / vanilla-js / vanilla-ts · build ✅ vite build green; CSS ≈7 KB (base + preset) angular · build ✅ ng build green; styles.css 7.75 KB (global via angular.json) jquery · build ✅ kept on Bootstrap (Tailwind skipped by design)

1.2 emulator-dev — 2026-06-12. PASS. Built debug APK (release-AAR override), installed + launched on emulator-5554 against capsule dev (Vite :5181 + sidecar :6181 + adb reverse). Verified on-device by screenshot: all 4 tabs (Home/Tools/Settings/Server) render with iOS-style native layout; Home — Device info live via bridge (Model sdk_gphone64_x86_64, Google, Android 15/SDK 35, Virtual true, WebView 124.0.6367.219) + Location resolved to 37.42200, -122.08400 after adb emu geo fix; Tools — Haptics/Clipboard/Storage sections render; Settings — Alert-style radios (Default/Dark/Brand/Warning) + native Show alert dialog ("Hello from Capsule!" → OK) confirms the alert bridge; Server — Call hello route → "Hello, World! (from QuickJS)" and GET /api/ping → {"status":"ok","path":"/api/ping"} rendered inline; tab navigation between all 4 tabs works.

Finding (fixed this session): the example shipped with no route files — its Server tab calls hello (JSON-RPC) and /api/ping (HTTP) but src/routes/ and src/server/routes/ were empty, so both returned 404. Added canonical src/routes/hello.ts + src/server/routes/ping.ts (same content as the from-template baseline); the running capsule dev sidecar hot-reloaded them and both resolve on-device. Note: the debug APK used here was built before the route files were added, but emulator-dev forwards route calls to the Node sidecar (not the bundled QuickJS), so the empty assets/server/bundle.js is irrelevant for this pass — a rebuild is required before the emulator-release pass so the QuickJS bundle includes the new routes.

Carried-over findings (still apply, see §1.1): capsule run android installs but doesn't launch (used adb shell am start); dev routes run in the Node sidecar, not real QuickJS (the "(from QuickJS)" string is misleading in dev — real QuickJS verified in the release pass).

docs.title: Group 2 — Non-Vite transparent proxy (3 examples)
docs.text:
Validates the CLI dev proxy (Option B) — Capsule acts as a transparent HTTP proxy between the WebView and any bundler's dev server. HMR and route injection must work for all three.

Port scheme: devPort = proxy (WebView connects here), devPort+1 = bundler internal, devPort+1000 = sidecar.

# Example Bundler devPort Bundler port Sidecar 2.1 webpack-preact Webpack 5 5184 5185 6184 2.2 rspack-lit Rspack 1 5186 5187 6186 2.3 rollup-solid Rollup 4 5185 5186 6185

Ports above are the actual devPort values from each example's capsule.config.ts (verified 2026-06-15; previous values 5182/5183/5185 were wrong, same drift as Group 0). Overlap note: 2.1's bundler-internal (5185) and 2.3's proxy (5185) collide, as do 2.3's bundler-internal (5186) and 2.2's proxy (5186) — harmless because Group 2 examples are run one at a time, but don't run them concurrently.

docs.title: Checks (apply to each of the 3)
docs.text:
Check browser-dev emulator-dev emulator-release device-release capsule dev starts without error; proxy log shows correct ports ✅ 🔲 ❌ ❌ Browser at devPort renders app (proxy is transparent) ✅ 🔲 ❌ ❌ /__capsule.js present in page (injected by proxy) ✅ 🔲 ❌ ❌ HMR: edit src file → browser updates without full reload ⚠️ 🔲 ❌ ❌ Native tab: all demo sections render ✅ 🔲 🔲 🔲 Server tab: "Call hello route" → result ✅ 🔲 🔲 🔲 Server tab: "GET /api/ping" → result ✅ 🔲 🔲 🔲 Bundler uses devPort+1 (not the user-facing port) ✅ n/a ❌ ❌ No port conflict with sidecar ✅ 🔲 ❌ ❌

⚠️ HMR check is example-config-dependent, not a proxy capability gap: the proxy's WebSocket-upgrade forwarding works for all three. webpack-preact and rspack-lit propagate edits over the proxied WS but do a live-reload (full page reload), not a true hot-swap — neither example configures a framework HMR boundary (preact-prefresh / lit hot). rollup-solid has no auto-reload at all (rollup-plugin-serve only, no rollup-plugin-livereload) — edits rebuild dist, browser needs a manual refresh.

docs.title: 2.3 rollup-solid extra check
docs.text: Check browser-dev emulator-dev emulator-release device-release CAPSULE_INTERNAL_PORT env var read by rollup-plugin-serve ✅ n/a ❌ ❌ serve plugin binds to port 5186 (not 5185) ✅ n/a ❌ ❌

docs.title: Group 2 results log
docs.text:
Cell Date Result 2.1 webpack-preact · browser-dev 2026-06-15 ✅ PASS — proxy :5184 → bundler :5185, sidecar :6184. App renders (Preact), __capsule.js injected, window.fetch patched, GET /api/ping → {"status":"ok","path":"/api/ping"}, POST /_capsule/rpc hello → {"message":"Hello, World! (from QuickJS)"}, 0 console/page errors (verified headless Chromium). HMR: live-reload via proxied WS. Surfaced + fixed a real proxy bug — see below. 2.2 rspack-lit · browser-dev 2026-06-15 ✅ PASS — proxy :5186 → bundler :5187, sidecar :6186. <capsule-app> renders into Shadow DOM (3188 chars), __capsule.js injected, fetch patched, /api/ping + hello RPC OK, 0 errors. HMR: live-reload via proxied WS (hot: true). 2.3 rollup-solid · browser-dev 2026-06-15 ✅ PASS — proxy :5185 → bundler :5186, sidecar :6185. Solid app renders, __capsule.js injected, fetch patched, /api/ping + hello RPC OK, 0 errors. Extra checks ✅: rollup-plugin-serve reads CAPSULE_INTERNAL_PORT and binds :5186 (not :5185). No auto-reload configured (rebuild-on-save only).

Proxy bug fixed this session (dev-proxy-server.ts forwardInjectHtml): the non-Vite dev proxy buffered the bundler's HTML to inject <script src="/__capsule.js">, but did so assuming uncompressed bytes. Real browsers and the on-device WebView send Accept-Encoding: gzip; webpack-dev-server (default compress: true) then gzips the HTML. The proxy read the gzip bytes as UTF-8 (injection silently no-op'd), stripped the content-encoding header, and forwarded the still-compressed body labeled text/html → a garbled page with no Capsule injection. curl masked it by not requesting compression by default. Fix: delete the accept-encoding request header before forwarding through forwardInjectHtml, so the bundler always returns injectable plaintext. This bug would have broken all non-Vite examples in capsule dev on a real device/emulator, not just in-browser.

docs.text:
These apply across all 13 examples once at least one of each group passes.

Check Notes capsule build android + capsule run android succeeds for each example Full Gradle pipeline adb reverse ports set correctly in dev mode Verify in adb shell Route sidecar starts on devPort+1000 for all examples Check console output src/routes/hello.ts loaded by sidecar (check via Server tab) Sidecar picks up file-based routes src/server/routes/ping.ts responds at /api/ping HTTP route handler Switching to device: WebView connects to same port as browser adb reverse prerequisite Release build: QuickJS evaluates routes (not Node.js sidecar) Check runtime field in ping response

docs.title: Test order recommendation
docs.text:
Group 0.1 (react-from-template) browser-dev → emulator-dev → emulator-release
Group 0 remaining (0.2–0.7) browser-dev only first pass
Group 2 (non-Vite) browser-dev — validates proxy
Group 1 (custom React) emulator-dev — validates full native API coverage
All groups emulator-release → device-release

Start with react-from-template as it has the simplest surface area and covers the entire chain (Vite + sidecar + routes).

docs.title: Dependency & Tooling Upkeep
docs.text: How Capsule keeps every pinned dependency, toolchain and store requirement current — what is automated, what a person decides, and how a bump is applied. The version numbers below are the baseline after the last sweep; the live state always comes from pnpm upkeep, never from this page.

docs.title: The tools
docs.text:
Tool What it does When it runs pnpm upkeep (scripts/upkeep/) One report, 🔴/🟡/🟢/⚪ per row: store rules, Android platform + NDK, Gradle/AGP/Kotlin, every Gradle library, the vendored C (CivetWeb, QuickJS + their security advisories), SwiftPM packages + Xcode/Swift + the Docker image, and Node (pnpm outdated + pnpm audit). On demand; weekly in CI Upkeep workflow (.github/workflows/upkeep.yml) Runs the report weekly and keeps one open "Upkeep report" issue up to date. Mondays + manual dispatch Renovate (renovate.json) Opens the dependency PRs, grouped (Android toolchain, AndroidX, kotlinx, Node dev tooling, examples monthly), and a dependency dashboard. Weekly requirements.json (packages/cli/src/platform/) The curated Google Play / App Store rules, each with its effective date and source URL. Drives the report, capsule doctor and capsule build. Updated by hand, when the report says a watched page changed capsule doctor For app developers: checks their capsule.config.ts against the rules bundled in their CLI, and warns when those rules are over 120 days old. --strict exits non-zero on a violation (for CI). Users run it

pnpm upkeep options: --only <section,…> (store, android-platform, android-toolchain, android-libraries, vendored, swift, node) · --examples (also report the examples/ workspace — run pnpm install there first) · --markdown / --json · --strict (exit 1 on any 🔴) · --offline. Status: 🔴 security advisory or violated store rule · 🟡 behind, or a rule due within 90 days · 🟢 current · ⚪ source unavailable (the run never fails on one source).

docs.title: Where versions live — one source each
docs.text:
What Source of truth Copies (generated or checked) Android toolchain + libraries (AGP, Kotlin, Gradle, compileSdk, minSdk, NDK, AndroidX, …) packages/capsule-android/gradle/libs.versions.toml, gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties, capsule/build.gradle.kts packages/cli/src/platform/android-toolchain.ts — generated by pnpm gen (scripts/gen/android-toolchain.mjs); capsule sync / capsule init read it, so generated apps follow the library. gen:check fails CI when it is stale. Store rules packages/cli/src/platform/requirements.json — Vendored C packages/native/{civetweb,quickjs}/VERSION — (re-vendor with the update scripts) Swift packages Package.swift (ranges) + Package.resolved — Swift toolchain image swift:X.Y-jammy in .github/workflows/ci.yml and scripts/verify.mjs Renovate tracks both Node each package.json + pnpm-lock.yaml; transitive fixes in the root pnpm.overrides — Templates (separate repo) capsule-templates/*/package.json —

When the AAR gains a runtime dependency, add it to APP_LIBRARIES in packages/cli/src/sync/sync.ts too — a local AAR does not carry its dependencies into the app.

Examples and templates (examples/, and the separate capsule-templates repo) are their own installs, so the root audit does not cover them — pnpm upkeep --examples, or pnpm audit in examples/ and in each template folder. 2026-10-24: Angular 19 (out of support, no patched 19.x) → Angular 22, zoneless, TypeScript ~6.0 (@angular/build 22 peers on >=6.0 <6.1); @rspack/cli → 2; vite floor ^6.4.5; every Vite template and example declares "type": "module" (current @sveltejs/vite-plugin-svelte 5.x is ESM-only). Templates: 0.

docs.title: Sweep procedure
docs.text:
1. pnpm upkeep (plus --examples after cd examples && pnpm install). Read the 🔴 first.
  2. Store rules — a 🟡 "page changed since last review" row: read the page, update requirements.json and its reviewed date, then pnpm upkeep --accept-watch <id|all>.
  3. Decide per row: bump now, bump with its group, or hold. A hold gets a reason in scripts/upkeep/knowledge.mjs (HOLDS) so the report explains it next time.
  4. Couplings are in scripts/upkeep/knowledge.mjs (AGP → minimum Gradle, API level → minimum AGP). Re-check them against about-agp and refresh its checked date when you bump the toolchain. AndroidX AARs state their own floor: unzip META-INF/com/android/build/gradle/aar-metadata.properties (minCompileSdk, minAndroidGradlePluginVersion).
  5. Apply the bump (next section), run the tests, log the sweep below.

docs.title: How to apply a bump
docs.text:
• Android — edit the source files above, then pnpm gen (regenerates android-toolchain.ts) and commit both. Renovate cannot run the generator, so on a Renovate toolchain PR run pnpm gen on the branch before it can pass CI.
  • Vendored C — pnpm update:quickjs <tag> / pnpm update:civetweb <tag> (release tags only). Renovate PRs for packages/native/*/VERSION wait for dashboard approval because a VERSION-only change is wrong: run the update script on the branch.
  • Swift — widen the range in Package.swift if needed, then swift package update in the container (pnpm verify:ios runs the tests).
  • Node — bump the range, pnpm install, then the green bar.
  • Tests — pnpm verify, pnpm verify:android, pnpm verify:ios; a QuickJS, CivetWeb, NDK or AGP bump also needs the instrumented tests (connectedDebugAndroidTest) and a device smoke run, because the JVM tier cannot see native or packaging regressions. After any Android change, rebuild the AAR (assembleRelease) before capsule build android.
  • Commit as chore(deps): … / build: ….

docs.title: Cadence
docs.text:
• Weekly: the workflow refreshes the report; skim the issue for 🔴.
  • Quarterly: a full sweep (this page's procedure).
  • At every phase kick-off and before any release.
  • Immediately on a 🔴 (an advisory in shipped code, or a store rule taking effect).

docs.title: CONTEXT — workflows/ (Layer 2: recurring agent procedures)
docs.text:
Stage contracts for multi-step tasks an agent performs repeatedly. Each subfolder is one procedure with an Inputs / Process / Outputs contract (ICM "configure the factory"): load the Inputs, run the Process, produce the Outputs, stop at the human checkpoints. Workspace map: ../CONTEXT.md. Conventions: ../../_core/conventions.md.

Workflow When to run it add-native-api/ Add a new native capability to @capsule/core (interface → Android → demo → tests). author-plugin/ Author a third-party SDK-wrapper plugin (manifest + Android/iOS/web bridge). Forward contract — plugin CLI not built yet. upkeep-sweep/ Periodic dependency/tooling audit across the three version sources.

These are how-to contracts, not task output — they hold no one-off results. A workflow's Outputs are edits to real source + docs, not a new artifact folder (this is a product repo).

docs.title: CONTEXT — add-native-api (stage contract)
docs.text: Add a new native capability to @capsule/core end-to-end. Interface-first: the TS interface and the Android + (eventual) iOS implementations must all satisfy one contract. Area index: ../CONTEXT.md.

docs.title: Inputs (load these first)
docs.text: Source Why ../../../reference/core-api.md The @capsule/core API spec + error-code ranges. ../../../concepts/principles.md Interface-first + fakes-mandatory rule. ../../../concepts/architecture.md Bridge protocol (JSON-RPC envelope), handler registration. ../../testing.md Which test tiers apply. An existing API as the template Mirror it. Core: packages/core/src/ (e.g. clipboard.ts, haptics.ts). Android: packages/capsule-android/capsule/src/main/kotlin/dev/capsule/ (handler + provider). iOS: packages/capsule-ios/Sources/dev/capsule/. Demo: examples/react-ts/src/features/.

docs.title: Process (ordered)
docs.text:
1. TS interface → capsule/packages/core/src/<api>.ts — methods call bridge.call('<api>.method', …); include a web fallback. Add error codes to errors.ts if a new range is needed.
  2. Kotlin provider (seam) → …/dev/capsule/<api>/<Api>Provider.kt interface + Android<Api>Provider impl (so it's fakeable).
  3. Kotlin handler → …/dev/capsule/handlers/<api>/…Handler.kt implements BridgeHandler, delegates to the provider.
  4. Register the handler in …/dev/capsule/CapsuleBridge.kt (init block).
  5. Demo screen → examples/react-ts/src/features/<Api>Screen.tsx, wired into the feature-screen registry + ui.tsx. (Never demo in react-ts-native.)
  6. Unit tests → TS in core/src/__tests__/<api>.test.ts; Kotlin in capsule-android/…/src/test/…HandlerTest.kt (provider faked).
  7. AUDIT — run offline tiers (../../commands.md §9): pnpm test + gradlew test must pass. Format gate before any commit.
  8. Rebuild AAR (stale-AAR rule) → gradlew assembleRelease after the Kotlin change.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: core/src/<api>.ts (+ test, + errors.ts), the Kotlin provider + handler (+ test) + bridge registration, the react-ts demo screen, the rebuilt AAR. Update ../../../reference/core-api.md if the public contract changed.

docs.title: Checkpoints (human)
docs.text:
• Device/emulator smoke test → hand to the user (don't run device builds yourself): app loads, the demo screen calls each method, correct result + graceful errors.
  • iOS parity is required by the contract even when implemented later — leave the Swift seam defined so the interface is satisfiable.

docs.title: CONTEXT — author-plugin (stage contract)
docs.text:
Author a third-party SDK-wrapper plugin (community integration), distinct from a core native API: it ships outside @capsule/core and is wired in via capsule.config.ts. Area index: ../CONTEXT.md.

Status: forward contract. The plugin model is specified in plugin-authoring.md, but the capsule plugin check|call|publish CLI tooling is not implemented yet (post-Phase-1). Steps 8+ describe the intended flow; verify the CLI supports them before relying on it.

docs.title: Inputs (load these first)
docs.text: Source Why ../../plugin-authoring.md The authoring guide: file structure, manifest fields, the worked example. ../../../guide/plugins.md Dispatch model, binary vs source mode, language feasibility, what already exists.

docs.title: Process (ordered)
docs.text:
1. Scaffold → capsule-plugins/<name>/ with capsule-plugin.json, android/<Name>.kt, ios/<Name>.swift, web/index.ts.
  2. Manifest → capsule-plugin.json: name, version, platforms, android.{permissions,dependencies,minSdk}, ios.infoPlist, sourceRepo (npm mode). Fields per 031 §"Plugin Manifest".
  3. Android → android/<Name>.kt extends CapsulePlugin(bridge); methods @BridgeMethod, params via call.getString()/…, respond with call.resolve() / call.reject(code,msg).
  4. iOS → ios/<Name>.swift — same CapsulePlugin + @BridgeMethod API.
  5. Web bridge → web/index.ts exports a typed object calling bridge.call('<name>.method', …), JSDoc'd.
  6. Wire in → add to the plugins array in capsule.config.ts ('./capsule-plugins/<name>' source mode, or '@scope/<name>' npm mode).
  7. Sync → capsule sync merges deps into .capsule/android/build.gradle.kts and permissions into the manifest.
  8. AUDIT → capsule plugin check <name> (every @BridgeMethod has a matching web export); capsule plugin call <name> <method> '<json>' exercises it on a running emulator without writing JS.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: capsule-plugins/<name>/{capsule-plugin.json,android,ios,web}; regenerated .capsule/android/ (gradle + manifest). Optional: published npm package when @scope/ + sourceRepo are set (capsule plugin publish).

docs.title: Checkpoints (human)
docs.text:
• capsule plugin check clean and capsule plugin call resolves on the emulator.
  • Device build/test handed to the user: capsule build android produces a valid APK, app loads, plugin callable, no crash.
  • Decide binary vs source distribution up front (030 §"Plugin Dispatch") — it changes packaging.

docs.title: CONTEXT — upkeep-sweep (stage contract)
docs.text: Periodic dependency/tooling audit. The hard part is that versions are pinned in three places that must move in lockstep — miss one and generated projects drift from the AAR. Area index: ../CONTEXT.md.

docs.title: Inputs (load these first)
docs.text: Source Why ../../upkeep.md The whole procedure: three version sources, baseline pins, per-sweep checklist, sweep log, cadence. This workflow is a thin pointer to it. ../../testing.md Tiers to run if a bump is applied.

docs.title: The three version sources (keep in lockstep)
docs.text:
1. Library catalog (the AAR's own build) — capsule/packages/capsule-android/gradle/libs.versions.toml, …/capsule/build.gradle.kts, gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties.
  2. CLI generator (what capsule sync/init emit) — capsule/packages/cli/src/sync/sync.ts, …/commands/init.ts, …/testing.ts. Duplicates #1 as template strings — the #1↔#2 lockstep is the main trap.
  3. Templates (web starters) — templates/*/package.json.

docs.title: Process (ordered)
docs.text:
1. Check latest per 110 §"Per-sweep checklist": QuickJS-ng, CivetWeb (release tags + advisories), Android SDK + Play targetSdk deadline, Gradle/AGP/Kotlin/NDK (as a compatibility unit), CLI/core deps (pnpm outdated, pnpm audit), template framework majors.
  2. Classify each finding: 🟢 current / 🟡 optional / 🔴 security or forced platform requirement.
  3. Log → append a row to the Sweep log in ../../upkeep.md (Date · By · areas · findings · action). Always log, even on a no-action sweep.
  4. (🔴 only) Apply bump → edit source #1, mirror into #2, then #3; rebuild affected packages.
  5. AUDIT → run all test tiers (testing.md); if native/Kotlin/Gradle changed, rebuild the AAR (stale-AAR rule). Commit per-repo, chore(deps):.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: Always: updated Sweep log in ../../upkeep.md. On a bump: the touched files across the three sources above.

docs.title: Checkpoints (human)
docs.text:
• No-action sweep is a valid outcome — the log entry is the deliverable.
  • Bumps that touch native code → hand the device/instrumented test to the user.
  • Cadence (110 §"Cadence"): quarterly, at each phase kickoff, before any release, and immediately on a known CVE or Play enforcement date.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
Binding architecture decisions (ADRs). A decision here is never re-litigated in code comments or other docs — change it by amending the ADR (dated section) or superseding it with a new one.

Decision 000N is the ADR previously cited as adr-00N; both ids name the same record.

Id Decision Status 0001 Embedded runtime — loopback HTTP server + QuickJS route runtime Decided (amended) 0002 Capsule UI — framework-agnostic native-look component layer Proposed (foundation + capsule add-ui built) 0003 On-device AI & agents — tiered ai API Proposed (Tier-1 spike built) 0004 Web-serving transport — CivetWeb on both platforms, http://127.0.0.1 Decided (amended 2026-10-24)

Smaller, earlier decisions are recorded in the decision log.

docs.title: Writing a new decision
docs.text: Copy the shape of an existing ADR: Status · Date · Context · Decision · Alternatives considered · Consequences. Number it 000N-short-title.md, add it to the table above and to mkdocs.yml.

docs.title: ADR-001 — Embedded Runtime Architecture
docs.text: Status: Decided Date: 2026-06-02

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
Capsule currently serves production web assets from file:///android_asset/www/index.html. This has known limitations (no service workers, CORS issues, storage sandboxing). The alternative — WebViewAssetLoader — closes the file:// gap but adds nothing new.

The decision was made to go further: embed a real HTTP server (NanoHTTPD on Android, GCDWebServer on iOS) and a JS runtime (QuickJS) to enable on-device server-side rendering and API routing. This is Capsule's primary differentiator vs Ionic/Capacitor.

Server library superseded (2026-10-24): both platforms now embed CivetWeb instead of NanoHTTPD / GCDWebServer — see the adr-004 amendment. The rest of this ADR is unchanged; NanoHTTPD mentions below are historical.

docs.title: 1. Purpose
docs.text: The embedded server's primary job is dynamic API routing and SSR, not static asset serving. Static serving is a side effect.

docs.title: 2. Route ownership — Model C
docs.text:
• Capsule owns /capsule/* (internal bridge migration, built-in APIs)
  • Developer owns /api/* (custom route handlers)
  • Clear namespace separation, no conflicts

docs.title: 3. Server language — TypeScript + QuickJS
docs.text: Developer writes TypeScript route handlers. Same language as the client. Same @capsule/core package works in both contexts. QuickJS (ES2020, ~700KB) evaluates the server bundle on-device. Node.js evaluates it in dev mode. No Kotlin/Swift route handler code required from developers.

docs.title: 4. Bridge stays for events — HTTP is data only
docs.text:
HTTP (NanoHTTPD/GCDWebServer)  →  request / response  →  data, mutations, SSR
Bridge (JavascriptInterface)    →  push / events        →  native APIs, real-time
No WebSockets, no SSE, no full web server features. Deliberately minimal.

Amended by adr-004 (2026-06-26). HTTP fidelity is now tiered, not minimal-forever: static + request/response + streaming are in scope now; WebSockets and SSE are deferred-by-design future features (they need a new core route model), not permanently excluded. The Bridge-vs-HTTP channel split above still holds — WS/SSE would be web-standard real-time inside the on-device server (for "any web app just works" fidelity), distinct from the native-event Bridge.

docs.title: 5. QuickJSBridge implements Bridge interface
docs.text:
@capsule/core is universal: same package, same API, three contexts: - CapsuleBridge — WebView + native shell - WebBridge — browser dev - FakeBridge — unit tests - QuickJSBridge — server handlers (new)

Server handler code is identical to client code for all @capsule/core calls.

docs.title: 6. Server readiness — Splash + timeout
docs.text:
• Splash shows immediately on launch
  • CapsuleRuntime.start() binds NanoHTTPD + evaluates QuickJS bundle
  • On ready → navigate WebView to http://127.0.0.1:{port}/
  • On timeout (3s default) → error screen with retry button
  • On crash loop (3 failures / 60s) → auto-rollback via codeSync

Amended 2026-10-15 (bind race, 2026-10-embedded-server-startup.md). Contract made explicit: CapsuleServer.start() returns only when the server accepts connections. NanoHTTPD 2.3.1's start() returns before bind() (verified in the bytecode), which let the WebView race the bind (ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED on fast devices) and made the 3s bind timeout dead code. Enforcement = readiness probe + bind retry in NanoHttpdServer (SR-1..SR-5 in the linked doc). Enforcement superseded 2026-10-24 (the contract stands): CivetWeb's mg_start2 returns only after the bind, so the probe and retry were removed — see the Resolution section of the linked doc.

docs.title: 7. Port — deterministic hash from appId
docs.text: Port derived from appId hash, range 49152–65535. Invisible to developer. No configuration. Amended 2026-10-24: computed at runtime from the app's own package name / bundle identifier (CapsuleShellConfig.appId defaults to it), not baked in by capsule sync — the generated MainActivity never passed it, so every app used the shared default and the second Capsule app on a device found its port taken.

docs.title: 8. Dev mode — Node.js runs server bundle
docs.text:
capsule dev starts two processes: 1. Vite/ng dev server (client code, hot reload) 2. Node.js process (server bundle, same TypeScript, watches src/server/routes/)

adb reverse forwards both ports to device. Browser and device both work. Developer uses one capsule dev android command — two processes are invisible.

docs.title: 9. File-based routing
docs.text:
src/
  server/
    routes/
      users.ts          → GET /api/users, POST /api/users
      users/
        [id].ts         → GET /api/users/:id
Exports GET, POST, PUT, DELETE functions. CLI scans at build time. Adding a file creates a route. No registration, no config.

docs.title: 10. Server is optional
docs.text: src/server/routes/ presence activates full stack. Absent → NanoHTTPD serves static assets only, QuickJS never starts. Developer opts in by creating a file.

docs.title: 11. Two bundles, one atomic deploy
docs.text:
capsule build android
  → vite/ng build  →  assets/www/          (client)
  → esbuild        →  assets/server/        (server bundle.js)
Always both, always together. Developer sees one build, one deploy, one version. codeSync deploys atomically. No independent channel configuration.

docs.title: 12. Developer visibility — zero
docs.text: The embedded server is invisible infrastructure. Developer writes a web app. Port, bundles, QuickJS, NanoHTTPD — none of this appears in docs, CLI output, or capsule.config.ts. Crash + rollback is silent recovery.

docs.title: 13. CapsuleRuntime coordinator
docs.text:
class CapsuleRuntime(
    val bridge: CapsuleBridge,
    val server: CapsuleServer,       // interface → NanoHTTPD (Android) / GCDWebServer (iOS)
    val jsRuntime: QuickJSEngine,    // interface → QuickJS JNI (both platforms)
    val splash: SplashController,    // interface → WebView splash impl
    val codeSync: CodeSyncManager,   // interface → rollback on crash loop
)
CapsuleActivity becomes a thin shell. All lifecycle, readiness, and crash handling owned by CapsuleRuntime.

docs.title: 14. Interfaces + fakes — mandatory pattern
docs.text:
Every new component ships with an interface and a fake on the same day: - CapsuleServer + FakeCapsuleServer (neverStarts, startsAfter, crashesAfter) - QuickJSEngine + FakeQuickJSEngine (evaluationFails, slowStart, callReturns) - SplashController + FakeSplashController

All CapsuleRuntime behavior covered by pure JVM unit tests, no device needed.

docs.title: Android (Phase 2)
docs.text:
Step 1 — Interfaces + fakes CapsuleServer, QuickJSEngine, SplashController interfaces. All three fakes. CapsuleRuntime wired with fakes. Full unit test suite: server not ready, timeout, crash loop, successful start.

Step 2 — NanoHTTPD for static assets NanoHttpdServer implements CapsuleServer. Replaces file:///android_asset/www/index.html with http://127.0.0.1:{port}/. No QuickJS yet. Verifiable immediately on device.

Step 3 — Splash + readiness WebViewSplashController. CapsuleRuntime.start() shows splash, waits for NanoHTTPD bind, navigates. Timeout + error screen. Tested with FakeCapsuleServer.neverStarts().

Step 4 — QuickJS JNI embedding QuickJS C library in AAR via JNI. QuickJSEngine.evaluate(bundle) and call(fn, args). Prove JS evaluation works. No routes yet.

Step 5 — QuickJSBridge Bridge interface implementation backed by JNI → Kotlin providers. @capsule/core runs inside QuickJS. Every existing bridge method tested from QuickJS context.

Step 6 — Route handling + CLI build step NanoHTTPD /api/* → QuickJSEngine.call("handleRequest", ...) → response. CLI build adds esbuild server bundle step. CLI dev adds Node.js server process + second adb reverse port.

Step 7 — codeSync crash loop + rollback Atomic bundle zip: www/ + server/bundle.js. 3 crashes in 60s → rollback to previous zip. Tested with FakeCapsuleServer.crashesAfterRequests(1).

docs.title: iOS (Phase 4)
docs.text:
CapsuleRuntime untouched. Swap: - NanoHttpdServer → GCDWebServerImpl implements CapsuleServer - QuickJSEngine JNI → QuickJS compiled for iOS (same C source) - SplashController → WKWebViewSplashController

Zero developer-facing changes. Same capsule.config.ts, same TypeScript route handlers, same CLI commands.

docs.title: What stays unchanged
docs.text:
• Existing JSON-RPC bridge and all 6 native API handlers
  • @capsule/core public API — modules, types, exports
  • capsule.config.ts schema (minor additions only: server.timeout)
  • All existing templates and examples
  • Dev flow: capsule dev android still starts everything

docs.title: ADR-002 — Capsule UI (native-look component layer)
docs.text: Status: Proposed / Future (target Phase 5 — native-look component layer, slotted right after iOS so its iOS/Material presets target a real WKWebView shell; per the canonical roadmap). Not started. Date: 2026-06-12

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
Capsule provides a native runtime + bridge + tooling layer but no UI layer. The hand-written CSS in the starter templates looks "web," not like a native app button (iOS/Material). Developers either hand-roll native styling or pull in a third-party kit.

The two competing kits in this space are tied to the Framework7 ecosystem: - Framework7 — full mobile UI + router; packages natively via Capacitor/Cordova (which is what Capsule competes with at the runtime layer). - Konsta UI — F7's Tailwind-based component library (iOS/Material), React/Vue/Svelte only.

We want a native look without building our identity on a competitor-adjacent dependency, and it must work across all 7 supported frameworks (React, Vue, Svelte, Angular, vanilla JS, vanilla TS, jQuery) — Capsule's framework-agnostic promise.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Build Capsule UI as our own native-look component layer, on these principles:

  1. Tailwind + a custom iOS/Material preset authored by us — the styling foundation. Native button/list/tab/sheet shapes we design, not a borrowed web aesthetic.
  2. Framework-agnostic CSS classes first — components are Tailwind classes (or a daisyUI-style semantic layer) that work in every framework. Per-framework headless behavior (Radix for React, Reka for Vue, Bits for Svelte, Angular CDK) only where complex interaction needs it.
  3. shadcn-style distribution — capsule add ui <component> copies source the developer owns into their project (no runtime dependency), via the same registry/manifest machinery built for templates. This is the on-brand, high-value part.

daisyUI is the structural model to borrow (or literally build on): pure-CSS, framework-agnostic, themeable — exactly our constraints. We add the native shapes + minimal behavior it lacks.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text: Option Native look All frameworks Why not (as the base) Konsta UI (dependency) ★★★ React/Vue/Svelte only Not agnostic; competitor-adjacent. Good interim recommendation for the 3 it supports. shadcn / Radix base ✗ desktop-web React-mostly React-bound; desktop aesthetic; no mobile primitives. Borrow its delivery model, not its components. daisyUI ✗ web (themeable) ✅ pure CSS Best-aligned model; ship native theme on top. Flowbite / Preline ✗ dashboard mixed + JS dep Web aesthetic + runtime JS plugin + uneven multi-framework. Bulma / Bootstrap ✗ web ✅ classes Web look (the original problem). Ionic ★★★ (Angular/React/Vue) Different stack (web components), heavy, reshapes the app.

docs.title: Phasing
docs.text:
• Now (separate, shipped first): optional --css tailwind flag + a shared native preset (iOS/Material classes mapped onto the existing .btn/.card/.tab names) so every template looks native immediately, no per-template rewrite. Recommend Konsta as a documented interim for React/Vue/Svelte.
  • Phase 5 (this ADR): the capsule add ui registry + shared iOS/Material Tailwind preset + per-framework behavior. Capsule's own "Konsta," independent of F7's ecosystem. Placed after iOS (Phase 4) so the iOS preset can be validated against a real WKWebView shell, before the OTA cloud.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A real, multi-week initiative (effectively a component framework + registry). Deferred until the runtime is hardened (Step 7) and core testing is complete.
  • Reuses the template manifest/registry infra → lower incremental cost than starting from scratch.

docs.title: ADR-003 — On-device AI & Agents
docs.text: Status: Proposed / Future. Capability spike fits late Phase 3; the agent layer + hosted inference pairs with Phase 6 (OTA cloud). Not started. Date: 2026-06-22 Supersedes/relates: Q16 monolithic core · adr-001 embedded runtime · Business model

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Every mobile-app platform is being asked for AI. We evaluated whether Capsule should expose an AI capability and, beyond that, an agent capability (LLM + tools + loop). Two findings from the 2026-06 landscape scan shaped the decision.

docs.title: What competitors have done
docs.text:
• Ionic/Capacitor already shipped capacitor-local-llm (Capacitor Labs / experimental): a unified TS API for on-device text/image generation + sessions. Crucially it wraps the OS-native models (Apple Foundation Models, Android Gemini Nano/AICore) — it does not bundle its own runtime. They openly state "the first-party on-device AI story is still in flux, especially on Android." A community plugin (@capgo/capacitor-llm) adds Apple Intelligence + MLX.
  • Framework7 — no AI story. It is a UI kit.

So a flag is planted, but it's thin (a shim over whatever the OS ships) and experimental. Nobody has shipped the "bundle-your-own portable model + agent tools + OTA-updatable agent logic" approach on a web-native shell — which is exactly the seam Capsule's architecture already occupies.

docs.title: The device-coverage cliff (the fact that reframes everything)
docs.text:
The OS-native path only works on premium, recent flagships: - Apple Foundation Models require Apple Intelligence: iPhone 15 Pro+ / 16+, M1+ iPad/Mac. Every base 15/14/13, every SE — excluded. - Gemini Nano / AICore: Pixel 8+, Galaxy S24+; Gemini Nano 4 (late 2026) wants 12 GB RAM, flagship-only.

Conclusion: "wrap the OS model" (what Ionic shipped) is a demo/checkbox, not a real capability — and it is worst for the mass-market / emerging-market apps that Capsule's agency ICP tends to build. Universal coverage requires bundling a small model (a portable C/C++ inference engine) or cloud. That pushes the real product toward a hybrid — which is precisely where Phase-5 OTA cloud lives.

docs.title: The runtime engine ("the QuickJS of LLMs")
docs.text:
Same kind of decision we made for the JS engine — pick a portable C/C++ core we embed via JNI:

Engine What it is Fit llama.cpp Foundational C/C++ lib, GGUF single-file models, maximally portable, CPU-first Closest in spirit to QuickJS; we'd build all mobile glue ourselves. The safe escape hatch. ExecuTorch (Meta) 1.0 GA Oct 2025, 50 KB runtime, 12+ HW backends, runs in WhatsApp/IG at scale Heaviest integration (PyTorch toolchain); the "big production" option. MLC-LLM Compiles models to native via Apache TVM, GPU (Vulkan/Metal) Best raw perf on specific targets; complex build. 🌵 Cactus C API + C++ ARM-SIMD kernels, native Kotlin + Swift bindings, cloud fallback built in, sub-50 ms TTFT, open source Strongest architectural match — embeds like our QuickJS-ng JNI work, cross-platform from one core (iOS parity), cloud-fallback dovetails with Phase-5. Risks: young YC startup, v1 moved to a proprietary .cact format, license unconfirmed.

docs.title: Decision (proposed)
docs.text: Adopt AI as a first-class core capability following the existing interface → provider → Fake → handler → @capsule/core pattern (consistent with Q16: an OS API → @capsule/core), structured in two tiers plus an agent layer:

docs.title: 1. The ai core API — tiered inference, one TS surface
docs.text:
A single ai singleton in @capsule/core with a provider behind it, exactly like geolocation/camera:

import { ai } from '@capsule/core'

// Text generation — provider chosen by config/availability
const reply = await ai.generate({ prompt: 'Summarise this note', maxTokens: 256 })
for await (const tok of ai.stream({ prompt })) { /* streaming */ }
const ready = await ai.availability()  // 'os-native' | 'bundled' | 'cloud' | 'unavailable'

Three provider tiers behind that surface, chosen by availability + capsule.config.ts:

Tier Provider Coverage When Tier 1 — OS-native Apple Foundation Models / Gemini Nano via AICore Flagships only (see cliff) Cheap "we have AI" checkbox; ships fast; zero model bundling. Matches Ionic feature-for-feature. Tier 2 — Bundled Cactus (primary) / llama.cpp (escape hatch); a quantised model fetched outside the OTA bundle dirs Universal The real on-device capability; offline + private. Tier 3 — Cloud Capsule OTA cloud → Claude/other; or Cactus cloud-fallback by confidence Universal Reasoning-heavy work; the billing meter.

Default = hybrid: use on-device when available/sufficient, fall back to cloud otherwise.

docs.title: 2. The agent layer — native bridge as the tool surface
docs.text:
An agent is LLM + tools + loop. Capsule's hard parts already exist: - The JSON-RPC native bridge (camera, filesystem, geolocation, notifications, db, …) is the tool palette. Every Phase-3 API is one more agent tool for free. This reframes Phase 3 — we're not just adding device features, we're building the agent's hands. - The QuickJS server runtime is the natural home for the agent loop + tool dispatch (it's JSON + bridge calls — exactly what QuickJS is good at). Inference itself never runs in QuickJS — it is a bridge call to the native/cloud provider. This split is clean and already supported by adr-001. - Server Code Push (Phase 6) makes agent definitions — system prompt, tool registry, routing — hot-patchable over the air, because they live in src/server/routes. "Update your app's AI agent behavior without an app-store release" is a story Ionic structurally cannot tell. This is the moat.

// src/server/routes/agent.ts (runs in QuickJS; OTA-updatable)
import { defineAgent, tools } from '@capsule/core/agent'

export default defineAgent({
  model: 'hybrid',
  system: 'You are the in-app assistant.',
  tools: [tools.camera.capturePhoto, tools.filesystem.readFile, tools.geolocation.current],
})

We do NOT build LangChain. The agent loop/abstraction is a commodity (Vercel AI SDK et al.). Our value is tools = native capabilities + OTA-updatable + cross-platform. Keep the loop thin; let an existing model SDK drive it. Strongly consider speaking MCP so the tool surface is a standard any model can drive — "your phone's capabilities as MCP tools" is a clean, ownable framing.

docs.title: 3. Cross-cutting constraints (inherit Phase-3 OTA rules)
docs.text:
• Models persist outside the OTA-swappable bundle dirs (www/ + server/bundle.js) — a bundle swap must never wipe a multi-GB model download (same rule camera/filesystem already follow).
  • Native-capability version gating — the ai capability carries a version so the Phase-5 OTA server can refuse to push agent JS that calls an ai/tool feature the installed shell predates.
  • Tool-permission model — an agent with programmatic access to camera/files/location/contacts is a security surface. Per-tool grants + user confirmation for sensitive actions, designed in from day one, not bolted on. Reuses the existing PermissionManager.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text: Option Why not (as the strategy) OS-native only (Ionic's path) The device-coverage cliff makes it a checkbox, not a capability. Adopt it as Tier 1 only. Cloud only No offline/private story; nothing differentiated vs. calling an API from any web app. Keep as Tier 3. Bundle a big model for everyone App-size + RAM cost punishes low-end devices; not all apps want AI. Must be opt-in + tree-shaken (Q16). Build a full agent framework (LangChain-style) Commodity surface; high maintenance; not the moat. Build the thin tool-registry instead. Ship now, before iOS The differentiator (Cactus cross-platform, OTA-updatable agents) only fully lands once iOS parity + OTA cloud exist. Spike the API now; land the agent layer with Phase 6.

docs.title: Phasing (the plan)
docs.text:
Phase 3 (now-ish) — ai capability spike (Tier 1 + interface). Cheap, proves the pattern. 1. AiProvider interface + FakeAiProvider (scripted completions / tool-calls) — day one, per R14. 2. ai singleton in @capsule/core + AiHandler (bridge method) + WebBridge fallback (browser dev → cloud or echo). 3. Tier-1 Android provider over Gemini Nano / AICore; ai.availability() returns the honest tier. 4. Capability-version field; docs note the device-coverage cliff loudly.

Phase 4 — iOS parity. Tier-1 iOS provider over Apple Foundation Models (mirrors Android).

Phase 6 — the real product (paired with OTA cloud). 5. Tier 2 — embed Cactus (or llama.cpp) via JNI/Swift; model download → outside bundle dirs; resume/verify. 6.
