docs.title: Session 2026-06-16 — Phase 3 #1: Filesystem API (Android)
docs.text:
Shipped the Filesystem native API (capsule 083b2cf, examples 18103d8) — the foundational Phase-3 capability, built with the proven interface + provider + Fake pattern across all three layers:

  • @capsule/core — FilesystemModule: readFile / writeFile / appendFile / deleteFile / mkdir / rmdir / readdir / stat / getUri / downloadFile; FilesystemDirectory (data/cache/documents), FileEncoding (utf8/base64), FileEntry/FileStat; FilesystemMethods shared with WebBridge. New error codes 5xxx: FILE_NOT_FOUND / FILE_IO_ERROR / PATH_NOT_ALLOWED.
  • WebBridge dev fallback — localStorage-backed FS keyed by (directory, path), base64-canonical storage with unicode-safe utf8⇄base64, implicit-directory readdir, traversal guard. Methods are async so the synchronous traversal check rejects (per the Bridge.call promise contract) rather than throwing.
  • capsule-android — FilesystemProvider (iOS seam) + AndroidFilesystemProvider over java.io.File, all I/O on Dispatchers.IO, canonical-path traversal guard, downloadFile via HttpURLConnection; filesystemHandlers(...) wired into CapsuleActivity.
  • @capsule/cli — sync.ts now auto-declares INTERNET (normal permission, no dialog) for downloadFile.
  • react-ts example — new Filesystem playground tab (directory toggle + write/append/read/stat/ delete + mkdir/readdir + download).

OTA-safety constraint (a) honored concretely: roots are filesDir/capsule/fs/{data,documents} and cacheDir/capsule/fs/cache, deliberately not under filesDir/bundles (the OTA swap target) — an instrumented test (rootsLiveOutsideTheOtaBundleDir) asserts the invariant. Constraint (b) native-capability version: deferred by design — no consumer until the Phase-5 OTA server exists; building the gate now would be speculative. Land it alongside Phase 5.

Full test sweep — all green (2026-06-16): TS unit 91 (@capsule/core; +12 filesystem module, +9 web-bridge fs) · Kotlin JVM unit 85 (+14 FilesystemHandlerTest; testReleaseUnitTest BUILD SUCCESSFUL) · Android instrumented 23 (+10 AndroidFilesystemProviderTest — real encoding round-trips, traversal guard, directory isolation, OTA-safety) on CapsuleTest emulator (API 35) · react-ts example tsc --noEmit clean · release AAR rebuilt clean.

Review + refactor (same day, capsule f99315b): re-read the Filesystem implementation for smells. Three fixed: 1. getUri contract violation — resolve() did root().apply { mkdirs() }, so the documented "pure, no I/O" getUri (and reads/stat) created the root dir as a side effect. Now resolve() is pure; roots are created lazily only by the write paths (prepareParent/mkdir). 2. Repeated try/catch → FileIoError across 4 provider methods → extracted a single io { } helper (runs on Dispatchers.IO, passes CapsuleException through, maps anything else to FileIoError). Also fixed a case where decode()'s specific error got re-wrapped/lost. 3. Cross-file param-parsing duplication (camera + filesystem each had private string/bool/contentOrNullSafe) → new shared handlers/JsonParams.kt (optString/optInt/optDouble/optBool); both handler sets migrated. Sets the convention for every future API's param parsing. No behavior change intended — verification pending the user's full test run before commit.

Overall health — good. Phase 3 on track (Camera + Filesystem done, tested release + dev + browser); pattern consistency holding (interface + provider + Fake + DTO); test pyramid healthy. No architectural debt surfaced beyond the three smells above.

Design note — Share / "save to user-visible location" (discussed, not built): share is a native OS feature everywhere (Android ACTION_SEND share sheet, iOS UIActivityViewController, Web Share API) — Capsule just bridges it; reuses the camera FileProvider. It's the truly cross-platform primitive for "give the user this file," because iOS has no public Downloads folder (its share sheet covers Save to Files/Photos). A saveToDownloads is therefore an Android/web specialization (Android MediaStore.Downloads, web Save-As), not a core API. filesystem.downloadFile is correctly app-private (verified: browser stores under __capsule_fs__:* in localStorage; device under filesDir). Share stays at roadmap Phase 3 #7 unless pulled forward.

Next: Phase 3 #2 — App lifecycle + deep links (fg/bg events + incoming URLs/universal links; infrastructure that push tap-routing and OTA foreground re-checks both depend on). Share (#7) can be pulled forward on request — it's self-contained and low-risk.

docs.title: Session 2026-06-15 — Group 2 browser-dev + Phase 2 Step 7 (CodeSync crash-loop)
docs.text:
Group 2 (non-Vite transparent proxy) browser-dev — all 3 PASS (verified with headless Chromium, not just curl): - webpack-preact (proxy :5184), rspack-lit (:5186, Shadow DOM), rollup-solid (:5185, CAPSULE_INTERNAL_PORT→:5186). App renders, /__capsule.js injected, window.fetch patched, /api/ping + hello RPC resolve through the sidecar, 0 console/page errors. Results logged in docs/TEST_PLAN.md (Group 2 results log). - Real proxy bug found + fixed in cli/src/dev-proxy-server.ts (forwardInjectHtml): the non-Vite proxy buffered HTML to inject the Capsule script assuming uncompressed bytes. Browsers/WebView send Accept-Encoding: gzip; webpack-dev-server (default compress: true) gzipped the HTML → proxy injected into gzip garbage, stripped content-encoding, forwarded compressed bytes as text/html → garbled page, no injection. curl masked it by not requesting compression. Fix: strip accept-encoding before forwarding so the bundler returns injectable plaintext. Would have broken all non-Vite examples under capsule dev on device, not just in-browser. CLI rebuilt. - Corrected Group 2 ports in TEST_PLAN.md (were 5182/5183/5185; actual 5184/5186/5185 — same drift as Group 0). Noted the 5185/5186 overlaps (harmless — run one at a time). - HMR-through-proxy: WebSocket upgrade forwarding works for all 3. webpack/rspack do live-reload (no prefresh/lit-hot boundary configured in the examples); rollup has no rollup-plugin-livereload (rebuild-on-save only). Marked ⚠️ in the matrix — example config, not a proxy gap.

Phase 2 Step 7 — CodeSync crash-loop + rollback ✅ (on-device mechanism; OTA network delivery still Phase 4): - New runtime classes (interface-first, all pure-JVM testable): Clock/SystemClock, CrashLog + PrefsCrashLog (SharedPreferences, survives process death), CrashLoopGuard ("3 crashes in 60s", injectable clock+log), BundleStore + FileBundleStore (two-slot active/previous, atomic dir swap, validates www/index.html, server/bundle.js carried alongside). - CapsuleRuntime: rolls back to previous known-good bundle on start() when crash-looping (+ onRollback() hook), records each launch attempt, notifyAppReady() confirms a healthy boot and clears the counter. Wired into CapsuleActivity prod path (PrefsCrashLog + FileBundleStore(filesDir/bundles)); CapsuleWebViewClient.onPageFinished → notifyAppReady(). - 25 new pure-JVM tests + fakes (FakeClock/FakeCrashLog/FakeBundleStore): CrashLoopGuard 9 · FileBundleStore 10 · CapsuleRuntime rollback 6, incl. the spec's FakeCapsuleServer.CrashesAfter(0) "three crashes → fourth launch rolls back" path. Full JVM suite 71 green; release AAR rebuilt clean. - Design note: a crash loop is only confirmable on the next boot (the crash kills the process), so rollback fires on the launch after the 3rd recorded crash — matching CodePush/Expo semantics.

Senior-architect review + pre-commit verification (2026-06-15): - Patterns: Step 7 follows the existing interface + impl + fake convention (Clock/SystemClock, CrashLog/PrefsCrashLog/FakeCrashLog, BundleStore/FileBundleStore/FakeBundleStore) and CapsuleRuntime's Orchestrator + Template-Method shape (onRollback() added next to onStartTimeout()). No pre-existing clock/currentTimeMillis usage in main — the abstraction is introduced cleanly. - Refactor applied: FileBundleStore now leans on Kotlin stdlib File.copyRecursively/deleteRecursively and drops redundant explicit deletes (move() already clears its destination), removing two hand-rolled helpers. docs.title: Phase — Testing (2026-06-11 session)
docs.text:
This session: - Fixed FakeQuickJSBridge — was missing handleHttpRequest (added in Step 6 interface), broke gradlew test. Now implemented (records calls in httpRequests, returns settable httpResult). gradlew test green. - Full test pyramid verified: TS unit (60) ✅ · Kotlin JVM unit ✅ · Android instrumented (13: QuickJSEngineImpl 4 + QuickJSBridge 4 + QuickJSBridgeHttp 5) ✅ on emulator. - Added examples/scripts/ — emulator.ps1 <start|stop|status> (software GPU default to avoid Intel-UHD boot hang, detached + log-redirected, -Fresh/-NoWait/-Headless/-Gpu flags) + env.ps1 + README. - Group 0.1 react-from-template browser-dev ✅ PASS (all 8 checks). Server on devPort 5190 (sidecar 6190). - Group 0.1 emulator-dev ✅ PASS — surfaced + fixed a real architectural gap (below). - Fixed wrong devPort values in docs/TEST_PLAN.md + examples/README.md for 6 of 7 from-template examples (real ports: react 5190, vue 5175, svelte 5176, angular 5177, vanilla-js 5182, vanilla-ts 5174, jquery 5183). - Tab-state decision: results persist across tab switches by design (state lifted to App). Removed the wrong "state resets" check. Added a Clear button to react-from-template Server tab only.

Code fixes this session (in capsule-android + cli): - Dev-mode JSON-RPC routes on-device — bridge.call('hello') returned METHOD_NOT_FOUND under capsule dev android. Root cause: @capsule/core uses the native bridge whenever __capsule_host is injected (always on Android), but in dev mode CapsuleActivity.loadApp() returns early and never attaches QuickJS, so custom src/routes/*.ts had no handler. Fix: CapsuleBridge.postMessage now forwards unmatched methods, in dev mode, to the dev sidecar (POST ${devServerUrl}/_capsule/rpc via adb reverse) and relays the response. Built-in native APIs still resolve via Kotlin handlers first. Added TAG/Log.d diagnostics on the forward path. Verified working on emulator. - dev.ts Vite watcher — added server.watch.ignored: ['**/.capsule/**','**/dist/**','**/.gradle/**'] so capsule dev and capsule build android run concurrently. Previously the Vite watcher held handles in .capsule/android/.gradle, breaking Gradle's atomic rename on Windows ("Could not move temporary workspace to immutable location"). CLI rebuilt.

Workflow rule settled: always use the release AAR (isMinifyEnabled=false, no log stripping, identical behavior; app build-type decides dev/embedded, not the AAR). The recurring trap is a stale AAR — always gradlew assembleRelease after any Kotlin change before build android, and confirm the override line + AAR timestamp. See env_checklist memory.

Emulator: Intel UHD GPU hangs host-GPU boot (boot_completed never flips) → examples/scripts/emulator.ps1 now defaults to -gpu swiftshader_indirect.

Repo + templates (2026-06-12): - Repo layout settled: capsule / examples / docs / templates are separate git repos (not a monorepo); templates kept separate due to higher churn. templates/ git init'd + committed. All four committed this session. - Template extensibility implemented in init.ts: single templates-repo model with templates/manifest.json (no CLI release to add a template); --template now accepts official names or any source (gh:owner/repo[/subdir][#ref], tarball URL, local path); won't clobber a custom template's capsule.config.ts. TEMPLATES_REPO/TEMPLATES_BRANCH constants to confirm at GitHub-publish time. - Deferred to publish: confirm published templates-repo org/name; company-registry config (~/.capsulerc); "Authoring a template" doc + template contract.

Design decisions (2026-06-12) — recorded in Build/000-Roadmap.md "Design decisions" + Architecture/adr-002-capsule-ui.md: - Compatibility: frontend framework runs in the WebView (any framework/version OK); QuickJS only runs server routes — the real surface. Freeze the contract (bridge protocol + @capsule/core API + pinned QuickJS), not the framework. capsule.lock pins the shell; CI should build templates + run route bundles in QuickJS. - CLI updates: prefer project-local devDep (pinned); update-notifier, no silent auto-update; capsule upgrade + doctor report versions. - Existing-project adoption: CLI-assisted (capsule init in-place / integrate) — detect bundler, gen config + add core + add android; dev/build already wrap any bundler. - Capsule UI (future, Phase 5): Tailwind + own iOS/Material preset + shadcn-style capsule add ui registry; daisyUI as structural model; Konsta as interim for React/Vue/Svelte. See adr-002.

Immediate next: ship optional --css tailwind (shared native preset reusing existing .btn/.card/.tab class names; default --css none), then regenerate the 7 from-template examples. Then Group 1/2 + device-release, then Step 7.

User chose example-only for now.

docs.title: Browser QuickJS testing — open question
docs.text:
Q: The developer can change Vite to another bundler. Will Option B (Vitest/Jest in Node.js) still work?

Yes — completely. Vitest tests @capsule/core source directly using its own internal bundler (esbuild). The app's bundler (Vite, Webpack, Rollup, Parcel, esbuild…) is irrelevant. Changing the app bundler has zero effect on the test suite. The 36 TS tests and any future Vitest tests will keep working regardless.

The only thing that changes between bundlers is the shape of assets/www/index.js (the app bundle). That is tested end-to-end on device, not by Vitest.

Three browser testing options:

  • A — quickjs-emscripten: run the same C engine as WASM in Node.js — highest fidelity, tests that bundles actually execute in QuickJS before hitting the device
  • B — Vitest + happy-dom ✅ DONE: test WebBridge (browser fallback) in a browser-like environment — bundler-agnostic, no device needed
  • C — Chrome DevTools on WebView: chrome://inspect → connect to device WebView → run bridge calls in devtools console

  3. Added packages/core/src/__tests__/web-bridge.test.ts (@vitest-environment happy-dom) — 12 new tests

Key note on vi.spyOn: happy-dom implements navigator.clipboard.readText() (returns ''). The "clipboard unavailable" tests use vi.spyOn(navigator, 'clipboard', 'get').mockReturnValue(undefined) to simulate a browser with no clipboard API, then vi.restoreAllMocks() in afterEach.

docs.text: Two sub-tasks (both deliver independent value, built together):

docs.title: Sub-task A — JSON-RPC file discovery
docs.text: User creates src/routes/device.getInfo.ts, CLI bundles it, QuickJS intercepts that method before Kotlin. - File: src/routes/<method>.ts (method name = filename without extension) - Handler: export default function handler(params) { return {...} } - CLI auto-discovers files and generates addRoute("method.name", handler) calls - No registration needed — file presence = route registration

docs.title: Sub-task B — HTTP API routing
docs.text: User creates src/server/routes/users.ts, NanoHTTPD routes /api/users to QuickJS. - File: src/server/routes/<name>.ts (path = /api/<name>) - Handler exports: export function GET(req: CapsuleHttpRequest) { return { status: 200, body: '...' } } - NanoHTTPD intercepts /api/* and calls QuickJSEngine.call("handleHttpRequest", ...) - @capsule/core/routes exports CapsuleHttpRequest, CapsuleHttpResponse, addHttpRoute, handleHttpRequest - Framework-agnostic: completely independent of Angular/React/Vue client routing

docs.title: 2026-06-15 — Strategy session (business model + iOS sequencing + migration)
docs.text:
No code changes; this session set product/business direction and reorganized the roadmap. New docs:

  • docs/Architecture/ionic-framework7-migration.md — Ionic/F7 UI migrates ~free (they're web UI libs; Capsule serves any bundle); the work is native plugins → importer + a @capsule/compat-capacitor shim (alias @capacitor/*, zero app-code change for Level-1 plugins). Worth it as a GTM on-ramp, never a runtime compat layer. Table-stakes: App/Keyboard/StatusBar bridge equivalents.
  • docs/Business/000-Business-Model.md — open-core SaaS. Framework free/OSS + self-hostable server (defuses the CodePush "unlimited free bandwidth" death). Market timing: App Center retired Mar-2025 / CodePush dead / Appflow expensive. ICP: agencies first, freelancers as the free-tier funnel. Meter on MAU + bandwidth, not deploy count. Flagship paid = canary + auto-rollback (monetizes the Step-7 crash-loop guard) + multi-tenant. MCP = distribution channel (mostly free), AI app-builder = deferred scope creep. Store story = codesync publish (OTA, no review) + publish (automated submission); headline "most updates never touch the store."
  • docs/Business/010-Pricing.md — tiers (Community self-host / Free 1k MAU / Pro ~$49 / Team ~$199 / Business ~$499 / Enterprise custom); MoR payments (Paddle/Lemon Squeezy first for VAT, Stripe at scale); 14-day Team trial, free tier forever, annual ~17% off. Numbers illustrative — validate.
  • docs/Business/020-OTA-Policy-and-Liability.md — customer owns store compliance (tool-vendor posture; CodePush/Expo/Appflow precedent). Shield with ToS/AUP + non-evasion marketing. Build the deterministic capability gate (minNativeVersion/permissions/native → force publish); semantic "primary purpose" check = best-effort warn + acknowledgment + audit log. Watch the QuickJS-vs- JavaScriptCore clause (Hermes/CodePush precedent says tolerated).
  • docs/Build/080-iOS-BringUp.md — iOS pulled ahead (was Phase 6 → Phase 4; after native APIs, before the OTA cloud which needs cross-platform). No Mac purchase yet: Simulator covers unit+integration tiers; GitHub Actions macOS works on private repos (10× metered) and is free when public — matches "go public at launch." Recent-macOS VM only as throwaway interactive scratchpad (EULA-gray); Lion is useless. Interface-first Swift/QuickJS port mirrors the Android runtime classes.
  • docs/Build/090-Infrastructure.md — bandwidth is the OTA margin driver; AWS/Azure egress ~$0.08/GB vs Hetzner ~€1/TB vs R2 $0 egress. Data plane on R2/Hetzner+CDN, control plane on Hetzner k8s; AWS/Azure reserved for enterprise data-residency/on-prem (billed). Differential updates cut bandwidth.

Roadmap (docs/Build/000-Roadmap.md) re-sequenced (revised — capability first): Phase 3 native APIs → Phase 4 iOS → Phase 5 OTA cloud → Phase 6 migration on-ramp → Phase 7 ecosystem → Phase 8 DX. Much of the Server Code Push technical design already existed (docs/Server/*, 050-Publishing.md); this session added the strategy/business layer and the sequencing, not new technical specs.

docs.title: Infrastructure & Hosting Economics (Server Code Push)
docs.text: Where to run the Capsule Cloud, and why bandwidth — not compute — is the decision that makes or breaks OTA margins. Decided in the 2026-06-15 strategy session. The application stack (API, dashboard, Postgres, Redis, MinIO/S3, workers) is specified in ../Server/; this doc is about deployment targets and cost.

docs.title: The one fact that dominates everything
docs.text:
OTA = shipping bundles to thousands of devices. Bandwidth is the dominant variable cost. And cloud egress is where AWS/Azure quietly destroy OTA margins:

Provider Egress (approx) AWS / Azure ~$0.08–0.09 / GB Hetzner ~€1 / TB (≈ $0.001/GB) + generous included traffic Cloudflare R2 $0 egress (S3-compatible)

That's a ~100× difference on the exact operation the product does most. Do not serve OTA bundles from AWS/Azure egress unless a customer is paying a premium that covers it.

docs.title: Split the planes
docs.text:
Plane What runs Where Why Data plane (bandwidth-heavy) Bundle storage + delivery (the actual OTA downloads) Cloudflare R2 (zero egress) and/or Hetzner behind Bunny.net / Cloudflare CDN Margin lives or dies here. file-storage.md already recommends R2. Control plane (low bandwidth) API, dashboard, Postgres, Redis, BullMQ workers Hetzner k8s (k3s / Talos) to start Keeps fixed cost near-zero while bootstrapping.

Rule of thumb: control plane wherever is convenient; data plane wherever egress is cheapest.

docs.title: Recommended starting topology
docs.text:
• Bundle storage: Cloudflare R2 (content-addressed, per server-design/file-storage.md).
  • CDN: Cloudflare or Bunny.net in front of R2/origin for global edge delivery + cheap egress.
  • Control plane: k8s nodes running the server-design/overview.md stack (Postgres, Redis, API, dashboard, workers) translated from docker-compose to manifests/Helm.
  • Differential updates (binary diffs) on the data plane cut bandwidth further and sell as a premium "instant updates" feature — double win on the cost axis.

docs.title: Available infrastructure (mapped 2026-06-15)
docs.text:
The creator's actual clusters/machines, and how each maps to a role (the maintainer's hosted CodeSync offer — self-hosters bring their own; see server-design/overview.md).

Resource Specs / cost Already running Capsule role aks-azure (own) ~$500/mo subscription Keycloak, Postgres, pgAdmin, MongoDB (min resources) Control plane. Reuse the existing Postgres for the CodeSync DB and Keycloak for auth — see below. aks-ssdnodes 64 GB RAM / 1 TB disk, temporary (3-mo trial), shared — Staging / load-test only. Great for bringing up + load-testing the server stack; never persistent production state (expires, shared). k0s box 8 GB RAM / 50 GB disk — Dev / single-node. Run the whole docker-compose stack as one local instance, or a CI/runner. Too small for production. Cloudflare R2 + CDN $0 egress — Data plane (bundle storage + delivery). Add this — it's the margin decision.

docs.title: Reuse what's already on aks-azure
docs.text:
• Postgres → point DATABASE_URL at the existing instance (separate database/schema for CodeSync). Saves standing up a new DB; watch resource limits ("min resources" today — may need a bump).
  • Keycloak → a genuine upgrade over the Server doc's built-in email/password JWT auth. Keycloak gives OIDC + SAML SSO out of the box, which server-design/overview.md lists as "roadmap" and which is a paid enterprise feature in the business model. Wire the API/dashboard to Keycloak as the IdP instead of (or alongside) the built-in auth.
  • MongoDB / pgAdmin → not required by the design (it's Postgres-first); leave as-is.

docs.title: Critical caveat: keep bundle egress OFF aks-azure
docs.text: The control plane on aks-azure is fine cost-wise because it's low bandwidth — device check-ins are many small JSON requests (cached in Redis), not the heavy bytes. The bundle downloads — the only bandwidth that matters — must go to R2/CDN, never AKS/Azure egress (~$0.08/GB would wreck margins). This split is exactly the data-plane/control-plane separation above.

docs.title: Suggested bring-up sequence
docs.text:
1. Dev: run the full stack via docker-compose on the k0s box (or locally) against a scratch DB.
  2. Staging / load-test: deploy to aks-ssdnodes (64 GB) while it lasts; hammer the check + download paths; validate R2/CDN delivery.
  3. Production control plane: aks-azure, reusing Postgres + Keycloak; bundles on R2 + CDN.
  4. Reserve a migration path off aks-ssdnodes before its 3-month trial expires.

docs.title: When to reach for AWS / Azure
docs.text:
You have Azure + AWS accounts and k8s skills — keep them for enterprise-driven needs, billed accordingly:

  • A customer requires a specific cloud / region for data residency or procurement reasons.
  • On-prem / self-managed Enterprise license: ship the same k8s manifests for the customer to run in their own AKS/EKS/on-prem cluster (high-ticket — see business/business-model.md).

Until then, AWS/Azure are options you charge for, not the default.

docs.title: Reliability is the trust currency
docs.text: A startup running production OTA infra must earn trust: uptime, CDN reliability, and — eventually — an SLA for paid tiers. Atomic two-slot bundles + on-device crash-loop rollback (Phase 2 Step 7) already protect the device side; the service side needs monitoring, health checks, and staged rollout of the control plane itself.

docs.title: Capsule Framework — Issues, Solutions & Prior Art
docs.text: Raised against principles.md. Each issue includes severity, recommended solution, and relevant existing projects to adopt or study.

docs.title: Issue 1 — .capsule/ Directory Commit Strategy is Ambiguous
docs.text: Severity: Medium

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: The doc says "commit it for reproducibility, treat it like a lock file." This causes: - Every capsule sync produces noisy, meaningless diffs - CI always regenerates it anyway — committed state drifts silently - Developers fight the .gitignore default (do I commit or not?)

docs.title: Recommended Solution
docs.text:
Gitignore .capsule/ by default. Commit only capsule.lock.

# .gitignore (generated by capsule init)
.capsule/

# capsule.lock — DO commit this

capsule.lock records the resolved versions of the native capsule and all plugins (like package-lock.json). CI runs capsule sync as an explicit pre-build step using the lock file to reproduce the exact same generated wrappers deterministically.

# CI pipeline
capsule sync --frozen-lockfile   # fails if lock is out of date
capsule build android

docs.title: Prior Art
docs.text:
• Gradle wrapper (gradlew) — generated but committed because it's a bootstrap shim, not generated output
  • package-lock.json — lock the versions, regenerate the artifacts
  • CocoaPods Podfile.lock — same pattern for iOS deps

docs.title: Issue 2 — Bridge Protocol Underspecified
docs.text: Severity: High — affects every plugin author and the entire SDK contract

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
The current spec only covers request/response: 

window.__capsule.call('camera.capture', { quality: 0.8 })
window.__capsule.resolve(callId, { path: '/tmp/img.jpg' })
Missing: - Streaming (video frames, file download progress, sensor data) - Cancellation (user navigates away mid-operation) - Error taxonomy (permission denied vs hardware error vs timeout — all look the same) - Event subscriptions (native pushes to web without a web-initiated call)

docs.title: Recommended Solution
docs.text:
Adopt JSON-RPC 2.0 as the bridge wire format, extended with Capsule-specific envelope fields.

// Web → Native (request)
{
  jsonrpc: '2.0',
  id: 'uuid-v4',           // callId
  method: 'camera.capture',
  params: { quality: 0.8 }
}

// Native → Web (success)
{
  jsonrpc: '2.0',
  id: 'uuid-v4',
  result: { path: '/tmp/img.jpg' }
}

// Native → Web (error — typed)
{
  jsonrpc: '2.0',
  id: 'uuid-v4',
  error: {
    code: 4001,              // Capsule error registry
    message: 'PERMISSION_DENIED',
    data: { permission: 'CAMERA' }
  }
}

// Native → Web (event / stream chunk — JSON-RPC "notification")
// IMPORTANT: notifications omit the `id` field entirely.
// id: null is NOT a notification — it is a response to a null-id request.
{
  jsonrpc: '2.0',
  method: 'push.messageReceived',
  params: { title: '...', body: '...' }
}

Capsule Error Code Registry (define upfront):

Range Category 1xxx Framework errors (bridge timeout, serialization) 2xxx Permission errors 3xxx Hardware errors (camera unavailable) 4xxx Plugin-specific errors 5xxx User cancellation

Cancellation via a capsule.cancel(callId) call — native must honor it for any long-running operation.

docs.title: Prior Art
docs.text:
• JSON-RPC 2.0 spec — jsonrpc.org — battle-tested, tooling exists, readable
  • Capacitor's bridge (@capacitor/core) — study src/bridge.ts for real-world handling of callbacks and events
  • @trpc/server — for inspiration on typed procedure definitions that could generate bridge manifests

docs.title: Issue 3 — Hot Reload on Physical Devices is Fragile
docs.text: Severity: Medium — major DX pain point, especially in corporate environments

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: "Same WiFi: load from machine's LAN IP" fails when: - Corporate/guest WiFi isolates clients (very common) - Dynamic IP requires manual reconfiguration - Developer switches networks without noticing

docs.title: Recommended Solution
docs.text:
Build tunneling into capsule dev as a first-class mode.

capsule dev                   # LAN mode (default, fastest)
capsule dev --tunnel          # HTTPS tunnel (works everywhere)
capsule dev --qr              # Display QR code for device pairing

The --tunnel flag should: 1. Use Cloudflare Tunnel (free tier, no account needed for ephemeral tunnels via cloudflared) or a self-hosted tunnel endpoint 2. Generate a https://random.trycloudflare.com URL 3. Display a QR code in the terminal — scan with the device to set the dev server URL

Why Cloudflare over ngrok: Cloudflare Tunnel's ephemeral mode requires no account, no auth token, no rate limit on free tier.

# capsule dev --tunnel internals
npx cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:5173
# → https://abc123.trycloudflare.com
# → QR code rendered in terminal via qrcode-terminal npm package

docs.title: Prior Art
docs.text:
• Expo CLI (expo start --tunnel) — uses @expo/ngrok internally, same QR pattern
  • cloudflared — github.com/cloudflare/cloudflared — single binary, works on CI too
  • qrcode-terminal npm package — used by Expo, renders QR in terminal

docs.title: Issue 4 — No Signing & Distribution Story
docs.text: Severity: High — blocks real-world production use

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
Build pipeline ends at .apk. Real releases require: - Android: signing with a keystore, aligning, uploading to Play Store - iOS: provisioning profiles, certificates, notarization, App Store Connect upload

If developers must do this manually, Capsule's DX promise breaks at the last mile.

docs.title: Recommended Solution
docs.text:
Integrate Fastlane as the signing/distribution backend, invoked by the Capsule CLI.

capsule sign android            # configure signing (stores config, not keystore)
capsule build android --release # builds + signs
capsule publish android         # uploads to Play Store (via Fastlane supply)
capsule publish ios             # uploads to App Store (via Fastlane deliver)

Capsule wraps Fastlane so developers never write a Fastfile. The CLI generates it from capsule.config.ts.

Keystore management: Never store the keystore in the project. Capsule should: 1. Generate a keystore on first capsule sign android 2. Encrypt it with a passphrase 3. Optionally push to a secrets backend (env var, 1Password, GitHub Secrets)

// capsule.config.ts signing block
android: {
  signing: {
    storeFile: process.env.CAPSULE_KEYSTORE_PATH,
    storePassword: process.env.CAPSULE_KEYSTORE_PASS,
    keyAlias: process.env.CAPSULE_KEY_ALIAS,
    keyPassword: process.env.CAPSULE_KEY_PASS
  }
}

docs.title: Prior Art
docs.text:
• Fastlane (fastlane.tools) — github.com/fastlane/fastlane — industry standard, handles both platforms
  • Fastlane Match — syncs certificates/profiles via a private git repo or S3
  • EAS Build (Expo Application Services) — study how they abstract signing from developers, good UX reference
  • Gradle signing config — signingConfigs block in build.gradle, already standard

docs.title: Issue 5 — Community Plugin Trust Model is Missing
docs.text: Severity: High — architectural integrity risk

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
The document's core promise is "the shell is a binary dependency, developers never touch native code." A community plugin can completely bypass this — it can include arbitrary Kotlin/Swift code, request any permission, execute any native API.

There is no stated policy on: - What native code community plugins are allowed to include - How plugin quality/safety is vetted - Whether a rogue plugin can escalate privileges beyond what capsule.config.ts declares

docs.title: Recommended Solution
docs.text:
Define a Plugin Trust Tier system with enforcement at install time:

Tier 1 — @capsule/* (official)
  - Maintained by Capsule team
  - Full native access
  - Code audited, signed
  - Example: @capsule/wasm (extends the shell with the WASM runtime for code-logic integrations)

Tier 2 — @capsule-community/* (verified)
  - Third-party, reviewed by Capsule team
  - Native code declared in plugin manifest
  - Automatically flagged in capsule.config.ts

Tier 3 — Unverified plugins
  - Require explicit opt-in in capsule.config.ts (see syntax below)
  - CLI warns on install and on every build

Plugin manifest (capsule-plugin.json) — required for any plugin with native code:

{
  "name": "@capsule-community/stripe",
  "nativePermissions": [],
  "nativePlatforms": {
    "android": { "aar": "https://maven.../stripe.aar" },
    "ios": { "xcframework": "https://..." }
  }
}

Note: trustTier is not self-declared in the manifest — a rogue plugin would simply claim Tier 1. The CLI determines the trust tier from the npm package scope: - @capsule/* → Tier 1 (hardcoded in CLI) — first-party plugins like @capsule/wasm that extend the shell with optional native capabilities - @capsule-community/* → Tier 2 (verified by Capsule team, signed release) - anything else → Tier 3 (unverified, explicit opt-in required)

Tier 3 opt-in syntax in capsule.config.ts:

plugins: [
  '@capsule/wasm',                         // Tier 1 — no opt-in needed
  '@capsule-community/stripe',             // Tier 2 — no opt-in needed

  // Local source plugins — always trusted (you own the source)
  './capsule-plugins/my-scanner',          // shorthand, local: true implied
  { path: './capsule-plugins/my-scanner', local: true },  // explicit form

  // Third-party npm plugin outside @capsule or @capsule-community scopes
  // MUST use object form with trust: 'unverified'
  // CLI prints a warning on every build until this is acknowledged
  { path: 'some-npm-plugin', local: false, trust: 'unverified' }
]

The local: true flag signals the plugin is compiled from source in your project. It is always implied for ./ paths and always false for bare npm package names. The object form exists for cases where you need to be explicit or add trust: 'unverified'.

The CLI reads the manifest at capsule sync and: 1. Merges declared permissions into the generated AndroidManifest.xml / Info.plist 2. Rejects undeclared permissions that weren't in capsule.config.ts 3. Warns if a plugin requests more permissions than the app declared

docs.title: Prior Art
docs.text:
• npm provenance (--provenance flag) — ties npm packages to their source git commit via Sigstore
  • Capacitor plugin registry — capacitorjs.com/docs/plugins — unofficial but curated list
  • Android Play Protect — permission declaration model is already what this borrows from
  • VS Code Extension Marketplace — trust tiers and capability declarations are the model to follow

docs.title: Issue 6 — iOS Phase Deferred but Config Already Exists
docs.text: Severity: Low — documentation gap, easy to handle

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: Phase 1 is Android-only, but capsule.config.ts already shows ios: config keys. A Phase 1 developer adding iOS config gets either silent ignoring or a confusing error.

docs.title: Recommended Solution
docs.text:
CLI should surface clear platform-availability errors with upgrade path:

$ capsule add ios
✖ iOS support is not available in @capsule/cli@1.x
  → Upgrade to @capsule/cli@2.x when iOS support ships
  → Track progress: github.com/capsule-framework/capsule/milestone/3

And in capsule.config.ts, mark the iOS block with a JSDoc that the TS language server will show:

ios: {
  /** @experimental Available in Capsule Phase 4+ */
  deployment: '16.0',
}

docs.title: Issue 7 — Server Readiness Race Condition (Known and Solved)
docs.text: Severity: High — would cause a blank/ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED screen on launch without mitigation

docs.title: Problem (was)
docs.text: Phase 2 adds an embedded HTTP server (NanoHTTPD on Android). The WebView navigates to http://127.0.0.1:{port}/ on launch. If the WebView navigates before the server is bound and listening, the user sees ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED.

docs.title: Solution (decided in ADR-001)
docs.text:
CapsuleRuntime owns the startup sequence. CapsuleActivity delegates entirely to it:

  1. Splash screen shows immediately (zero blank frame)
  2. CapsuleRuntime.start() binds NanoHTTPD and (if routes exist) evaluates the QuickJS server bundle
  3. On ready → WebView navigates to http://127.0.0.1:{port}/ and splash hides
  4. On timeout (default 3 s, configurable via server.timeout in capsule.config.ts) → error screen with a retry button

The SplashController interface and FakeSplashController fake enable this entire flow to be tested in pure JVM unit tests — no device or emulator needed.

docs.title: Prior Art
docs.text:
• React Native's splash pattern — AppRegistry.registerComponent deferred until JS bundle is loaded
  • Capacitor's WebViewAssetLoader — avoids this problem by serving from a pre-bound URL, but Capsule's embedded server approach gives more capability in exchange for managing readiness explicitly

docs.title: Issue 8 — Crash Loop Recovery (Known and Solved)
docs.text: Severity: High — without mitigation, a bad OTA (codeSync) deploy could permanently brick the app until a store update

docs.title: Problem (was)
docs.text: codeSync can push a new web bundle or server bundle to the device. If the new bundle crashes on launch (runtime error, bad JS, incompatible API), the app crashes on every open. The user has no recovery path short of reinstalling.

docs.title: Solution (decided in ADR-001)
docs.text:
CapsuleRuntime tracks start failures. Three failures within 60 seconds triggers automatic rollback to the previous known-good bundle zip. The rollback is silent — the user sees a brief restart, not an error.

  • CodeSyncManager interface owns the rollback logic
  • The "bundle" is always atomic: www/ + server/bundle.js together in one zip; they are never deployed independently
  • The crash loop counter resets on a successful startup
  • Tested via FakeCapsuleServer.crashesAfterRequests(1) in pure JVM unit tests

This means a bad codeSync deploy is self-healing. Developers and users never see the rollback unless they inspect logs.

docs.title: Summary Table
docs.text: # Issue Severity Solution Key Prior Art 1 .capsule/ commit strategy Medium Gitignore dir, commit lock file package-lock.json, CocoaPods 2 Bridge protocol gaps High JSON-RPC 2.0 + error registry + events JSON-RPC spec, Capacitor bridge 3 Hot reload device fragility Medium --tunnel via Cloudflare + QR Expo CLI tunnel, cloudflared 4 No signing/distribution High Fastlane integration, env-based keystore Fastlane, EAS Build 5 Plugin trust model missing High Trust tiers + plugin manifest + CLI enforcement npm provenance, VS Code Marketplace 6 iOS config in Phase 1 Low CLI error + JSDoc @experimental N/A 7 Server readiness race condition High Splash + CapsuleRuntime startup sequence + timeout React Native splash, ADR-001 §6 8 Crash loop after bad OTA deploy High 3-failures/60s auto-rollback via CodeSyncManager ADR-001 §7

docs.title: Capsule Framework — Implementation Overview
docs.text:
This folder contains the step-by-step implementation guide for building the Capsule Framework itself — the CLI, native shells, core SDK, and CodeSync infrastructure.

Prerequisites: machine setup complete (environment.md). GitHub org and CI/CD are Phase 8 (Ecosystem).

docs.title: Implementation Phases
docs.text:
Re-sequenced 2026-06-15 (strategy session, revised). Capsule is a personal project — not racing for funding, so capability comes before monetization: native-API expansion stays Phase 3, then iOS, then Capsule UI (native-look layer, Phase 5 — slotted after iOS so its presets target a real iOS shell), then the Server Code Push / OTA cloud (the eventual funding engine, gated on iOS) and the migration on-ramp. The strategy/business docs (../Business/) still hold — they're just sequenced later. The old phase content is preserved; only order changed.

Phase Deliverable Status Phase 1 — Foundation CLI (capsule init/add/sync/dev/build/run) + Android shell (Kotlin AAR) + 6 native APIs (geolocation, camera, haptics, push, biometrics, alerts) + templates + WebBridge (browser dev fallback) ✅ Done Phase 2 — Embedded Runtime (Android) Embedded HTTP server (NanoHTTPD; replaced by CivetWeb 2026-10-24 — adr-004 amendment) + QuickJS on-device JS runtime + CapsuleRuntime coordinator + file-based route handlers + atomic CodeSync bundles + crash-loop rollback ✅ Steps 1–7 complete · Group 0 + Group 2 browser-dev e2e tested (OTA network delivery deferred to Phase 6) Phase 3 — Native APIs Expansion Ordered (foundational → specialized): Camera ✅ → Filesystem ✅ → App lifecycle + deep links ✅ → Network status ✅ → Push (FCM/APNs) → Local notifications → Biometrics → Status bar / Keyboard / Share → SQLite db → ai inference (Tier-1 OS-native spike, see adr-003) → NFC / Bluetooth → Background jobs → Telecom / SMS. Every API honours two OTA-driven constraints — persist user data outside the OTA-swappable bundle dirs, and carry a native-capability version (see "Phase 3 ordering" below). 🔄 Camera + Filesystem + App lifecycle/deep links + Network status done · SQLite db + ai Tier-1 spike built out of order (2026-10-24, device tests pending) · rest ⬜ Phase 4 — iOS (pulled forward, was Phase 6) CivetWeb — the same C server as Android, ✅ built + Linux-tested (embedded loopback HTTP server → http://127.0.0.1:{port}/, symmetric with Android — WKURLSchemeHandler rejected, see adr-004) + QuickJS compiled for iOS + WKWebView shell — same capsule.config.ts, same TS route handlers. No Mac purchase needed for bring‑up — see ios-bring-up.md. Now using xtool / XKit for cross‑platform SwiftPM build and optional helpers (networking, crypto, device management). Contract‑readiness audit (2026‑06‑26): the Android interfaces are essentially iOS‑ready — seam is at the provider/controller boundary, only platform‑edge glue leaks android.*; QuickJS C lib compiles unchanged (only the JNI glue is re‑written). Tiered breakdown + the one BundleStore/java.io.File nit in 080. In progress – SwiftPM conversion + tested CodeSync client core done (2026-10-15, Linux-tested via Docker); next: xtool container build + Apple auth Phase 5 — Capsule UI (native-look component layer) capsule add-ui (shadcn-style; shipped 2026-10-24 — copies ui-kit class builders) + shared iOS/Material Tailwind preset + per-framework behaviour — "Capsule's own Konsta". Slotted after iOS so the iOS/Material presets target a real WKWebView shell and the native look is proven on both platforms (the native capabilities already land in Phase 3). Pure frontend/CSS — touches no native APIs. See adr-002. 🔄 Foundation done — framework-agnostic class builders + iOS/Material presets in packages/ui-kit (tsc strict clean, 15/15 tests green); capsule add-ui shipped (2026-10-24); per-framework adapters next Phase 6 — Server Code Push / OTA Cloud (the funding engine) OTA network delivery (capsule codesync publish + on-device fetch — the deferred half of Step 7) + Portal/control plane (server design) + canary + auto-rollback + multi-tenant + metrics/logs + billing. + AI agent layer (native bridge as agent tool surface) + hybrid/on-device inference (Cactus/llama.cpp Tier 2) + cloud inference (metered, Tier 3) + OTA-updatable agent logic — see adr-003. 🔄 Server design done + local self-hosted server implemented & E2E-verified (packages/codesync-api); CLI codesync publish done + on-device fetch client JS/API implemented + native implementation pending + portal + billing + AI/agents pending Phase 7 — Migration On-Ramp (go-to-market) capsule migrate ionic + @capsule/compat-capacitor shim + plugin importer (Capacitor/Cordova → Capsule ABI). Acquisition funnel — can overlap Phase 6. See ../concepts/ionic-framework7-migration.md + research/chatgpt-plugin-compatibility.md. ⬜ Not started Phase 8 — Ecosystem GitHub org, publishing pipeline, CI/CD, npm publish, Docker images, Shell registry via GitHub Releases, template registry, docs site. OSS/package release readiness — repo-target, docs split, license, de-Windows, npm+Maven publish — is captured as pending decisions + a pre-publish checklist in release.md (the public-launch flip itself is gated at Phase 6, see D1/D6 there). 🔄 Template extensibility ✅; publish pending (decisions logged: release.md) Phase 9 — DX VS Code extension, error overlays, device inspector, Fastlane signing automation ⬜ Not started

Start here: cli.md (CLI) → architecture.md (core + Android shell) Strategy & business: business/business-model.md · business/pricing.md · business/ota-policy-and-liability.md · infra infrastructure.md

Recurring upkeep (cross-cutting, all phases): a periodic dependency & tooling audit — QuickJS-ng, CivetWeb, Android SDK / Play targetSdk, Gradle/AGP/Kotlin/NDK, CLI + core npm deps, and the templates — runs at every phase kick-off, before each release, and quarterly. Routine, baseline, and sweep log: upkeep.md. (iOS toolchain added there in Phase 4.)

HTTP fidelity roadmap (embedded server, both platforms — adr-004): the on-device /api server delivers a full web experience, tiered so each step is realistic and works properly:

Capability Status / phase Static serving + request/response /api/* (GET/POST/PUT/DELETE) ✅ Android (Phase 2) · Phase 4 for iOS parity Streaming responses (chunked) Phase 4 parity target WebSockets (ws://localhost, on-device real-time) ⬜ Future — needs a new core route model (onOpen/onMessage/onClose) + single-thread-engine frame pumping. Designed, not excluded. Not promised in the first iOS cut. Server-Sent Events (SSE) ⬜ Future — new core streaming-route model (pairs with WebSockets work) Range requests (media seeking) ⬜ Future — server-side Range handling

These amend adr-001 #4 ("deliberately minimal, no WS/SSE"): HTTP fidelity is now tiered, not minimal-forever. The Bridge-vs-HTTP channel split still holds — WS/SSE are web-standard real-time inside the on-device server, distinct from the native-event Bridge.

docs.title: Phase 2 — Embedded Runtime
docs.text:
Key deliverables, in order:

Step 1: Interfaces + fakes ✅
  [x] CapsuleServer interface + FakeCapsuleServer (neverStarts, startsAfter, crashesAfter)
  [x] QuickJSEngine interface + FakeQuickJSEngine (evaluationFails, slowStart, callReturns)
  [x] SplashController interface + FakeSplashController
  [x] AppNavigator interface + FakeAppNavigator
  [x] CapsuleRuntime wired with fakes — 15 unit tests passing (pure JVM, no device)

Step 2: Embedded server for static assets ✅ (NanoHTTPD; CivetWeb since 2026-10-24)
  [x] CivetwebServer implements CapsuleServer (originally NanoHttpdServer)
  [x] Replaces file:///android_asset/www/index.html with http://127.0.0.1:{port}/
  [x] Port = deterministic hash from appId, range 49152–65535, baked into MainActivity

Step 3: Splash + readiness ✅
  [x] WebViewSplashController implements SplashController
  [x] CapsuleRuntime.start(): show splash → wait for server bind → navigate WebView
  [x] Timeout (3s default) → error screen with retry button

Step 4: QuickJS JNI embedding ✅
  [x] QuickJS-ng v0.15.1 C library in AAR via JNI (CMakeLists.txt, single-thread dispatcher)
  [x] QuickJSEngine.evaluate(bundle) and call(fn, args) working
  [x] QuickJSException sealed class (EvaluateError, CallError)
  [x] 4 instrumented tests passing

Step 5: QuickJSBridge ✅
  [x] QuickJSBridge interface + QuickJSBridgeImpl (AssetManager-backed) + FakeQuickJSBridge
  [x] @capsule/core router runs inside QuickJS — dispatch() returns plain object (not string)
  [x] routes.js bundled by esbuild IIFE into assets/www/ on capsule build
  [x] CapsuleBridge tries JS dispatch first, falls through to Kotlin handlers if null
  [x] 30 unit tests + 8 instrumented tests passing
  [x] Validated end-to-end on emulator (release build): all Kotlin handlers working,
      QuickJS bridge initialises cleanly, METHOD_NOT_FOUND for unregistered methods

Step 6: File-based routing + embedded-server /api/* routing ✅
  Sub-task A — JSON-RPC file discovery (bridge handler overrides):
  [x] src/routes/<method>.ts → export default handler(params) → auto-registered via addRoute()
  [x] CLI discovers files at build time, generates addRoute() calls bundled into server bundle
  [x] Example: src/routes/device.getInfo.ts intercepts device.getInfo before Kotlin

  Sub-task B — HTTP API routing (new /api/* endpoints):
  [x] src/server/routes/*.ts → export GET/POST/PUT/DELETE(req: CapsuleHttpRequest)
  [x] RequestRouter routes /api/* → QuickJSEngine.call("handleHttpRequest", ...) → response
  [x] CLI discovers HTTP route files, generates addHttpRoute() calls in server bundle
  [x] @capsule/core/routes exports CapsuleHttpRequest, CapsuleHttpResponse, addHttpRoute, handleHttpRequest
  [ ] Dynamic segments: users/[id].ts → /api/users/:id (deferred — exact paths only for now)

  Bundle path:
  [x] assets/server/bundle.js (server code never served as a static asset)
  [x] QuickJSBridgeImpl loads from assets/server/bundle.js; the server only serves assets/www/

  Dev-mode routes (resolved during Group 0 testing, 2026-06-12):
  [x] Release: routes run in QuickJS. Dev on-device: CapsuleBridge forwards unmatched
      JSON-RPC methods to the dev sidecar (POST devServerUrl/_capsule/rpc via adb reverse),
      so src/routes/*.ts work under `capsule dev android` too (previously METHOD_NOT_FOUND).

Group 0 end-to-end testing ✅ (2026-06-12)
  [x] All 7 from-template examples: browser-dev · emulator-dev · emulator-release
  [ ] Group 1 (custom React) + Group 2 (non-Vite proxy) + device-release — pending

Step 7: codeSync crash loop + rollback ✅ (2026-06-15)
  [x] BundleStore (two-slot active/previous) + FileBundleStore — atomic install/swap of a bundle
      dir (www/ + server/bundle.js), validates www/index.html; rollback restores previous
  [x] CrashLoopGuard — "3 crashes in 60s" detection over a persistent CrashLog (PrefsCrashLog =
      SharedPreferences, survives process death) + injectable Clock
  [x] CapsuleRuntime: on start() rolls back to previous known-good bundle when crash-looping,
      records each launch attempt, notifyAppReady() (WebView onPageFinished) confirms healthy boot
  [x] Wired into CapsuleActivity (prod path): PrefsCrashLog + FileBundleStore(filesDir/bundles)
  [x] 25 new pure-JVM unit tests (CrashLoopGuard 9 · FileBundleStore 10 · CapsuleRuntime rollback 6),
      incl. the FakeCapsuleServer.CrashesAfter(0) "three crashes → fourth launch rolls back" path.
      Full suite: 71 JVM unit tests green.
  [ ] OTA download/install (capsule codesync publish + on-device fetch) — deferred to Phase 6 (the
      crash-loop + rollback mechanism is in place; only the network delivery of bundles remains)

docs.title: Template extensibility (Phase 1 init + Phase 8 ecosystem) ✅ 2026-06-12
docs.text:
The CLI's init resolves templates from a single templates repo (subdirs per template), driven by a manifest.json so adding a template needs no CLI release:

capsule init my-app --template react-ts                  # official (manifest → templates-repo subdir)
capsule init my-app --template gh:acme/capsule-tpl#v2    # any giget source (GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket/tarball)
capsule init my-app --template ./my-local-template       # local path
  • Dev: reads local templates/manifest.json + copies the subdir.
  • Prod: fetches the manifest from the templates repo (raw URL), giget pulls gh:<repo>/<dir>#<branch>; bundled list is the offline fallback.
  • Custom templates: any source that isn't an official name is passed straight to giget (or copied if a local path). The CLI won't clobber a capsule.config.ts a custom template ships.

Pending (revisit at GitHub publish): confirm the published templates repo name/org (TEMPLATES_REPO in init.ts); company-registry config (~/.capsulerc adding internal templates to the picker); an "Authoring a template" doc + template contract.

docs.title: Compatibility — what Capsule guarantees, and for how long
docs.text:
• The frontend framework runs in the WebView, NOT in QuickJS. QuickJS only runs server routes (src/routes, src/server/routes) + @capsule/core's router. → Any frontend framework, any version, is fine; the only ceiling is the WebView/browser baseline (tied to minSdk / OS).
  • The one real compatibility surface is QuickJS — server-route code must stay within QuickJS-ng's supported JS feature/API set (no Node/DOM globals).
  • The contract to freeze (not the framework): JSON-RPC bridge protocol + @capsule/core API + pinned QuickJS-ng version. Semver + a protocol-version field.
  • Guarantees: capsule.lock pins the shell per project (reproducible); publish a compat matrix (CLI ⇄ shell ⇄ core ⇄ QuickJS ⇄ min WebView); CI builds every template AND runs each route bundle in real QuickJS per release. Framework version is documented as out-of-scope for Capsule compat.

docs.title: CLI distribution & self-update
docs.text:
• Prefer project-local CLI (@capsule/cli devDependency, run via pnpm capsule) → version pinned per project, reproducible. Global install stays for capsule init.
  • No silent auto-update. Add an update-notifier ("update available → npm i -g @capsule/cli@x").
  • capsule upgrade bumps @capsule/core + shell in a project and rewrites capsule.lock (explicit). capsule doctor reports CLI/core/shell/QuickJS versions + compat.

docs.title: Adding Capsule to an existing web project — CLI-assisted (planned)
docs.text:
• capsule dev/build already wrap any bundler (web.buildCommand/devCommand + transparent proxy).
  • A capsule init in an existing dir (or capsule integrate): detect bundler/framework, skip UI scaffold, generate capsule.config.ts (+ build/dev commands), add @capsule/core, run capsule add android. Developer only owns: static build output dir + dev/build commands.

docs.title: Next steps (re-sequenced 2026-06-15, revised)
docs.text:
Capability before monetization: native APIs → iOS → OTA cloud → migration on-ramp. The business strategy (business/business-model.md) holds but is sequenced after the platform is capable and cross-platform.

  1. Phase 3 — Native APIs Expansion (next). Each via the proven interface + provider + Fake pattern, pure-JVM testable. (Realigns with ../decisions/log.md which already scopes camera/filesystem/push/db here.) Ordering — re-sequenced 2026-06-15 to foundational-first (so the table-stakes APIs that later work leans on land before the specialized ones):
# API Why here ✅ Camera done — capturePhoto / pickImage ✅ Filesystem done — read/write/append/delete/mkdir/rmdir/readdir/stat/getUri/downloadFile; data/cache/documents roots kept outside filesDir/bundles; localStorage dev fallback; INTERNET auto-declared for downloads ✅ App lifecycle + deep links done — app.getState/onStateChange/onResume/onPause (ProcessLifecycleOwner — true app-level fg/bg, ignores in-app activity transitions) + app.getLaunchUrl (cold-start, consume-once) / onUrlOpen (warm, via onNewIntent + launchMode=singleTask); strict cold/warm split; CLI generates deep-link intent-filters from deepLinks config; introduced the CapabilityRegistry (capsule.getCapabilities, seeds app/camera/filesystem) for OTA gating; verified on device ✅ Network status done — network.getStatus() + onStatusChange() (no replay-on-subscribe, mirrors app.onStateChange); ConnectionType = wifi\|cellular\|ethernet\|none\|unknown with the invariant none ⇔ !connected; Android ConnectivityManager.registerDefaultNetworkCallback (NetworkRequest fallback < API 24) behind a pure-JVM NetworkProvider seam + de-dup NetworkStatusController; WebBridge maps navigator.onLine + online/offline events; CLI auto-declares ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE; registered in CapabilityRegistry (network=1). Introduced the shared BridgeEventEmitter (extracted from the app-lifecycle AppEventEmitter) reused by both event-driven controllers. OTA/push lean on it. (device smoke + instrumented test pending — see below) 4 Push (FCM/APNs) needs App lifecycle + deep links (✅) to route notification taps 5 Local notifications pairs with push (scheduled, no server) 6 Biometrics auth gate 7 Status bar · Keyboard · Share UI/UX table-stakes group 8 SQLite db — ✅ built 2026-10-24 (database.md) structured storage 8.5 ai inference (Tier-1 spike) — ✅ built 2026-10-24 (ai.md) OS-native wrap (Gemini Nano/AICore; Apple Foundation Models in Phase 4) via the same interface+provider+Fake pattern — proves the bridge surface cheaply. Tier-2 bundled (Cactus/llama.cpp) + Tier-3 cloud + the agent layer land in Phase 6. See adr-003. Every Phase-3 API above is, by then, a free agent tool. 9 NFC · Bluetooth specialized hardware 10 Background jobs WorkManager / BGTaskScheduler 11 Telecom · SMS call / messaging (later)

Two cross-cutting constraints on every Phase-3 API (driven by the Phase-5 OTA model, cheap now / expensive to retrofit): (a) persist user data outside the OTA-swappable bundle dirs (www/ + server/bundle.js) so an OTA bundle swap never wipes it — camera already writes to cacheDir/capsule/camera; (b) carry a native-capability version so the Phase-5 OTA server can gate a JS update against the installed shell (avoid pushed JS calling a native API the shell predates).

Parked (revisit post-iOS): install/manage other apps (an "app store" capability — download .apk + PackageInstaller, or device-owner for silent/kiosk installs). Deliberately not scheduled: it's Android-only — iOS has no app-install API, so it breaks the cross-platform seam. If pursued, it would be an explicit opt-in Android-only module built on Filesystem, kept off the core API surface. 2. Phase 4 — iOS bring-up. Interface-first Swift/QuickJS port mirroring the Android runtime; build + Simulator tests on GitHub Actions macOS (free — the repo is public; ios-macos job already runs swift test). No Mac purchase required yet. Plan: ios-bring-up.md. 3. Phase 5 — Capsule UI (native-look component layer). capsule add-ui (shipped) + shared iOS/Material Tailwind preset + per-framework behaviour — Capsule's own "Konsta". Slotted after iOS so its presets target a real WKWebView shell and native look is proven on both platforms; pure frontend/CSS, touches no native APIs. See adr-002. 4. Phase 6 — Server Code Push / OTA cloud. OTA network delivery (capsule codesync publish + the deferred half of Step 7) + portal + canary/auto-rollback + multi-tenant + billing. Infra on Hetzner + R2/CDN (infrastructure.md). Launch → repos public → free macOS CI. Pulled ahead 2026-09: the local file-based server half is done — packages/codesync-api (Fastify, E2E-verified: publish/rollback/pause/resume, ETag, key auth); remaining: the CLI codesync publish command and the on-device fetch client in packages/core. Pairs with the AI/agents workstream (adr-003): the Tier-2 on-device engine (Cactus/llama.cpp), Tier-3 cloud inference (a metered billing surface), the thin agent layer (native bridge methods = agent tools, MCP-style), and OTA-updatable agent logic all land here — the agent definitions ride Server Code Push, protected by the canary + auto-rollback built in Step 7. Differentiator Ionic can't match (theirs is an experimental OS-model shim; see adr-003's device-coverage cliff). 5. Phase 7 — Migration on-ramp (can overlap Phase 6 as GTM): capsule migrate ionic + @capsule/compat-capacitor + plugin importer. Then Phase 8 ecosystem / Phase 9 DX.

Phase-2 regression — fix at the next code session (user-visible): S1 — embedded-server bind race — ✅ resolved 2026-10-24 (found 2026-10-15): NanoHTTPD 2.3.1 returned from start() before bind(). Fixed by replacing the server with CivetWeb on both platforms — mg_start2 returns only after bind + listen, so readiness holds by construction. Pinned by the instrumented CivetwebServerTest and the Swift CivetwebServerTests. Still to run: SR-4's manual cold-start check on emulator + device. See 2026-10-embedded-server-startup.md → Resolution. NetworkStatusControllerTest + NetworkHandlerTest + the migrated shared-emitter app tests); finish test matrix (Group 0/1 emulator-release + device-release, Group 2 emulator/device); exclude assets/testing/** from CLI vitest sweep; Angular component test; --css tailwind; CLI update-notifier; confirm TEMPLATES_REPO at publish; soften BundleStore's java.io.File signature (activeDir(): File?, install(File)) to a neutral path/URI type so it becomes a literal cross-platform contract — flagged by the 2026-06-26 iOS contract-readiness audit (ios-bring-up.md); every other interface is already platform-neutral; CI docs job installs plain mkdocs but mkdocs.yml requires the material theme (pip install mkdocs mkdocs-material in the workflow fixes it).
