docs.title: process-bundle — Bundle Processing
docs.text:
Triggered by: POST /v1/bundles/upload (immediately after receiving the ZIP)

// packages/codesync-api/src/jobs/process-bundle.ts
import { Job } from 'bullmq'
import AdmZip from 'adm-zip'
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
import { s3, putFile, fileExists } from '../storage/client.js'
import { db } from '../db/knex.js'

interface ProcessBundlePayload {
  bundleId:  string
  zipBuffer: Buffer   // the raw bundle.zip bytes
  appId:     string
  channelId: string
}

export async function processBundleJob(job: Job<ProcessBundlePayload>) {
  const { bundleId, zipBuffer, appId, channelId } = job.data

  await job.updateProgress(5)

  // 1. Parse ZIP
  const zip = new AdmZip(zipBuffer)
  const entries = zip.getEntries().filter(e => !e.isDirectory)

  await job.updateProgress(15)

  // 2. Process each file — store by content hash
  const fileManifest: Record<string, string> = {}
  let processed = 0

  for (const entry of entries) {
    const content = entry.getData()
    const sha256  = 'sha256:' + createHash('sha256').update(content).digest('hex')
    const path    = entry.entryName

    fileManifest[path] = sha256

    // Upsert file record
    await db('bundle_files')
      .insert({ sha256, size_bytes: content.length, first_seen_at: new Date(), last_seen_at: new Date() })
      .onConflict('sha256')
      .merge({ last_seen_at: new Date() })

    // Only upload to storage if not already there (dedup)
    if (!(await fileExists(sha256.replace('sha256:', '')))) {
      await putFile(sha256.replace('sha256:', ''), content)
    }

    processed++
    await job.updateProgress(15 + Math.floor((processed / entries.length) * 70))
  }

  // 3. Store the full ZIP itself (for full-bundle fallback)
  const zipHash = createHash('sha256').update(zipBuffer).digest('hex')
  await putFile(zipHash, zipBuffer)

  await job.updateProgress(90)

  // 4. Mark bundle active, archive previous
  await db.transaction(async (trx) => {
    // Archive previous active bundle
    await trx('bundles')
      .where({ app_id: appId, channel_id: channelId, status: 'active' })
      .update({ status: 'archived', archived_at: new Date() })

    // Activate this bundle
    await trx('bundles')
      .where({ id: bundleId })
      .update({
        status:       'active',
        file_manifest: JSON.stringify(fileManifest),
        activated_at:  new Date(),
      })
  })

  await job.updateProgress(100)

  return { bundleId, fileCount: entries.length }
}

Error handling: If processing fails, status is set to 'failed' with processing_error = err.message. BullMQ retries 3 times with exponential backoff before marking the job as failed.

docs.title: send-notifications — Push Notification Dispatch
docs.text:
Triggered by: CodeSync dashboard when a mandatory update is published, or by a scheduled job checking for devices still on old bundles.

The native push capability (FCM/APNs) is Phase 3 (Native APIs Expansion); server-side dispatch through this worker ships with the OTA cloud in Phase 6. Initial MVP: this job logs which devices need notification — actual push delivery is a Phase 6 addition.

// packages/codesync-api/src/jobs/send-notifications.ts
import { Job } from 'bullmq'
import { db } from '../db/knex.js'

interface SendNotificationsPayload {
  bundleId:  string
  appId:     string
  mandatory: boolean
}

export async function sendNotificationsJob(job: Job<SendNotificationsPayload>) {
  const { bundleId, appId, mandatory } = job.data

  if (!mandatory) return  // only push for mandatory updates initially

  // Find devices still on old bundles
  const staleDevices = await db('devices')
    .where({ app_id: appId })
    .whereNot({ current_bundle_id: bundleId })
    .select('device_id', 'platform')

  // Phase 6: send FCM/APNs push to each device
  // MVP: just log
  console.log(`[notifications] ${staleDevices.length} devices need mandatory update ${bundleId}`)

  return { notified: staleDevices.length }
}

docs.title: cleanup-devices — Stale Device Cleanup
docs.text:
Triggered by: Scheduled cron job (daily at 03:00 UTC)

// packages/codesync-api/src/jobs/cleanup-devices.ts
import { Job } from 'bullmq'
import { db } from '../db/knex.js'

const STALE_DEVICE_DAYS = 180

export async function cleanupDevicesJob(_job: Job) {
  const cutoff = new Date()
  cutoff.setDate(cutoff.getDate() - STALE_DEVICE_DAYS)

  const { rowCount } = await db.raw(
    `DELETE FROM devices WHERE last_seen_at < ? RETURNING id`,
    [cutoff]
  )

  console.log(`[cleanup] Removed ${rowCount} stale devices (last seen > ${STALE_DEVICE_DAYS} days ago)`)
  return { removed: rowCount }
}

docs.title: cleanup-orphaned-files — Storage Cleanup
docs.text:
Triggered by: Weekly scheduled job. Removes objects from S3/MinIO that are no longer referenced by any bundle.

// packages/codesync-api/src/jobs/cleanup-orphaned-files.ts
import { Job } from 'bullmq'
import { db } from '../db/knex.js'
import { s3 } from '../storage/client.js'
import { ListObjectsV2Command, DeleteObjectsCommand } from '@aws-sdk/client-s3'

const BUCKET = process.env.STORAGE_BUCKET!

export async function cleanupOrphanedFilesJob(_job: Job) {
  // Get all SHA-256 hashes referenced by active/archived bundles
  const referencedHashes = new Set<string>()

  const bundles = await db('bundles')
    .whereIn('status', ['active', 'archived'])
    .select('file_manifest', 'zip_hash')

  for (const bundle of bundles) {
    const manifest: Record<string, string> = JSON.parse(bundle.file_manifest ?? '{}')
    for (const sha256 of Object.values(manifest)) {
      referencedHashes.add(sha256.replace('sha256:', ''))
    }
    if (bundle.zip_hash) referencedHashes.add(bundle.zip_hash)
  }

  // List all objects in storage
  let deletedCount = 0
  let continuationToken: string | undefined

  do {
    const response = await s3.send(new ListObjectsV2Command({
      Bucket: BUCKET,
      Prefix: 'bundles/',
      ContinuationToken: continuationToken,
    }))

    const toDelete = (response.Contents ?? [])
      .map(obj => obj.Key!)
      .filter(key => {
        const hash = key.split('/').pop()!
        return !referencedHashes.has(hash)
      })

    if (toDelete.length > 0) {
      await s3.send(new DeleteObjectsCommand({
        Bucket: BUCKET,
        Delete: { Objects: toDelete.map(Key => ({ Key })) },
      }))
      deletedCount += toDelete.length
    }

    continuationToken = response.NextContinuationToken
  } while (continuationToken)

  console.log(`[cleanup] Deleted ${deletedCount} orphaned objects from storage`)
  return { deletedCount }
}

docs.title: aggregate-analytics — Daily Analytics Rollup
docs.text:
Triggered by: Scheduled job (daily at 02:00 UTC). Aggregates update_checks into summary rows for the dashboard charts (reduces query cost on large datasets).

// packages/codesync-api/src/jobs/aggregate-analytics.ts
import { Job } from 'bullmq'
import { db } from '../db/knex.js'

export async function aggregateAnalyticsJob(_job: Job) {
  // Aggregate yesterday's update_checks into daily summaries
  await db.raw(`
    INSERT INTO update_check_daily_summary (app_id, date, total_checks, updates_delivered, no_update, bytes_transferred)
    SELECT
      app_id,
      DATE(created_at) AS date,
      COUNT(*) AS total_checks,
      COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE response_type = 'update_available') AS updates_delivered,
      COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE response_type = 'no_update') AS no_update,
      COALESCE(SUM(bytes_to_transfer), 0) AS bytes_transferred
    FROM update_checks
    WHERE DATE(created_at) = CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '1 day'
    GROUP BY app_id, DATE(created_at)
    ON CONFLICT (app_id, date) DO UPDATE
      SET total_checks      = EXCLUDED.total_checks,
          updates_delivered = EXCLUDED.updates_delivered,
          no_update         = EXCLUDED.no_update,
          bytes_transferred = EXCLUDED.bytes_transferred
  `)
}

docs.title: Scheduled Jobs (Cron)
docs.text:
BullMQ supports repeatable jobs. Register these in the worker startup:

// packages/codesync-api/src/worker.ts (additions)
import { Queue } from 'bullmq'

const deviceCleanupQueue = new Queue('device-cleanup', { connection })
const analyticsQueue     = new Queue('analytics', { connection })
const storageCleanupQueue = new Queue('storage-cleanup', { connection })

// Register repeatable jobs (idempotent — safe to run on every worker restart)
await deviceCleanupQueue.add('daily-cleanup', {}, {
  repeat: { pattern: '0 3 * * *' },   // 03:00 UTC daily
  jobId: 'device-cleanup-daily',       // fixed ID prevents duplicates
})

await analyticsQueue.add('daily-rollup', {}, {
  repeat: { pattern: '0 2 * * *' },   // 02:00 UTC daily
  jobId: 'analytics-daily-rollup',
})

await storageCleanupQueue.add('weekly-cleanup', {}, {
  repeat: { pattern: '0 4 * * 0' },   // 04:00 UTC every Sunday
  jobId: 'storage-cleanup-weekly',
})

docs.title: Retry Policy
Monitoring
docs.text:
BullMQ exposes job counts and health via the BullMQ Board UI or custom metrics:

// packages/codesync-api/src/routes/health.ts
import { Queue } from 'bullmq'

export async function queueHealth() {
  const queues = ['bundle-processing', 'notifications', 'device-cleanup', 'analytics']

  return Promise.all(queues.map(async (name) => {
    const q = new Queue(name, { connection })
    const counts = await q.getJobCounts('waiting', 'active', 'failed', 'delayed')
    return { queue: name, ...counts }
  }))
}

GET /health/queues
→ [
    { "queue": "bundle-processing", "waiting": 0, "active": 1, "failed": 0, "delayed": 0 },
    { "queue": "notifications", "waiting": 5, "active": 2, "failed": 0, "delayed": 0 }
  ]

Dead letter (consistently failing) jobs are visible in the BullMQ Board dashboard at http://localhost:8080/queues (served by the codesync-dashboard container).

docs.title: CLI (@capsule/cli)
docs.text:
The capsule command creates, runs, builds and ships Capsule apps. This page explains what each command does and which files it reads and writes.

  • Every command, argument, option and default: generated CLI reference, built from the commander definitions, so it is always current.
  • Every capsule.config.ts field: generated config reference.

docs.title: Running the CLI
docs.text:
Inside this repo, build the CLI and run its entry point:

pnpm --filter @capsule/cli build
node packages/cli/dist/index.js --version

The examples below write capsule …; substitute node <repo>/packages/cli/dist/index.js … until you have the binary on your PATH.

Android builds need two things from your environment: a JDK 17 (JAVA_HOME) and, today, the path of a locally built shell AAR in CAPSULE_SHELL_OVERRIDE_PATH (see capsule sync). environment.md covers the full machine setup.

docs.title: The app workflow
docs.text:
capsule init my-app --template react-ts --app-id com.example.myapp
cd my-app
capsule add android          # registers the platform and generates .capsule/android/
capsule dev                  # live reload on a device or emulator (debug build)
capsule build android        # web bundle + route bundle + Gradle build
capsule run android          # install the APK on a device or emulator
capsule codesync publish     # ship a web-only update over the air

A debug build loads the app from the dev server (capsule dev). A release build (--release) serves the bundled files from the embedded server inside the app and needs no dev server.

docs.title: capsule init
docs.text:
Creates a project folder from a template, then runs pnpm install in it.

Template sources. --template accepts:

  • an official name (react-ts, vue-ts, svelte-ts, angular-ts, vanilla-ts, vanilla-js, jquery-bootstrap). In a checkout of this workspace the CLI copies it from the local templates/ folder; otherwise it downloads it from the templates repository with giget. The template list itself comes from that repository's manifest.json, with a built-in list as the offline fallback;
  • a GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket URL as copied from the browser, or giget shorthand (gh:owner/repo[/subdir][#ref]), or a tarball URL;
  • a local path.

Files written. capsule.config.ts (only if the template does not ship one), capsule.lock, and .gitignore (only if missing). The generated config sets appId, appName, version and the Android SDK levels; for angular-ts it also sets web.buildCommand and web.devCommand.

Styling and tests.

  • --css tailwind adds Tailwind CSS with the Capsule "native preset": an iOS-style look on the shared .btn/.card/.tab class names, so the same markup looks consistent across templates. Templates without Tailwind support keep plain CSS and the CLI says so.
  • --test vitest adds the opt-in test harness (route contract, unit, component and QuickJS fidelity tiers). Run it with capsule test. See testing.md.

CSS preprocessors (Sass/SCSS, Less, Stylus) are your bundler's job, not Capsule's: install them in the app exactly as in any Vite, Webpack, Rspack or Rollup project. A native component layer ("Capsule UI") is a separate track, see 0002-capsule-ui.md and capsule add-ui.

docs.title: capsule add
docs.text: capsule add android records the platform in capsule.lock and runs capsule sync. capsule add ios records the platform too, but sync generates only the Android project today; the iOS shell is in bring-up (ios-bring-up.md).

docs.title: capsule add-ui
docs.text:
Copies Capsule UI components (0002-capsule-ui.md) into the app, shadcn-style: the app owns the copy and may edit it. The components are Tailwind class builders from @capsule/ui-kit (functions that return a class string), not framework components, so the same files work in every template.

capsule add-ui button card          # one or more component names
capsule add-ui dialog --dir src/lib/ui
capsule add-ui button --force       # overwrite a copy you already have

Component names are the files in ui-kit's src/components/ (case-insensitive): today button, card, dialog, input (which also exports textarea), select, table. An unknown name fails before anything is copied and lists the available ones. Without --force, existing files are kept and reported, because you may have customised them.

What lands in the project mirrors ui-kit's own layout, so the components' ../tokens imports keep working: <dir>/tokens.ts (shared presets and cn) and <dir>/components/<name>.ts.

import { button } from './ui/components/button'
// <button class={button({ variant: 'outline', preset: 'ios' })}>Save</button>

The command does not edit capsule.config.ts; make sure your Tailwind content globs include the target directory. Sources come from the installed @capsule/ui-kit package, which ships its src/ for this purpose.

docs.title: capsule sync
docs.text:
Reads capsule.config.ts and regenerates .capsule/android/, the native project you never edit by hand. Run it after changing the config; add and build run it for you.

Shell. The Capsule shell AAR comes from CAPSULE_SHELL_OVERRIDE_PATH (a locally built capsule-release.aar). Resolving released shells from a registry is planned (Phase 8); until then sync fails without the variable.

Generated files, all under .capsule/android/:

settings.gradle.kts, build.gradle.kts, gradle.properties
gradle/libs.versions.toml          ← dependency versions for the app module
gradlew, gradlew.bat, gradle/wrapper/
libs/capsule.aar                   ← the shell
app/build.gradle.kts               ← SDK levels, version, dev-server URL for debug builds
app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml   ← permissions from android.permissions
app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml
app/src/main/res/xml/capsule_file_paths.xml
app/src/main/kotlin/<appId>/MainActivity.kt         ← extends CapsuleActivity
app/src/androidTest/kotlin/<appId>/SmokeTest.kt     ← on-device smoke test
app/src/main/assets/www/, assets/server/            ← filled by capsule build

sync deletes and rewrites only these generated sources. It never touches build/, where the Gradle daemon may hold file locks. The Gradle wrapper is copied from the shell's own Gradle project when the AAR sits inside one; otherwise sync runs gradle wrapper.

Lock file. sync then writes capsule.lock with the CLI version, the SHA-256 of the shell AAR and a hash of the config (lockfile.md). capsule sync --frozen-lockfile regenerates nothing: it fails when the AAR or the config changed since the last sync, which makes it a CI check.

docs.title: capsule dev
docs.text:
Starts the dev server with hot reload, for a debug build on a device or emulator.

  • Ports. The dev server listens on devPort (default 5173, or --port). A route sidecar on devPort + 1000 runs your /api routes and serves /_capsule and /__capsule.js.
  • Device access. adb reverse maps both ports, so the device reaches them as localhost on a USB device and on an emulator alike. The debug build's dev-server URL is http://localhost:<devPort>.
  • Vite (the default): the CLI starts Vite itself, proxies the sidecar paths and injects /__capsule.js into every page. It ignores .capsule/, dist/ and .gradle/ so Gradle builds can run at the same time.
  • Other bundlers (web.devCommand): for ng serve the CLI writes .capsule/proxy.json and adds --proxy-config. For webpack serve/rspack serve it runs a dev proxy on devPort and the bundler on devPort + 1 (passed as CAPSULE_INTERNAL_PORT).
  • --tunnel exposes the server through a Cloudflare quick tunnel (cloudflared) and prints a QR code; --qr prints one for the LAN address.

docs.title: capsule build
docs.text:
capsule build android produces an installable app:

  1. warns when the config breaks or will soon break an app-store rule (see capsule doctor); the build continues;
  2. runs capsule sync;
  3. builds the web app (web.buildCommand, or pnpm exec vite build) into dist/;
  4. injects the mobile CSS reset into dist/index.html unless web.mobileReset: false (mobile-css-reset.md);
  5. copies dist/ to .capsule/android/app/src/main/assets/www/;
  6. bundles the route handlers with esbuild into assets/server/bundle.js for QuickJS: src/routes/<method>.ts default exports become JSON-RPC overrides, and src/server/routes/**/*.ts exported GET/POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH functions become /api/<path> routes;
  7. runs Gradle: assembleDebug, assembleRelease with --release, or bundleRelease with --release --format aab.

The APK lands in .capsule/android/app/build/outputs/apk/{debug,release}/. Only Android is supported so far. Release signing is left to Gradle.

docs.title: capsule run
docs.text: capsule run android installs the built APK with adb install -r: the debug APK, or the release APK with --release (it falls back to app-release-unsigned.apk when no signed one exists). --device picks a device from adb devices. It installs but does not launch the app; open it on the device.

docs.title: capsule test
docs.text: Runs the app's Vitest suite (pnpm exec vitest run, or watch mode with --watch). Extra arguments pass through to Vitest, e.g. capsule test routes. The project needs the harness from capsule init --test vitest; without a vitest.config.ts the command explains how to add it. Suites are hermetic; set CAPSULE_API_BASE to also run the integration test against a live API.

docs.title: capsule doctor
docs.text:
Checks the development environment: Node.js, pnpm, a JDK, adb, whether a device or emulator is connected, and whether CAPSULE_SHELL_OVERRIDE_PATH is set. It exits with code 1 when a required tool is missing.

Run inside an app (a folder with capsule.config.ts), it also checks the config against the app-store rules bundled with the CLI, such as the minimum targetSdk Google Play accepts, and prints the date those rules were last reviewed. --strict makes a violated rule exit non-zero.

docs.title: capsule codesync publish
docs.text: Builds, zips and uploads a web-only update to a CodeSync server. How to set it up and use it: ota-updates.md. The bundle format and protocol: codesync-internals.md.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Variable Used by Meaning CAPSULE_SHELL_OVERRIDE_PATH sync, add, build, doctor Path to the shell AAR to embed. Required until the shell registry exists. JAVA_HOME build (Gradle) JDK 17 used by the Android build. CAPSULE_API_BASE test Base URL for the optional live-API integration test. CAPSULE_INTERNAL_PORT set by dev The port a non-Vite bundler should listen on behind the dev proxy.

CODESYNC_URL and CODESYNC_API_KEY are a convention for the codeSync block in capsule.config.ts, not variables the CLI reads itself.

docs.title: For contributors: how the CLI is built
docs.text:
Path (packages/cli/) Responsibility src/index.ts, src/program.ts Entry point; createProgram() registers every command (also used by the docs generator). src/commands/*.ts One file per command, each exporting a commander Command. src/config.ts CapsuleConfig, loadConfig() (runs capsule.config.ts through jiti, no build step), and CONFIG_FIELDS, the field list behind the generated config reference. src/sync/sync.ts, src/sync/resolve-shell.ts The Android project generator and shell resolution. src/platform/ Store requirements and the Android toolchain versions the generator uses. src/dev-routes-server.ts, src/dev-proxy-server.ts The capsule dev route sidecar and the proxy for non-Vite bundlers. src/lib/ui-kit.ts, src/lib/zip.ts add-ui copy logic; the cross-platform ZIP writer for codesync publish. src/tailwind.ts, src/testing.ts, src/mobile-css-reset.ts init --css, init --test, and the reset build injects. src/__tests__/ Vitest suites (pnpm --filter @capsule/cli test).

To add a command: create src/commands/<name>.ts, register it in src/program.ts, describe every argument and option in the commander definition, then run pnpm docs:gen so the generated reference picks it up.

The exact dependency list and scripts are in packages/cli/package.json; versions follow upkeep.md.

docs.title: @capsule/core API
docs.text:
The TypeScript API an app uses to reach the device: camera, files, push, the database, on-device AI and more. Every module is imported from @capsule/core.

  • Exact signatures, types and doc comments: generated core API reference (TypeDoc, regenerated from packages/core/src by pnpm docs:gen).
  • This page: how the API is put together, what each module covers and its platform behaviour, the error codes, and the design of modules that are planned but not built.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
import { camera, filesystem, db } from '@capsule/core'

const photo = await camera.capturePhoto({ maxWidth: 1600 })
await filesystem.writeFile('today.txt', 'Hello')
const rows = await db.sql`SELECT * FROM notes WHERE pinned = ${true}`
  • One bridge, three implementations. Inside the Capsule shell, calls go to the native side over the JSON-RPC bridge. In a plain browser (during vite dev) @capsule/core switches to WebBridge, which maps what it can to web APIs and fails the rest with METHOD_NOT_FOUND. Tests use FakeBridge (exported) to script native responses.
  • Same API on the server side. Route handlers that run in QuickJS on the device (src/routes/, src/server/routes/) can import the same modules; there the calls go through QuickJSBridge. See 0001-embedded-runtime.md § R5.
  • Every module has the same shape: a TypeScript module over a bridge, a native interface, a fake for tests, and a platform provider. The method names live in one …Methods constant per module (for example NetworkMethods) shared by the module and WebBridge.
  • Errors are CapsuleError instances with a numeric code from CapsuleErrorCode and optional data (see Error codes).
  • Events (onStatusChange, onMessage, watchPosition, …) return an unsubscribe function.
  • Capability check. capabilities.has(name, minVersion) tells an over-the-air bundle whether the installed shell provides a native module at a given version, so new JS can avoid calling an API an older shell lacks.

docs.title: Modules
docs.text:
Built modules, as exported by packages/core/src/index.ts. Platform status per module is tracked in platform-parity.md.

Module What it does More alerts Native alert dialogs with custom buttons and styling (show). alerts-styling.md app App state and lifecycle (getState, onStateChange, onResume, onPause) and deep links (getLaunchUrl, onUrlOpen). App lifecycle camera Take a photo (capturePhoto) or pick one from the library (pickImage). Camera capabilities Which native modules the installed shell provides, and at what version. — clipboard Read and write plain text. — codesync Over-the-air update status and manual checks. ota-updates.md db SQLite: sql tagged template, transaction, schema migrations. database.md device Platform, model, manufacturer, OS and SDK version, emulator flag, WebView version. — filesystem Files in the app's data, cache and documents roots, plus downloads. Filesystem geolocation Current position and position updates. Geolocation haptics Vibration feedback (vibrate(style)). Haptics network Connection status and changes. Network push Remote notifications (FCM on Android, APNs on iOS). push-notifications.md storage A small persistent key-value store for settings and flags. Storage ai On-device text generation with tiered providers (availability, prepare, generate, stream). ai.md

The route API for QuickJS handlers is a separate entry point, @capsule/core/routes (Server routes).

docs.title: app
docs.text: getLaunchUrl() returns the deep link that launched the app once (consume-once), and onUrlOpen reports links that arrive while it runs. onResume/onPause are shortcuts over onStateChange.

docs.title: camera
docs.text:
Both methods resolve to a CameraPhoto whose webPath works directly as an <img src>; ask for result: 'dataUrl' to get the bytes inline instead. capturePhoto asks for the camera permission when needed. The lens choice (facing) is a preference; the system camera decides.

Planned additions (from the original design, not built): checkPermissions, requestPermissions, multi-select in the picker, EXIF data.

docs.title: filesystem
docs.text:
Paths are relative to a logical root, directory: 'data' | 'cache' | 'documents' (default data). A path that resolves outside its root, for example through .., fails with PATH_NOT_ALLOWED. Text crosses the bridge as utf8, binary as base64. downloadFile saves a URL straight to disk.

Planned additions: rename, copy, download progress callbacks, Android external storage.

docs.title: geolocation
docs.text:
getCurrentPosition and watchPosition follow the shape of the W3C Geolocation API (enableHighAccuracy, timeout, maximumAge). navigator.geolocation also works in the WebView; use this module when you want typed error codes.

Planned additions: checkPermissions / requestPermissions.

docs.title: haptics
docs.text:
vibrate(style) with light, medium (default), heavy, success, warning, error or selection. On a device without a vibrator it does nothing; it never throws.

Planned additions: the finer-grained design (impact, notification, the selection* trio, custom Android patterns).

docs.title: network
docs.text:
getStatus() returns { connected, connectionType } with connectionType one of wifi, cellular, ethernet, none, unknown. none always means connected: false; unknown means connected over a transport the OS did not report. onStatusChange does not replay the current state on subscribe.

  • Permissions: Android ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE is declared by the CLI (a normal permission, no dialog). iOS needs none.
  • Native: Android reads ConnectivityManager (default-network callback) behind a pure-JVM NetworkProvider seam, and a de-duplicating controller emits network.statusChange. iOS implements the same seam with NWPathMonitor (Phase 4). In the browser, WebBridge maps navigator.onLine and the online/offline events (transport unknown unless the Network Information API is present).

docs.title: storage
docs.text: get, set, remove, clear, keys over string values, backed by SharedPreferences on Android and UserDefaults on iOS. Use it for settings, tokens and flags; use db for real data. No permissions are needed. (The original design called this module preferences.)

docs.title: Server routes
docs.text:
@capsule/core/routes is what capsule build bundles into server/bundle.js for QuickJS:

  • addRoute(method, handler) overrides a JSON-RPC method with JavaScript (files in src/routes/);
  • addHttpRoute(path, verb, handler) serves /api/<path> (files in src/server/routes/), with CapsuleHttpRequest in and CapsuleHttpResponse out.

You rarely call these directly: the CLI generates the registration code from your route files (cli.md § capsule build).

docs.title: Error codes
docs.text:
The registry is CapsuleErrorCode in packages/core/src/errors.ts, mirrored by the Kotlin BridgeError. Bridge implementations must use these codes exactly. Each module gets its own range; the generic codes are shared.

Code Name When 1000 BRIDGE_UNAVAILABLE No native bridge to talk to. 1001 PARSE_ERROR A request or response could not be parsed. 1002 METHOD_NOT_FOUND No handler for the method (also: a module the shell or browser lacks). 1003 INTERNAL_ERROR Unexpected failure on the native side. 2001 PERMISSION_DENIED A runtime permission was refused (camera, location, …). 2002 OPERATION_CANCELLED The user dismissed a system UI (camera, picker, …). 3001 LOCATION_UNAVAILABLE No position could be obtained. 4001 CAMERA_UNAVAILABLE No camera, or it could not be opened. 4002 MEDIA_PROCESSING_FAILED Encoding or resizing the image failed. 5001 FILE_NOT_FOUND The path does not exist. 5002 FILE_IO_ERROR Reading or writing failed. 5003 PATH_NOT_ALLOWED The path resolves outside its directory root. 6001 PUSH_REGISTRATION_FAILED FCM/APNs registration failed. 7001 AI_UNAVAILABLE No AI tier can generate here, or the model needs ai.prepare(); the reason is in data. 7002 AI_GENERATION_FAILED A ready model failed mid-request. 8001 SQL_ERROR SQLite rejected the statement; details in data. 8002 SCHEMA_VERSION_REGRESSION The stored schema is newer than every db.schema() the app registers (e.g. after an OTA rollback).

Which module raises what:

Module Codes camera 2001, 2002, 4001, 4002 geolocation 2001, 3001 filesystem 5001, 5002, 5003 push 6001 (permission is reported as a status by checkPermissions/requestPermissions, not as an error) ai 1001, 7001, 7002 db 8001, 8002 any 1000–1003

New modules take the next free range, the way push (6xxx), AI (7xxx) and the database (8xxx) did. The planned modules below still carry draft codes from the original design; those numbers collide with the ranges above and will be reassigned when each module is built.

docs.title: Planned modules (design spec)
docs.text:
Everything from here on is design, not built: none of these modules is exported from @capsule/core today. The interfaces are the target contract for when each module is implemented, and they change when the build teaches us something (as network, push, db and camera did). Error-code numbers in these sections are drafts (see above).

The shared types these designs use:

/** Permission status, aligned with the W3C Permissions API (built: exported from push). */
export type PermissionStatus =
  | 'granted'
  | 'denied'
  | 'prompt'                  // first request: the system dialog will appear
  | 'prompt-with-rationale'   // Android: denied once, show a rationale before asking again

/** Returned by all event listeners and position watchers. Call it to stop. */
export type Unsubscribe = () => void

docs.title: biometrics
docs.text:
export type BiometricType = 'fingerprint' | 'face' | 'iris' | 'none'

export interface BiometricAvailability {
  isAvailable: boolean
  biometryType: BiometricType
  /** Why biometrics are unavailable, if applicable */
  reason?: 'NOT_ENROLLED' | 'HARDWARE_UNAVAILABLE' | 'LOCKED_OUT' | 'UNSUPPORTED'
}

export interface AuthenticateOptions {
  /** Reason string shown in the system prompt */
  reason: string
  /** Fallback button label. Set to '' to hide the button. Default: 'Use Passcode' */
  fallbackTitle?: string
  /** Cancel button label. Default: 'Cancel' */
  cancelTitle?: string
  /** Allow device PIN/password as fallback. Default: true */
  allowDeviceCredential?: boolean
}

export declare const biometrics: {
  checkAvailability(): Promise<BiometricAvailability>
  /** Prompt biometric authentication. Resolves on success, rejects on failure. */
  authenticate(options: AuthenticateOptions): Promise<void>
}

Error codes

Code Constant When 3001 BIOMETRICS_UNAVAILABLE No hardware or not enrolled 3002 BIOMETRICS_LOCKED_OUT Too many failed attempts 4001 BIOMETRICS_FAILED Authentication failed 5001 BIOMETRICS_CANCELLED User tapped Cancel or pressed back 5002 BIOMETRICS_FALLBACK User tapped the fallback (passcode) button

docs.title: microphone
docs.text:
export type AudioFormat = 'aac' | 'mp4' | 'wav'

export interface RecordOptions {
  /** Stop recording automatically after this many milliseconds */
  durationLimit?: number
  format?: AudioFormat           // Default: 'aac'
  sampleRate?: number            // Default: 44100
  bitRate?: number               // Default: 128000
}

  path: string

}

  startRecording(options?: RecordOptions): Promise<void>
  stopRecording(): Promise<RecordingResult>
  pauseRecording(): Promise<void>
  resumeRecording(): Promise<void>
  getStatus(): Promise<{ isRecording: boolean; isPaused: boolean; durationMs: number }>

  requestPermissions(): Promise<{ microphone: PermissionStatus }>
}

Code Constant When 2001 MICROPHONE_PERMISSION_DENIED Permission not granted 3001 RECORDING_IN_PROGRESS startRecording called while already recording 3002 NO_ACTIVE_RECORDING stopRecording/pause called with no active session

docs.title: barcode
docs.text:
export type BarcodeFormat =
  | 'QR_CODE' | 'DATA_MATRIX' | 'AZTEC' | 'PDF_417'    // 2D
  | 'EAN_13' | 'EAN_8' | 'UPC_A' | 'UPC_E'             // retail
  | 'CODE_128' | 'CODE_39' | 'CODE_93' | 'ITF' | 'CODABAR' // linear

export interface BarcodeResult {
  value: string
  format: BarcodeFormat
  /** Bounding box in camera preview, normalised 0.0–1.0. Only present when scanned live. */
  boundingBox?: { x: number; y: number; width: number; height: number }
}

export interface BarcodeScanOptions {
  /** Limit detection to specific formats for speed. Default: all formats */
  formats?: BarcodeFormat[]
  /** Show native camera viewfinder UI. Default: true */
  showUI?: boolean
}

export declare const barcode: {
  /** Open the native scanner UI and resolve when a code is detected. */
  scan(options?: BarcodeScanOptions): Promise<BarcodeResult>
  /** Detect barcodes in a static image (file:// or http://localhost/ URI). */
  scanImage(options: { path: string; formats?: BarcodeFormat[] }): Promise<BarcodeResult[]>
  checkPermissions(): Promise<{ camera: PermissionStatus }>
  requestPermissions(): Promise<{ camera: PermissionStatus }>
}

Error codes

Code Constant When 2001 CAMERA_PERMISSION_DENIED Permission not granted 5001 SCAN_CANCELLED User dismissed the scanner UI

docs.text:

docs.text:

  | 'portrait'
  | 'portrait-secondary'      // upside-down
  | 'landscape'               // home button / camera on right

docs.title: motion
docs.text:
Accelerometer and gyroscope combined into a single capability to avoid redundant permission requests.

export interface MotionReading {
  /** Acceleration including gravity, in m/s² */
  acceleration: { x: number; y: number; z: number }
  /** Acceleration with gravity removed */
  accelerationWithoutGravity: { x: number; y: number; z: number }
  /** Rotation rate in rad/s. null if device has no gyroscope. */
  rotationRate: { alpha: number; beta: number; gamma: number } | null
  timestamp: number
}

export declare const motion: {
  isAvailable(): Promise<{ accelerometer: boolean; gyroscope: boolean }>
  /** Start receiving motion updates. Returns an unsubscribe function. */
  watchMotion(
    options: { sampleIntervalMs?: number },    // Default: 100ms
    callback: (data: MotionReading) => void
  ): Unsubscribe
}

docs.title: nfc
docs.text:
export type NfcTechType =
  | 'NDEF' | 'ISO_DEP' | 'MIFARE_CLASSIC' | 'MIFARE_ULTRALIGHT'
  | 'NFC_A' | 'NFC_B' | 'NFC_F' | 'NFC_V'

export interface NdefRecord {
  tnf: 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7   // Type Name Format byte
  type: Uint8Array
  id: Uint8Array
  payload: Uint8Array
}

export interface NfcTag {
  /** Tag UID as hex string: 'A1B2C3D4' */
  id: string
  techTypes: NfcTechType[]
  ndefMessage?: NdefRecord[]
  maxNdefSize?: number
  isWritable?: boolean
}

export declare const nfc: {
  isAvailable(): Promise<{ available: boolean; enabled: boolean }>
  /** Start scanning. Resolves when a tag enters range. */
  scan(options?: { timeout?: number; techTypes?: NfcTechType[] }): Promise<NfcTag>
  /** Write NDEF records to the tag found in the most recent scan(). */
  write(records: NdefRecord[]): Promise<void>
  /** Make the tag read-only. Irreversible. */
  makeReadOnly(): Promise<void>
  checkPermissions(): Promise<{ nfc: PermissionStatus }>
  requestPermissions(): Promise<{ nfc: PermissionStatus }>
}

Error codes

Code Constant When 3001 NFC_UNAVAILABLE No NFC hardware 3002 NFC_DISABLED Hardware present but disabled in settings 3003 TAG_LOST Tag left range during operation 3004 TAG_NOT_WRITABLE Tag is read-only 3005 NDEF_NOT_SUPPORTED Tag does not support NDEF format 3006 NDEF_TOO_LARGE Message exceeds tag capacity 3007 SCAN_TIMEOUT No tag found within timeout ms

docs.text:
export interface BleDevice {
  deviceId: string

docs.title: navigation
docs.text:
export interface BackButtonEvent {
  /** true if window.history.length > 1 */
  canGoBack: boolean
}

export declare const navigation: {
  /**
   * Override the Android hardware back button.
   * The provided handler replaces the default shell behavior for back presses.
   * Returns an unsubscribe function.
   */
  onBackButton(handler: (event: BackButtonEvent) => void): Unsubscribe
  /** Programmatic back navigation — calls window.history.back() and fires popstate. */
  goBack(): void
}

Default shell behavior (built, Android): the back button calls WebView.goBack() when the WebView has history, which fires popstate, so SPA routers handle it with no code. With no history it falls through to the system back action and leaves the app. Planned: the navigation module above, and a capsule:backbutton event dispatched on window when there is no history. See Q11 in ../decisions/log.md.

docs.title: codesync (planned additions)
docs.text:
Built today: checkForUpdate, getStatus, applyUpdate (see ota-updates.md). The design below adds device metadata, the current-bundle query and an explicit reload; note its checkForUpdate signature differs from the built one.

export interface BundleInfo {
  id: string
  /** Canonical version: '{appVersion}+{bundlePatch}' e.g. '1.0.0+3' */
  version: string
  downloadedAt: number   // ms timestamp
}

export interface DeviceMetadata {
  [key: string]: string | number | boolean
}

export declare const codesync: {
  /**
   * Register custom device metadata sent on every check-in.
   * Call after user authentication when business context is known.
   * No PII — use opaque identifiers (tier, group, store_id), not email or name.
   */
  setDeviceMetadata(metadata: DeviceMetadata): Promise<void>
  /** Returns the currently active OTA bundle, or null if running the store build. */
  getCurrentBundle(): Promise<BundleInfo | null>
  /** Manually trigger an update check outside the normal foreground trigger. */
  checkForUpdate(): Promise<void>
  /** Immediately reload the web layer to apply a downloaded bundle. */
  reload(): Promise<void>
}

docs.title: db (planned additions)
docs.text: Built today: db.sql, db.transaction, db.schema (database.md). The design below adds a zero-SQL collection API on the same database file, and encrypted databases. Collections would also be usable inside db.transaction() (tx.collection(…)).

docs.title: db.collection<T>() — CRUD without SQL
docs.text:
Collections auto-create and auto-migrate their table. No CREATE TABLE, no migration files for simple schemas.

import { db } from '@capsule/core'

interface Note {
  id:     string   // auto UUID if omitted on insert
  title:  string
  body:   string
  pinned: boolean
  ts:     number
}

const notes = db.collection<Note>('notes')

// Insert — id is auto-generated if not provided
const note = await notes.add({ title: 'Hello', body: 'World', pinned: false, ts: Date.now() })

// Read
const one  = await notes.get(note.id)
const all  = await notes.getAll()

// Query builder — chainable
const pinned = await notes
  .where('pinned').eq(true)
  .orderBy('ts', 'desc')
  .limit(20)
  .getAll()

const recent = await notes
  .where('ts').gt(Date.now() - 86400_000)
  .orderBy('ts', 'desc')
  .getAll()

// Update / delete
await notes.update(note.id, { title: 'Updated' })
await notes.remove(note.id)
await notes.removeWhere('pinned', false)

// Sync helpers — get local changes since a timestamp, apply server changes
const changes = await notes.changesSince(lastSyncAt)   // { added, updated, removed }
await notes.applyChanges(serverChanges)                // server-authoritative apply

export interface CollectionHandle<T extends { id: string }> {
  add(row: Omit<T, 'id'> & { id?: string }): Promise<T>
  get(id: string): Promise<T | null>
  getAll(): Promise<T[]>
  where<K extends keyof T>(field: K): WhereClause<T>
  update(id: string, patch: Partial<Omit<T, 'id'>>): Promise<void>
  remove(id: string): Promise<void>
  removeWhere<K extends keyof T>(field: K, value: T[K]): Promise<void>
  changesSince(since: Date | number): Promise<CollectionChanges<T>>
  applyChanges(changes: CollectionChanges<T>): Promise<void>
  count(): Promise<number>
}

export interface WhereClause<T> {
  eq(value: unknown): QueryBuilder<T>
  gt(value: unknown): QueryBuilder<T>
  lt(value: unknown): QueryBuilder<T>
  gte(value: unknown): QueryBuilder<T>
  lte(value: unknown): QueryBuilder<T>
  like(pattern: string): QueryBuilder<T>
}

export interface QueryBuilder<T> {
  and<K extends keyof T>(field: K): WhereClause<T>
  orderBy(field: keyof T, direction?: 'asc' | 'desc'): QueryBuilder<T>
  limit(n: number): QueryBuilder<T>
  offset(n: number): QueryBuilder<T>
  getAll(): Promise<T[]>
  getFirst(): Promise<T | null>
  count(): Promise<number>
}

export interface CollectionChanges<T> {
  added:   T[]
  updated: T[]
  removed: string[]  // ids
}

docs.title: Encrypted database — database.open()
docs.text:
For sensitive data. Same combined API (collection + sql), encrypted at rest via SQLCipher. Developer supplies the key — Capsule never derives or stores it.

import { database } from '@capsule/core'

// Derive or retrieve your key — e.g. from biometrics or secure preferences
const key = await biometrics.getKey('db-encryption-key')

const secureDb = await database.open('secure', { key })

// Same API — collection and sql both available, encrypted
const secrets = secureDb.collection<Secret>('secrets')
await secrets.add({ label: 'token', value: '...' })

const rows = await secureDb.sql<Secret[]>`SELECT * FROM secrets`

await secureDb.close()

export declare const database: {
  open(name: string, options?: { key?: string | ArrayBuffer; journalMode?: 'DELETE' | 'WAL' | 'MEMORY' }): Promise<DatabaseInstance>
}

export interface DatabaseInstance {
  collection<T extends { id: string }>(name: string): CollectionHandle<T>
  sql: TaggedSql
  schema(version: number, fn: (tx: SchemaTransaction) => Promise<void>): void
  transaction(fn: (tx: TransactionHandle) => Promise<void>): Promise<void>
  close(): Promise<void>
}

docs.title: notifications (local)
docs.text:
Schedule future notifications that fire at an exact time — even when the app is closed. No server required. This is distinct from push (server-triggered FCM/APNs). Local notifications are scheduled by the app itself, fired by the OS alarm system.

Permission required. Both platforms require explicit user consent. Always call notifications.requestPermission() before scheduling.

import { notifications } from '@capsule/core'

// Request permission (prompt appears once; subsequent calls return current status)
const status = await notifications.requestPermission()
if (status !== 'granted') return

// Schedule a notification at an exact future time
await notifications.schedule({
  id:    'schedule-meeting-123',           // stable id — used to cancel/replace
  title: 'Team Meeting',
  body:  'Starts in 1 hour',
  at:    new Date(meetingStartTime - 60 * 60 * 1000),
  data:  { scheduleId: 'meeting-123' },   // passed back when user taps
  sound: true,                            // default: true
  badge: 1,                              // iOS app icon badge count
})

// Cancel a scheduled (not yet fired) notification
await notifications.cancel('schedule-meeting-123')

// Cancel all pending notifications
await notifications.cancelAll()

// List all scheduled (not yet fired) notifications
const pending = await notifications.getPending()

// React to user tapping a notification — fires when app opens from notification
const unsub = notifications.onTap((event) => {
  // event.id   — the notification id
  // event.data — the data object you passed to schedule()
  navigateTo(`/schedule/${event.data.scheduleId}`)
})

export interface NotificationOptions {
  id:      string            // stable identifier — scheduling again with same id replaces the existing one
  title:   string
  body:    string
  at:      Date | number     // exact fire time
  data?:   Record<string, unknown>
  sound?:  boolean           // default: true
  badge?:  number            // iOS only — app icon badge count
  channel?: string           // Android only — notification channel id (default: 'default')
}

export interface NotificationEvent {
  id:   string
  data: Record<string, unknown>
}

export declare const notifications: {
  requestPermission(): Promise<PermissionStatus>
  checkPermissions(): Promise<PermissionStatus>
  schedule(options: NotificationOptions): Promise<void>
  cancel(id: string): Promise<void>
  cancelAll(): Promise<void>
  getPending(): Promise<Array<{ id: string; scheduledAt: Date; title: string }>>
  onTap(handler: (event: NotificationEvent) => void): Unsubscribe
  /** Fires when a notification arrives while the app is in the foreground. */
  onForeground(handler: (event: NotificationEvent) => void): Unsubscribe
}

iOS limit: max 64 pending local notifications per app. If you exceed this, oldest scheduled notifications are silently dropped. For apps with many future events, schedule only the nearest N.

Android 12+: Exact alarms require SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM or USE_EXACT_ALARM permission. Capsule declares USE_EXACT_ALARM in the shell manifest — no additional config needed.

Error codes

Code Constant When 2010 NOTIFICATION_PERMISSION_DENIED schedule() called without permission 4020 NOTIFICATION_LIMIT_EXCEEDED iOS 64-notification limit reached

docs.title: jobs (background)
docs.text:
Register periodic background tasks that run even when the app is closed. Wraps WorkManager (Android) and BGTaskScheduler (iOS).

Mobile constraint: The OS controls when background jobs actually execute. "Every 4 hours" is a minimum interval hint — the OS may delay execution based on battery state, Doze mode (Android), or device usage patterns (iOS). Design your app to work correctly whether the job ran 4 hours ago or 12 hours ago.

docs.title: Two tiers
docs.text:
Tier 1 — Declarative (no native code, covers 80% of use cases):

// capsule.config.ts — registered at build time
import { defineConfig } from '@capsule/cli'

export default defineConfig({
  jobs: [
    {
      id:         'sync-schedules',
      interval:   '4h',             // minimum interval hint to the OS
      constraints: {
        network:  'required',       // only run when network is available
        battery:  'notLow',         // skip if battery is critically low
      },

      // Fetch from your API and merge into a local collection
      sync: {
        url:        'https://api.myapp.com/schedules',
        headers:    { Authorization: 'Bearer {{preferences.authToken}}' },
        collection: 'schedules',
        strategy:   'merge',        // 'merge' (upsert by id) | 'replace' (full replace)
      },

      // After sync: cancel old notifications and schedule new ones
      notify: {
        from:    'schedules',
        where:   { startsAt: { future: true } },
        limit:   60,                // respect iOS 64-notification cap
        notifications: [{
          trigger:     { minutesBefore: 60 },
          title:       '{{title}}',
          body:        'Starts in 1 hour',
          idTemplate:  'schedule-{{id}}-1h',
        }, {
          trigger:     { minutesBefore: 15 },
          title:       '{{title}}',
          body:        'Starting soon',
          idTemplate:  'schedule-{{id}}-15m',
        }]
      }
    }
  ]
})

Tier 2 — Native handler (for custom logic — use capsule override job:<id>):

capsule override job:sync-schedules
# scaffolds: capsule-overrides/jobs/SyncSchedulesJob.kt (Android)
#            capsule-overrides/jobs/SyncSchedulesJob.swift (iOS)

The scaffolded handler has full access to: HTTP client, SQLite (same db file), notification scheduling, and the Capsule bridge. The TypeScript API is unchanged from the app's perspective.

docs.title: Runtime API (query job state from the web layer)
docs.text:
import { jobs } from '@capsule/core'

// Get last run time and result of a registered job
const status = await jobs.status('sync-schedules')
// { lastRunAt: Date | null, lastResult: 'success' | 'failed' | 'skipped', nextRunAt: Date | null }

// Manually request an expedited run (best-effort — OS may still delay)
await jobs.requestRun('sync-schedules')

// Listen for job completion (fires when app is in foreground and job just finished)
const unsub = jobs.onComplete('sync-schedules', (result) => {
  console.log('Sync finished:', result.lastRunAt)
  // db.collection('schedules') is now up to date — refresh UI
})

export declare const jobs: {
  status(id: string): Promise<JobStatus>
  requestRun(id: string): Promise<void>
  onComplete(id: string, handler: (status: JobStatus) => void): Unsubscribe
}

export interface JobStatus {
  id:          string
  lastRunAt:   Date | null
  lastResult:  'success' | 'failed' | 'skipped' | 'never'
  nextRunAt:   Date | null
}

Note: Jobs are registered at build time via capsule.config.ts — you cannot register a new job dynamically at runtime. This is an OS requirement: both WorkManager and BGTaskScheduler require job identifiers to be declared at app install time.

Error codes

Code Constant When 4030 JOB_NOT_REGISTERED jobs.status() called with unknown job id 4031 JOB_SYNC_FAILED Network error or non-2xx response during declarative sync

docs.title: ui
docs.text:
Built today: native alert dialogs through alerts.show() (alerts-styling.md). The ui module below is the wider design (toasts, banners, an in-app event channel).

In-app UI layer — two complementary APIs on the same capability:

  • Native overlays (ui.toast, ui.banner, ui.alert) — render on top of the WebView. Zero web code needed. Work regardless of what component is mounted.
  • In-app event channel (ui.notify / ui.onNotify) — fire events from anywhere (web layer, native job handler, background task) and handle them in any web component with full UI control.

They compose: a native job fires ui.notify(), a React/Vue component subscribes and renders a rich modal. Or skips the component entirely and calls ui.toast(). Developer picks what fits.

Scope: ui.* only works when the app is open or coming to foreground. For OS-level notifications that appear when the app is closed, use notifications.schedule().

docs.title: ui.toast() — simple feedback
docs.text:
Renders a native toast on top of the WebView. No component needed, no framework dependency. Appears over any screen including loading states.

import { ui } from '@capsule/core'

// Simple
await ui.toast({ message: 'Schedules synced' })

// With duration and action
await ui.toast({
  message:  '42 schedules updated',
  duration: 4000,
  action: {
    label:   'View',
    onPress: () => navigate('/schedules')
  }
})

docs.title: ui.banner() — heads-up notification
docs.text:
Top-of-screen slide-in banner. Richer than a toast — has title, body, optional icon, optional action. Ideal for showing an in-app equivalent of a system notification while the user is already in the app.

await ui.banner({
  title:    'Team Meeting',
  body:     'Starts in 1 hour',
  icon:     '/assets/calendar.png',  // optional
  duration: 5000,
  action: {
    label: 'View schedule',
    data:  { scheduleId: 'meeting-123' }
  },
  onTap: (action) => navigate(`/schedule/${action.data.scheduleId}`)
})

docs.title: ui.alert() — native OS dialog
docs.text:
Displays a native platform alert dialog (not a web modal). Blocks until the user responds. Use for confirmations and destructive actions where a native dialog carries more trust weight.

const result = await ui.alert({
  title:   'Delete schedule?',
  message: 'This cannot be undone.',
  buttons: [
    { label: 'Cancel',  style: 'cancel' },
    { label: 'Delete',  style: 'destructive' }
  ]
})

if (result.label === 'Delete') {
  await schedules.remove(id)
}

docs.title: In-app event channel
docs.text:
ui.notify() / ui.onNotify() — a typed event bus that crosses the native/web boundary. Fire from anywhere: web layer, native job handler, notifications.onForeground(), jobs.onComplete(). Subscribe in any web component.

// ── Firing an event (from anywhere) ──────────────────────────────────

// From the web layer
ui.notify({ type: 'schedule-reminder', data: { scheduleId: '123', title: 'Team Meeting' } })

// From notifications (when notification arrives while app is open)
notifications.onForeground((event) => {
  ui.notify({ type: 'schedule-reminder', data: event.data })
})

// From a completed background job
jobs.onComplete('sync-schedules', (status) => {
  ui.notify({ type: 'sync-complete', data: { syncedAt: status.lastRunAt } })
})

// From a native job handler (Kotlin/Swift) — same bridge mechanism
// bridge.sendNotification("ui.notify", { type: "sync-complete", data: {...} })

// ── Subscribing in a component ────────────────────────────────────────

// Typed subscription — only receives 'schedule-reminder' events
const unsub = ui.onNotify('schedule-reminder', (data) => {
  // data is typed based on what you passed to ui.notify()
  openModal({ scheduleId: data.scheduleId, title: data.title })
})

// Catch-all subscription — receives all events
const unsub = ui.onNotify((event) => {
  console.log(event.type, event.data)
})

// Unsubscribe when component unmounts
onUnmount(() => unsub())

docs.title: Combining both — the full pattern
docs.text:
// ScheduleService.ts — registered once at app startup
import { notifications, jobs, ui } from '@capsule/core'

// Bridge OS notifications → in-app event channel
notifications.onForeground((event) => {
  ui.notify({ type: event.data.type ?? 'notification', data: event.data })
})

// Bridge job completion → in-app event channel
jobs.onComplete('sync-schedules', (status) => {
  ui.notify({ type: 'sync-complete', data: { at: status.lastRunAt } })
})

// ScheduleReminder.tsx — React component, handles rich UI
import { ui } from '@capsule/core'
import { useEffect } from 'react'

export function ScheduleReminder() {
  const [reminder, setReminder] = useState(null)

  useEffect(() => {
    // Rich UI path — component renders its own modal
    const unsub = ui.onNotify('schedule-reminder', (data) => {
      setReminder(data)
    })
    return unsub
  }, [])

  return reminder ? <ReminderModal data={reminder} onClose={() => setReminder(null)} /> : null
}

// BackgroundSyncIndicator.ts — simpler case, just needs a toast
import { ui } from '@capsule/core'

ui.onNotify('sync-complete', ({ at }) => {
  ui.toast({ message: `Synced ${at.toLocaleTimeString()}`, duration: 2000 })
})

docs.title: Interface
docs.text:
export interface ToastOptions {
  message:   string
  duration?: number                          // ms, default: 3000
  action?:   { label: string; onPress: () => void }
}

export interface BannerOptions {
  title:     string
  body?:     string
  icon?:     string                          // asset URL or base64
  duration?: number                          // ms, default: 5000
  action?:   { label: string; data?: unknown }
  onTap?:    (action: { data?: unknown }) => void
  onDismiss?: () => void
}

export interface AlertOptions {
  title:    string
  message:  string
  buttons?: Array<{ label: string; style?: 'default' | 'cancel' | 'destructive' }>
}

export interface AlertResult {
  index: number
  label: string
}

export interface InAppEvent<T = unknown> {
  type: string
  data?: T
}

export declare const ui: {
  // Native overlays
  toast(options: ToastOptions): Promise<void>
  banner(options: BannerOptions): Promise<void>
  alert(options: AlertOptions): Promise<AlertResult>

  // In-app event channel
  notify<T = unknown>(event: InAppEvent<T>): void
  onNotify<T = unknown>(type: string, handler: (data: T) => void): Unsubscribe
  onNotify(handler: (event: InAppEvent) => void): Unsubscribe  // catch-all
}

Error codes

Code Constant When 4040 UI_ALERT_DISMISSED Alert dismissed by OS (e.g. incoming call) without user tapping a button

docs.title: browser
docs.text:
Opens a URL in a native in-app browser overlay — Chrome Custom Tabs (Android) or SFSafariViewController (iOS). The user sees a real browser with an address bar, which is the correct trust signal for OAuth flows and payment pages.

export interface BrowserOpenOptions {
  url: string
  /** Toolbar tint color. Hex '#RRGGBB'. Applied on a best-effort basis per platform. */
  toolbarColor?: string
  /** Presentation style. Default: 'fullscreen' */
  presentationStyle?: 'fullscreen' | 'popover'
  /** Show share button in the toolbar. Default: true */
  enableShare?: boolean
}

export declare const browser: {
  /** Open a URL in the system in-app browser. */
  open(options: BrowserOpenOptions): Promise<void>
  /** Programmatically dismiss the browser (e.g. after detecting an OAuth callback URL). */
  close(): Promise<void>
  /** Fires when the browser is dismissed by the user or by close(). */
  onFinished(handler: () => void): Unsubscribe
  /**
   * Fires on every URL change inside the browser.
   * Primary use case: detect OAuth redirect URIs.
   */
  onNavigationChange(handler: (event: { url: string }) => void): Unsubscribe
  /**
   * Pre-warm a Chrome Custom Tab for faster subsequent open(). Android only, no-op on iOS.
   * Call early (e.g. when the login screen mounts) with the auth URL's origin.
   */
  prefetch(url: string): Promise<void>
}

Typical OAuth / payment flow:

import { browser } from '@capsule/core'

const unsub = browser.onNavigationChange(({ url }) => {
  if (url.startsWith('myapp://oauth/callback')) {
    browser.close()
    unsub()
    handleOAuthCallback(url)
  }
})

await browser.open({ url: authorizationUrl })

No permissions required. iOS restricts SFSafariViewController to https:// URLs.

Error codes

Code Constant When 3020 BROWSER_UNAVAILABLE No browser available on device (rare) 4022 INVALID_URL URL is not a valid https:// URL (iOS restriction) 5020 BROWSER_CANCELLED User dismissed before onFinished was set (edge case)

docs.title: inlineWebView
docs.text:
Renders a second native WebView as an overlay, positioned absolutely within the app. Use for embedded content that must live inside your app's layout — help center chat, embedded payment widgets, interactive third-party content.

export interface InlineWebViewOptions {
  /** URL to load. Mutually exclusive with `html`. */
  url?: string
  /** HTML string to render directly. Mutually exclusive with `url`. */
  html?: string
  /**
   * Position and size. Numbers are interpreted as dp (Android) / pts (iOS).
   * Strings ending in '%' are relative to the screen dimension.
   */
  rect: {
    top:    number | string
    left:   number | string
    width:  number | string
    height: number | string
  }
  /** Allow the embedded page to call through to the Capsule bridge. Default: false */
  allowBridgeAccess?: boolean
  /**
   * Prevent navigation away from the initial origin. Default: true.
   * Set false when you need multi-origin flows (e.g. payment redirects).
   */
  lockToOrigin?: boolean
  /** Background color shown before the page loads. Hex '#RRGGBB'. Default: '#FFFFFF' */
  backgroundColor?: string
}

export interface InlineWebViewHandle {
  /** Navigate to a new URL. */
  loadUrl(url: string): Promise<void>
  /** Replace content with an HTML string. */
  loadHtml(html: string): Promise<void>
  /** Reposition or resize without destroying the view. */
  setRect(rect: InlineWebViewOptions['rect']): Promise<void>
  show(): Promise<void>
  hide(): Promise<void>
  /**
   * Evaluate JavaScript inside the embedded page.
   * Returns the serialised result (JSON.stringify of the expression value).
   */
  evaluateJS(script: string): Promise<string>
  /** Fires on every URL change inside the embedded view. */
  onNavigationChange(handler: (event: { url: string; canGoBack: boolean }) => void): Unsubscribe
  /** Fires when a page finishes loading. */
  onLoad(handler: (event: { url: string }) => void): Unsubscribe
  /** Fires on any page-load error. */
  onError(handler: (event: { url: string; code: number; message: string }) => void): Unsubscribe
  /** Remove the overlay and free native resources. */
  destroy(): Promise<void>
}

export declare const inlineWebView: {
  /** Create and immediately display an inline WebView overlay. */
  create(options: InlineWebViewOptions): Promise<InlineWebViewHandle>
}

Usage example:

import { inlineWebView } from '@capsule/core'

const view = await inlineWebView.create({
  url: 'https://help.myapp.com',
  rect: { top: '10%', left: 0, width: '100%', height: '90%' }
})

// Close button in your own UI calls:
await view.destroy()

When to use browser vs inlineWebView:

Scenario Use OAuth / external auth browser — address bar builds trust Payment page redirect flow browser External link from inside app browser Embedded help center / chat widget inlineWebView Embedded payment widget (no redirect) inlineWebView Rendering controlled HTML inside app inlineWebView with html: option

Error codes

Code Constant When 4021 INVALID_WEBVIEW_OPTIONS Neither url nor html provided, or both provided 3021 WEBVIEW_LOAD_FAILED Page load failed (see onError for details)

docs.title: Capsule Framework — capsule.lock Specification
docs.text: The lock file pins every resolved native dependency so builds are reproducible across machines and CI. Always commit it. Never hand-edit it.

docs.title: Why a Lock File
docs.text:
capsule.config.ts expresses intent (e.g. shellVersion: '^1.4.0'). capsule.lock records the exact resolved versions that were actually used — specific AAR URLs, hashes, and compatibility metadata. This is the same pattern as package-lock.json / pnpm-lock.yaml / Podfile.lock.

capsule.config.ts    →  "I want @capsule/camera ^2.0.0"
capsule.lock         →  "Resolved to 2.1.3, SHA-256: abc123, from https://..."

CI always runs capsule sync --frozen-lockfile which fails if the lock is stale, making divergence impossible.

docs.title: Format: YAML
docs.text: YAML was chosen over JSON because: - Diffs are human-readable (important: lock changes are code-reviewed) - Comments are allowed (the CLI adds context comments) - Less syntactic noise than JSON for this kind of structured data

docs.title: Full Schema with Example
docs.text:
# capsule.lock
# Generated by @capsule/cli. Do not edit manually.
# Regenerate with: capsule sync
# Verify in CI with: capsule sync --frozen-lockfile

lockfileVersion: 1

# ── Capsule shell (the native binary dependency) ────────────────────────────
shell:
  android:
    version: "1.4.2"                        # exact version, never a range
    mavenCoordinate: "dev.capsule:capsule-android:1.4.2"
    aarUrl: "https://maven.capsule.dev/dev/capsule/capsule-android/1.4.2/capsule-android-1.4.2.aar"
    sha256: "e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855"
    targetSdk: 35
    minSdk: 21         # minimum supported by this shell version
    kotlinVersion: "2.0.21"
    agpVersion: "8.7.0"

  ios:
    version: "1.4.2"                        # kept in sync with android version
    swiftPackageUrl: "https://github.com/capsule-framework/capsule-ios"
    xcframeworkUrl: "https://cdn.capsule.dev/xcframework/1.4.2/CapsuleShell.xcframework.zip"
    sha256: "a665a45920422f9d417e4867efdc4fb8a04a1f3fff1fa07e998e86f7f7a27ae3"
    deploymentTarget: "16.0"
    swiftVersion: "5.9"

# ── Resolved community integrations (third-party SDK wrappers) ───────────────
# Core platform capabilities (camera, GPS, push, NFC, Bluetooth, etc.) are
# built into the shell version above — they are not listed here.
# Only third-party SDK integrations appear in this section.
plugins:

  # Binary integration (npm + native artifacts)
  - name: "@capsule-community/google-maps"
    version: "3.2.1"
    trust: "tier2"                  # derived from scope, not self-declared
    android:
      aarUrl: "https://github.com/capsule-community/google-maps/releases/download/3.2.1/google-maps-3.2.1.aar"
      sha256: "b94f6f125c79e3a5ffaa826f584c10d52ada669e6762051b826b55776d7a2fb9"
    ios:
      xcframeworkUrl: "https://github.com/capsule-community/google-maps/releases/download/3.2.1/CapsuleGoogleMaps.xcframework.zip"
      sha256: "c3ab8ff13720e8ad9047dd39466b3c8974e592c2fa383d4a3960714caef0c4f2"
    requiresShell: ">=1.4.0"        # npm semver range — must be satisfied by shell.android.version

  - name: "@capsule-community/stripe"
    version: "2.0.3"
    trust: "tier2"
    android:
      aarUrl: "https://github.com/capsule-community/stripe/releases/download/2.0.3/stripe-2.0.3.aar"
      sha256: "7f83b1657ff1fc53b92dc18148a1d65dfc2d4b1fa3d677284addd200126d9069"
    ios:
      xcframeworkUrl: "https://github.com/capsule-community/stripe/releases/download/2.0.3/CapsuleStripe.xcframework.zip"
      sha256: "9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b2b0b822cd15d6c15b0f00a08"
    requiresShell: ">=1.3.0"

  # Local source integration (compiled from source at build time)
  - name: "my-integration"
    path: "./capsule-plugins/my-integration"
    trust: "local"
    sourceHash: "sha256:2c624232cdd221771294dfbb310acbc6a60d7e43e59dedc2985ad15c9e6b93e0"   # SHA-256 of plugin source tree — detects drift
    android:
      minSdk: 26        # declared in capsule-plugin.json, validated against app minSdk
    ios: {}

# ── Gradle / build tool pins ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
build:
  gradleDistributionUrl: "https://services.gradle.org/distributions/gradle-8.10-bin.zip"
  gradleSha256: "6d5b4a738b7e38916b4e0c7c33de5d5fd12c31fcbb97b50b8e62b53c70e3e3f6"
  nodeVersion: "22"           # informational — checked by CLI on startup
  pnpmVersion: "9"            # informational

docs.title: shell section
docs.text:
Field Description version Exact semver of the Capsule native shell. Always a fixed version, never a range. mavenCoordinate groupId:artifactId:version — used in generated build.gradle aarUrl / xcframeworkUrl Canonical download URL sha256 SHA-256 of the artifact — verified by capsule sync before use targetSdk Android targetSdk baked into this shell version minSdk Lowest Android version this shell supports deploymentTarget Minimum iOS version this shell supports

The shell version determines which Android SDK and iOS deployment target the app targets. Updating the shell (via capsule update) may raise these values — the CLI reports the change and updates capsule.config.ts accordingly.

docs.title: plugins section
docs.text: Field Description trust tier1 / tier2 / local / unverified — set by CLI from npm scope, never by plugin itself requiresShell npm semver range — CLI errors if resolved shell version doesn't satisfy this sha256 Artifact integrity hash — verified before extraction sourceHash For local plugins: hash of the source tree — capsule sync warns if it changed since last lock android.minSdk Plugin's minimum Android version requirement — see conflict resolution below

docs.title: build section
docs.text: Pins the Gradle distribution URL and hash so every machine downloads the exact same wrapper. Also records the expected Node.js and pnpm versions for informational checks.

docs.title: Plugin minSdk Conflict Resolution
docs.text:
When a source plugin declares a higher minSdk than the app:

# App capsule.config.ts has:  android.minSdk: 26
# Plugin capsule-plugin.json has: android.minSdk: 30

CLI behavior:

⚠ Warning: Plugin "my-scanner" requires minSdk 30, but the app targets minSdk 26.
  Devices running Android 8.0–9.x (API 26–29) will not load this plugin.
  The plugin will be silently ignored on those devices.
  To suppress this warning: set android.minSdk: 30 in capsule.config.ts
  To understand impact: capsule codesync devices --platform android

The plugin is not removed — it is conditionally loaded at runtime only on devices that meet its minSdk. On older devices, the plugin's bridge methods return a 3001 PLUGIN_UNAVAILABLE error. The web bridge should handle this gracefully.

Scenarios where a plugin genuinely cannot support older Android versions: - Uses CameraX APIs added in API 28+ - Uses biometric authentication (BiometricPrompt, API 28+) - Uses Foreground Service types declared in API 29+ - Uses exact alarm scheduling (API 31+) - Uses Bluetooth LE with new permission model (API 31+)

In these cases the warning is accurate — the plugin truly does not work on older devices and the developer should either raise the app's minSdk or accept the limitation.

docs.title: Lifecycle: When the Lock File Changes
docs.text: Action Lock file change capsule init Created from capsule.config.ts with latest compatible versions capsule add android\|ios Shell entry added for the new platform capsule update Shell version bumped to latest compatible; sha256 updated. Core SDK capabilities update with the shell. npm install @capsule-community/maps + capsule sync Community integration entry added with resolved version + hashes npm update @capsule-community/maps + capsule sync Integration entry version + hashes updated capsule eject @capsule-community/maps Binary integration entry replaced with local source entry Editing capsule-plugin.json in a source integration sourceHash updated on next capsule sync capsule sync --frozen-lockfile No change — fails if lock would need to change

docs.title: Shell Version Registry
docs.text:
capsule sync and capsule update resolve version ranges by querying the GitHub Releases API for the capsule-framework/capsule repository. This requires zero Capsule-specific infrastructure — GitHub Releases is the canonical source of truth for shell versions.

Resolution process: 

GET https://api.github.com/repos/capsule-framework/capsule/releases
→ returns list of releases tagged v1.4.2, v1.4.1, v1.3.0, ...

Each release attaches a release.json asset containing full metadata for that version: 

{
  "version": "1.4.2",
  "android": {
    "aarUrl": "https://github.com/capsule-framework/capsule/releases/download/v1.4.2/capsule-android-1.4.2.aar",
    "sha256": "e3b0c44298fc1c...",
    "targetSdk": 35,
    "minSdk": 21,
    "kotlinVersion": "2.0.21",
    "agpVersion": "8.7.0"
  },
  "ios": {
    "xcframeworkUrl": "https://github.com/capsule-framework/capsule/releases/download/v1.4.2/CapsuleShell.xcframework.zip",
    "sha256": "a665a45920422f...",
    "deploymentTarget": "16.0",
    "swiftVersion": "5.9"
  }
}

Rate limiting: The CLI caches the release list locally (TTL 1 hour, stored in ~/.capsule/cache/releases.json). Authenticated requests (GITHUB_TOKEN env var) raise the limit from 60 to 5000 req/hour — relevant only for CI pipelines making many requests. For most teams, the unauthenticated limit is never reached.

Offline mode: If the GitHub API is unreachable and a cached list exists, the CLI uses the cache with a warning. If no cache exists, capsule sync fails with a clear network error — not a silent fallback to a wrong version.

Future path (Phase 8+): registry.capsule.dev will be added as a thin proxy in front of GitHub Releases (the base GitHub-Releases shell registry lands in Phase 8 — Ecosystem), enabling: deprecation notices, version yanking without deleting releases, first-party CDN routing, and analytics. The lock file format and resolution semantics are unchanged — only the query endpoint changes. The CLI will support both via a registryUrl setting.

docs.title: Auto-Creating the Lock File
docs.text:
When capsule sync is run and no capsule.lock exists (e.g. after cloning a repo that predates locking, or on capsule init):

1. Read capsule.config.ts
2. Resolve all version ranges to the latest compatible versions
   → shell: resolve '^1.0.0' to the latest 1.x release
   → plugins: resolve '^2.0.0' to the latest 2.x release
3. Fetch SHA-256 hashes for each resolved artifact
4. Write capsule.lock
5. Print: "capsule.lock created — commit this file"

For existing projects migrating to lock-file-based workflow: 

capsule sync          # creates capsule.lock from current capsule.config.ts
git add capsule.lock
git commit -m "chore: add capsule.lock"

docs.title: CI Usage
docs.text:
# .github/workflows/build.yml
- name: Sync capsule wrappers
  run: capsule sync --frozen-lockfile
  # Fails with exit code 1 if capsule.lock is out of date.
  # This catches: "developer updated capsule.config.ts but forgot to run capsule sync"

- name: Build Android
  run: capsule build android --release

--frozen-lockfile never writes to disk. It only validates that the current capsule.lock matches what capsule sync would produce from capsule.config.ts. If there is a mismatch, it prints a diff and exits non-zero.

docs.title: .gitignore Rules
docs.text:
# Generated by capsule — do not commit
.capsule/

# DO commit — this is the lock file
# capsule.lock   ← no entry here, it must be committed

The CLI's capsule init writes this .gitignore block automatically.

docs.title: Version Format: npm Semver
docs.text:
All version constraints in capsule.config.ts use npm semver syntax — the same format as package.json dependencies. This is intentional: same tooling, same mental model, no new syntax to learn.

// capsule.config.ts — version constraints (before resolution)
shellVersion: '^1.4.0'   // any 1.x.x >= 1.4.0
shellVersion: '~1.4.0'   // any 1.4.x >= 1.4.0
shellVersion: '1.4.2'    // exact pin

// capsule.lock — always exact after resolution
shell.android.version: "1.4.2"   // never a range

min_native_version in CodeSync bundles (see ../contributing/codesync-internals.md) also uses npm semver: 

capsule codesync publish --min-native-version ">=1.4.0"
# Devices running shell < 1.4.0 will not receive this bundle

The native client evaluates the constraint using a bundled semver library (same logic as npm's semver package).
