docs.title: CLI reference
docs.text:
Generated from the commander definitions in packages/cli/src/commands/ by pnpm gen — do not edit.

Capsule CLI — app ships inside a managed native capsule Version: run capsule --version.

docs.title: capsule init
docs.text:
Scaffold a new Capsule project from a template

capsule init [options] [name]
Argument Required Description Default [name] no project directory name — Option Description Default --template <template> official name (react-ts, vue-ts, …), a GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket URL (or gh:owner/repo[/subdir][#ref]), a tarball URL, or a local path — --app-id <appId> reverse-domain app ID — --css <css> optional CSS layer: none (default) | tailwind — --test <test> optional test harness: none (default) | vitest —

docs.title: capsule add
docs.text:
Add a platform to this Capsule project

capsule add [options] <platform>
Argument Required Description Default <platform> yes android | ios (ios is recorded in capsule.lock, but sync only generates android so far) —

docs.title: capsule add-ui
docs.text:
Copy Capsule UI components (Tailwind class builders) into this project

capsule add-ui [options] <components...>
Argument Required Description Default <components...> yes component names, e.g. button card — Option Description Default --dir <dir> target directory, relative to the project src/ui --force overwrite files that already exist false

docs.title: capsule sync
docs.text:
Regenerate .capsule/ wrappers from capsule.config.ts and capsule.lock

capsule sync [options]
Option Description Default --frozen-lockfile fail if capsule.lock is out of date —

docs.title: capsule codesync
docs.text:
CodeSync OTA update commands

capsule codesync [options] [command]

docs.title: capsule codesync publish
docs.text:
Publish a new bundle

capsule codesync publish [options]
Option Description Default --channel <channel> OTA channel (e.g., production, staging) production --notes <notes> Release notes (optional) —

docs.title: capsule dev
docs.text:
Start dev server with hot reload on device/emulator

capsule dev [options]
Option Description Default --port <port> dev server port 5173 --tunnel expose via Cloudflare tunnel (prints QR) — --qr print QR code for LAN access — --verbose print commands and timing —

docs.title: capsule build
docs.text:
Build a native app bundle

capsule build [options] <platform>
Argument Required Description Default <platform> yes android (the only platform supported so far) — Option Description Default --release minified release build, signed with the local debug keystore (~/.android/debug.keystore) — not accepted by app stores yet — --format <format> apk | aab apk --verbose print commands and timing —

docs.title: capsule run
docs.text:
Install the built APK on a device or emulator (does not launch it)

capsule run [options] <platform>
Argument Required Description Default <platform> yes android (the only platform supported so far) — Option Description Default --device <id> target device ID (from: adb devices) — --release install the release APK instead of debug —

docs.title: capsule test
docs.text:
Run the app test suite (Vitest)

capsule test [options] [args...]
Argument Required Description Default [args...] no arguments passed through to vitest (file filters, flags) — Option Description Default --watch run vitest in watch mode —

docs.title: capsule doctor
docs.text:
Diagnose the development environment and check store requirements

capsule doctor [options]
Option Description Default --strict exit non-zero when the app violates a store requirement —

docs.title: capsule.config.ts reference
docs.text:
Generated from CONFIG_FIELDS in packages/cli/src/config.ts by pnpm gen — do not edit.

The project config is a TypeScript module default-exporting a CapsuleConfig (wrap it in defineConfig() for type checking). Required means required within its parent: a required key of an optional section is only required when that section is present. [] marks the elements of an array.

docs.title: Top-level keys
docs.text: Key Type Required Default Description appId string yes — Reverse-DNS application id, e.g. com.acme.app — the Android applicationId; also seeds the embedded server port. appName string yes — Display name shown under the app icon. devPort number no 5173 Port of the web dev server that capsule dev and the debug app load.

docs.title: version
docs.text:
App version.

Key Type Required Default Description version object yes — App version. version.name string yes — User-visible version, e.g. 1.2.0 (Android versionName). version.buildNumber number yes — Monotonic build number (Android versionCode); also orders OTA bundles.

docs.title: android
docs.text:
Android build settings — required to build for Android.

Key Type Required Default Description android object no — Android build settings — required to build for Android. android.minSdk number yes — Lowest Android API level the app installs on. android.targetSdk number yes — API level the app targets (Google Play sets a floor). android.compileSdk number yes — API level the app compiles against. android.permissions string[] no — Extra Android permissions, by short name (CAMERA) — merged with the ones Capsule adds for the APIs you use. android.signing object no — Release signing. Prefer environment variables over literal passwords. android.signing.storeFile string no — Path to the keystore. android.signing.storePassword string no — Keystore password. android.signing.keyAlias string no — Alias of the signing key. android.signing.keyPassword string no — Password of the signing key. android.gradleOverrides Record<string, unknown> no — Raw overrides merged into the generated Gradle build. android.push object no — Push notification (FCM) settings. android.push.googleServicesFile string no — Path to the Firebase google-services.json.

docs.title: ios
docs.text:
iOS build settings (iOS shell in bring-up).

Key Type Required Default Description ios object no — iOS build settings (iOS shell in bring-up). ios.deployment string no — Minimum iOS version. ios.bundleId string no — iOS bundle identifier, when it differs from appId.

docs.title: deepLinks
docs.text:
Deep links / universal links that route into the app.

Key Type Required Default Description deepLinks object no — Deep links / universal links that route into the app. deepLinks.schemes string[] no — Custom URL schemes — ['myapp'] registers myapp://…. deepLinks.universalLinks object[] no — HTTPS App Links / Universal Links the app claims. deepLinks.universalLinks[].host string yes — Host to match, e.g. app.acme.com. deepLinks.universalLinks[].pathPrefix string no — Path prefix that scopes the match, e.g. /invite.

docs.title: plugins
docs.text:
Native plugins — a package name, or an object with a path (package name or local folder).

Key Type Required Default Description plugins Array no — Native plugins — a package name, or an object with a path (package name or local folder). plugins[].path string yes — Package name or local folder of the plugin. plugins[].trust string no — 'unverified' acknowledges a plugin outside the @capsule-community/* scope (closed-source or commercial). plugins[].overrides string no — Built-in API this plugin replaces at runtime, e.g. camera.

docs.title: codeSync
docs.text:
OTA updates (CodeSync). Absent or enabled: false → no OTA client in the app.

Key Type Required Default Description codeSync object no — OTA updates (CodeSync). Absent or enabled: false → no OTA client in the app. codeSync.enabled boolean yes — Turns OTA updates on. codeSync.url string no — CodeSync server URL (self-hosted or hosted). codeSync.apiKey string no — API key for the CodeSync server. codeSync.channel string no — Release channel the app follows, e.g. production, staging. codeSync.strategy 'background' | 'immediate' | 'on-next-launch' no — When a downloaded update is applied. codeSync.checkOnForeground boolean no — Also check for updates whenever the app returns to the foreground. codeSync.mandatory boolean no — Treat updates as mandatory by default (a bundle can override it).

docs.title: web
docs.text:
Web bundle build settings.

Key Type Required Default Description web object no — Web bundle build settings. web.mobileReset boolean no true Inject the ~150-byte mobile CSS reset into the built index.html. web.buildCommand string no vite build Command that builds the web bundle into dist/, e.g. ng build --output-path=dist. web.devCommand string no the Vite dev server Command that serves the web app in development, e.g. ng serve --port 5177.

docs.title: jobs
docs.text:
Background jobs (planned).

Key Type Required Default Description jobs object[] no — Background jobs (planned). jobs[].id string yes — Job id. jobs[].interval string yes — How often the job runs. jobs[].constraints object no — Conditions the job waits for. jobs[].constraints.network 'required' | 'unmetered' | 'none' no — Network condition. jobs[].constraints.battery 'notLow' | 'charging' | 'none' no — Battery condition. jobs[].sync object no — Sync a remote collection into local storage. jobs[].sync.url string yes — Source URL. jobs[].sync.collection string yes — Local collection to fill. jobs[].sync.strategy 'merge' | 'replace' yes — How fetched records combine with existing ones. jobs[].notify object no — Schedule local notifications from local data. jobs[].notify.from string yes — Collection to read. jobs[].notify.where Record<string, unknown> no — Filter on the records. jobs[].notify.limit number no — Maximum records to schedule for. jobs[].notify.notifications object[] yes — Notifications to schedule per record. jobs[].notify.notifications[].trigger object yes — When the notification fires. jobs[].notify.notifications[].trigger.minutesBefore number yes — Minutes before the record time. jobs[].notify.notifications[].title string yes — Notification title (template). jobs[].notify.notifications[].body string yes — Notification body (template). jobs[].notify.notifications[].idTemplate string yes — Template for a stable notification id, so reschedules replace instead of duplicate.

docs.title: @capsule/core
docs.text:
@capsule/core — the JavaScript API an app uses to reach the native shell.

Each native API is a ready-made singleton (camera, db, push, …). Inside the Capsule shell calls go over the native bridge; in a plain browser a web fallback answers instead, so an app can be developed without a device. Server routes for the on-device /api bundle live in the @capsule/core/routes entry point.

docs.title: AlertStyle
docs.text:
Per-dialog visual style.

IMPORTANT — this is NOT a CSS layer. Every property maps to a specific, tested native API call. Properties not listed here are not supported on any platform; they are intentionally absent (not forgotten). Unsupported things include: per-button colors, custom fonts, layout/padding, entry/exit animations, and dialog width.

Colors: hex string — #RGB, #RRGGBB, or #AARRGGBB (alpha-first). Sizes: sp on Android (scale-independent pixels), pt on iOS. Lengths: dp on Android, pt on iOS.

Each property documents its exact platform behaviour below. Properties marked "iOS: not supported" are silently ignored on iOS — they do not throw, but they have no visual effect.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: Property Type Description accentColor? string Button text color — applied to all button slots. Per-button colors are not supported by either platform's native dialog API. Android: getButton(slot).setTextColor() — fully supported. iOS: UIAlertController.view.tintColor — fully supported. backgroundColor? string Dialog panel background color. Android: GradientDrawable on dialog.window — fully supported. iOS: NOT SUPPORTED — UIAlertController background is system-controlled and cannot be changed via public API. Setting this has no effect on iOS. buttonAllCaps? boolean Whether button labels are rendered in uppercase. Android: Button.isAllCaps — fully supported. Platform default is true. iOS: NOT SUPPORTED — iOS buttons are always mixed-case. This property is silently ignored on iOS. cornerRadius? number Dialog panel corner radius in dp (Android) / pt (iOS). Android: GradientDrawable.cornerRadius on dialog.window — fully supported. iOS: NOT SUPPORTED — UIAlertController corner radius is system-controlled and overridden by internal masking. Setting this has no effect on iOS. dimAmount? number Backdrop scrim opacity behind the dialog. Range: 0.0 (fully transparent) → 1.0 (fully opaque black). Values outside this range are clamped. Platform default is ~0.5. Android: Window.setDimAmount() — fully supported. iOS: NOT SUPPORTED — UIAlertController scrim is system-controlled. Setting this has no effect on iOS. messageColor? string Message body text color. Android: TextView(android.R.id.message).setTextColor() — fully supported. iOS: NSAttributedString on alertController.setValue — fully supported. messageSize? number Message body text size in sp (Android) / pt (iOS). Android: TextView.setTextSize(COMPLEX_UNIT_SP, value) — fully supported. iOS: NSAttributedString font attribute — fully supported. titleColor? string Title text color. Android: TextView(android.R.id.title).setTextColor() — fully supported. iOS: NSAttributedString on alertController.setValue — fully supported. titleSize? number Title text size in sp (Android) / pt (iOS). Android: TextView.setTextSize(COMPLEX_UNIT_SP, value) — fully supported. iOS: NSAttributedString font attribute — fully supported.

docs.title: AppModule
docs.text:
App lifecycle + deep links. Infrastructure, not just an API: push tap-routing and OTA foreground re-checks both build on the events emitted here.

  • onStateChange / onResume / onPause — foreground & background transitions. On Android these come from ProcessLifecycleOwner, so internal activity transitions (e.g. opening the camera picker) do not spuriously fire background/foreground.
  • onUrlOpen — a deep link arriving while the app is already running.
  • getLaunchUrl — the deep link the app was cold-started with (consumed once; resolves null afterwards or on a normal launch).

docs.title: getLaunchUrl()
docs.text:
getLaunchUrl(): Promise<{
  url: string | null;
}>;

The URL the app was cold-started with via a deep link, or null for a normal launch. Consume-once: a second call resolves null.

Cold-start links surface here and not through onUrlOpen (which fires only for links arriving while the app is already running) — so route on both at startup to cover every entry path:

const { url } = await app.getLaunchUrl()
if (url) route(url)            // launched by a deep link
app.onUrlOpen(({ url }) => route(url))  // links while running

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: Promise\<{ url: string | null; }>

docs.title: AppState
docs.text:
Foreground/background state of the app.

Deliberately a binary contract: Android (resumed/paused/stopped) and iOS (active/inactive/background) disagree on the middle states, but both agree on "is the app in the foreground and interactive?". Modelling that single bit keeps the cross-platform seam honest — the same listener fires identically on both platforms. A richer state enum can be layered on later without breaking this shape.

docs.text: Property Type Description isActive boolean true while the app is foregrounded and receiving input.

docs.title: Bridge
docs.text:
Contract that all modules depend on. Allows injection of FakeBridge in tests.

Messages are JSON-RPC 2.0 over the WebView: requests carry an id and get exactly one response; notifications carry no id and fan out to every on() subscriber.

docs.title: schema()
docs.text:
schema(version, migrate): void;

Registers migration version (an integer ≥ 1) for tables you manage with db.sql. Pending migrations run in version order, each in its own transaction, before the next database operation; the applied version is kept in SQLite's PRAGMA user_version. Add a new version for each change — never edit one that has shipped.

If the database is already at a version newer than any registered (e.g. after an OTA rollback to an older bundle), every operation fails with SCHEMA_VERSION_REGRESSION.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type version number migrate Migration

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: void

docs.title: transaction()
docs.text:
transaction<T>(fn): Promise<T>;

Runs fn in a transaction: committed when it resolves, rolled back when it throws (the error is rethrown). Resolves to fn's result.

The database runs one thing at a time: while a transaction is open, other db.sql and db.transaction calls wait for it. So inside fn use tx.sql — awaiting db.sql or a nested db.transaction there would wait for the transaction it is part of, forever.

docs.title: PushModule
docs.text:
Remote push notifications (FCM / APNs).

Tap routing mirrors app deep links (the same cold/warm split #3 proved on device): a tap on a notification that cold-launches the app surfaces through the consume-once getLaunchNotification; a tap while the app is already running/backgrounded fires onNotificationTap. Route on both at startup to cover every entry path, just like app.getLaunchUrl + app.onUrlOpen:

const { message } = await push.getLaunchNotification()
if (message) route(message)               // launched by a notification tap
push.onNotificationTap((msg) => route(msg)) // taps while running
push.onMessage((msg) => toast(msg))         // foreground arrivals

Channel methods are Android-only (API 26+) and silently no-op on iOS.

type AiStatus = "ready" | "downloadable" | "downloading" | "unavailable";

  • downloadable — supported, but the model must be downloaded first: call AiModule.prepare.

docs.title: AiTier
docs.text:
type AiTier = "os-native" | "bundled" | "cloud" | "unavailable";

Which kind of backend serves AI requests (adr-003):

  • os-native — the OS model: Gemini Nano via AICore (Android), Apple Foundation Models (iOS). Flagships only (Pixel 8+, Galaxy S24+, iPhone 15 Pro+ …) — most devices don't have it.
  • bundled — a small model shipped with the app (Phase 6, not yet available).
  • cloud — Capsule OTA cloud inference (Phase 6, not yet available).
  • unavailable — no tier can serve on this device / shell build.

docs.title: FilesystemDirectory
docs.text:
type FilesystemDirectory = "data" | "cache" | "documents";

Logical storage location. Apps address files by (directory, relative path) rather than absolute paths, so the same code resolves correctly on Android, iOS, and the browser fallback.

All three map to app-private storage that is deliberately kept outside the OTA-swappable bundle dirs (www/ + server/bundle.js) — a code-push bundle swap never touches user data written here.

  • data — persistent app data. Survives until explicitly deleted.
  • cache — same API, but the OS may reclaim it under storage pressure.
  • documents — persistent, user-facing documents (export targets).

docs.title: @capsule/core/routes
docs.text:
@capsule/core/routes — register the handlers of an app's on-device /api server.

The CLI bundles the app's route files with this module; on the device QuickJS runs the bundle and the embedded server forwards each /api/ request (and each bridge RPC routed to JS) to the handler registered here.

docs.title: dispatch()
docs.text:
function dispatch(requestJson): object | null;

Dispatch entry point called by QuickJSBridge for every incoming JSON-RPC request.

Returns a plain JS object (NOT a JSON string). The C call helper wraps every return value in JSON.stringify(), so returning an object produces clean JSON on the Kotlin side. Returning a pre-serialised string would cause double-encoding.

Returns null to signal the Kotlin bridge to fall through to native Android handlers.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type requestJson string

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: object | null

docs.title: handleHttpRequest()
docs.text:
function handleHttpRequest(
   method, 
   path, 
   body, 
   headers
): object | null;

HTTP dispatch entry point called by the native RequestRouter for every /api/* request.

Arguments are passed as a JSON array by QuickJSBridgeImpl.handleHttpRequest(): [method, path, body|null, headers-object]. The C call helper parses the array and passes values as native JS types — no JSON.parse needed.

Returns a plain object with { status, body, mimeType } or null if no handler matches. Returning null makes the embedded server respond with 404.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type method string path string body string | null headers Record\<string, string>

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: object | null
